eps.name: A Letter I Wanted to Write

lines.st: Dear Martina,
I hesitated for a long time over whether I should write to you.
Ever since that rainy night when you reached out your hand and set me on the Messenger's path, I've been so grateful, and I've wanted to thank you in person.
But through one mix-up after another we could never manage to meet, and that has always made me sad.

To be honest, even the address on this letter is one I pieced together by asking around on my travels. I'm not sure I've spelled it right—I only confirmed it was a real place after looking it up on a map.
But there really is something I want to say to you.
I'm working for Rhodes Island now. You may have heard the name; they're a very, very good pharmaceutical company, and it's my home now, the most important place in the world to me.
It's just that there's one question I used to think was simple, and that I understand less and less...
To Rhodes Island, to this land, to Angelina the Messenger...
Where exactly do I belong?

lines.x: Hoo... hoo... This wheel's really dug itself in deep...
Maybe I should get down and help after all?
No need, no need. Somebody's got to work the wheel, and your Arts make the off-roader lighter, too, missy.
Don't underestimate a miner with five years down the shaft! Heave—!
It moved—the car moved!
Hey hey hey, don't stop your Arts now, missy, she'll roll back down! Quick, start her up, fire the engine!
R-right!
Haha! This takes me right back to last month, when the mine caught fire and the escape tunnel got blocked by a mine cart.
If I hadn't given it everything back then, I couldn't be helping you now, and I'd never have made it home to see my newborn.
Um... my problem is so much smaller than yours...
Now, don't talk like that.
You're headed to Great Springs, aren't you, miss? Then you're our guest! Your trouble is my trouble, An... uh... what was your name again?
I'm Angelina. Angelina Ajimu, a Messenger of Rhodes Island.

lines.loc: New Rhodes Island, Field Operations Meeting Room July 1102

lines.x: What? Great Springs never received the decryptor?
That's right. We just heard back from Peta, the data analysis operator at the Rhodes Island office in Great Springs.

It takes at least forty-five days to get from Rhodes Island HQ to Rim Billiton. I remember marking that decryptor package for expedited delivery—wasn't that because the data decryption was time-sensitive?
It was. The decryptor that should have arrived matches the data we collected in Rim Billiton's Far South.

Since last summer, when Terra started feeling the effects of abnormal Originium activity, we built a data collection station in the Far South of Rim Billiton, where atmospheric Originium concentration changes the most.
The concentration data we gather is sent via Rim Billiton's newly developed long-range comms technology to the Rhodes Island office in Great Springs, where it's decrypted and studied.
The finished conclusions are then carried back by Messenger to Rhodes Island, which has no long-range comms. By Closure's calculations, that strikes a rough balance between cost and security.
That package should be the one I handled when I sorted and dispatched the mail three months ago.
I've asked every Messenger who's run to Rim Billiton in the past six months. Nobody ever received it.
Then... the package was lost during sorting and dispatch? It was my mistake, which is why—
Oh, come on. There's so much correspondence between HQ and the rest of Terra, and so much freight, that mix-ups are inevitable—using a contingency plan is exactly what makes preparing one worthwhile!
A contingency plan?
Meaning we have Closure make another decryptor exactly like it. And don't worry about the original—it's just a decryption plug-in, so there's no leak risk even if it went to the wrong place.
If you hadn't happened to overhear me dealing with this, I wouldn't have gone out of my way to tell you...
So... this decryptor has to go to Great Springs too, right?
Well, of course—
Let me take it.
Didn't you just get back from a run to Columbia? And the Field Ops people say you've been holed up in the training room every free moment lately...
This really is a minor thing. You don't have to take it so much to heart.
Maybe I am making too much of it. But delivering the package to its destination by hand, so the same problem doesn't happen twice—that's a Messenger's responsibility too.
Haha, that's one of Rhodes Island's most reliable Messengers for you! I'll contact Closure right now and ask whether she's fine with you making the run.
She says it's no problem at all.
Wonderful.
Let me think—for this trip I'll need a map of Rim Billiton, protective gear against active Originium dust...
Oh, and! I hear Rim Billiton has all-terrain transporters. Which means my own car should probably also—
Leave it to me!
I came to Great Springs to find Peta, the one who handles data analysis at the Rhodes Island office. Do you know her?
Ahh, Angelina Ajimu... So you're Angelina Ajimu!
Has Miss Peta mentioned me?
Is she upset that I didn't deliver on—
What a great name!
H-huh?
That's right! Angelina Ajimu... Cute, distinctive, completely outside the usual naming conventions!
Running into you on Route Zero today is the greatest luck of my life. You have got to name our newborn little Timothy!
I thought... your little Timothy... was named little Timothy?
That's just a nickname. Picking the formal name is a big deal in our town!
Take me, for instance. My name's Barnett, and back in school there were four other Barnetts in my class besides me.
And that's not all—two Barnettinas, three Barnettios, three Barneysons, one Barney II, one Barney III... and eleven Barneys!
Wh-why?
Town's only so big, life doesn't change much, and folks have plenty of kids. A name that sounds good, is easy to remember, and means something nice? Course it's in demand.
Hang on, I'll let the family know right now—a naming genius is coming to Great Springs!
(Opens his terminal)
(Stares at his terminal)
(Closes his terminal)
Mr. Barnett, you send messages... awfully fast?
Nah, I got excited and forgot. Since the Great Disconnect, all we've got left is the old intercity network...
The Great Disconnect?
Doesn't matter, though! We're almost at Great Springs anyway. Angelina, I'm awful sorry, but could I trouble you for a lift the rest of the way?
Of course! I still haven't thanked you for pushing my car out. But what you said just now about the Great Disconnect—
It's nothing big. Anyway, this is a fine car you've got. Smaller than a transporter, but it still runs on this disaster-beaten road... it's an all-terrain conversion, right?
It is. Before I set out this time, a friend of mine in Rhodes Island's Engineering Department went to the trouble of modifying the off-roader I usually drive!
Angelina, I know this might be asking too much. But I've been driving for years, and I know the road to Great Springs by heart, so... uh... could you maybe...

Let me guess—
You want me to lend you the off-roader for a stretch?
Heh heh... Rim Billiton transporters are safe enough, but you can't open up the roof like on your car. Feeling the wind all around you as you drive... now that's romance!
Pff, you don't have to explain any further. That's fine with me.
Excellent!
Careful now, we'll get a little bump. There's a small crater up ahead—an Originium storm punched it out four, five years back.
R-right.
Not done yet. The next hundred meters or so of this stretch are washed out, so we've got to detour through the wastes. Nothing but gravel under the tires, so it might get a little wo-o-o-o—
A little wo-o-o-o—bu-bu-bu—umpy!
G-g-got it—!
Whew, made it through. The road up ahead is maintained by us Great Springs folk, so it's in much better shape.
I wondered about this last time I was in Rim Billiton—Rim Billiton gets hit by Catastrophes far more often than other regions, so how did Route Zero ever get built?
Well, it's less that we built Route Zero and more that the Catastrophes left us only one possible way to build a road at all.
Back in the day there were only one or two paths between tribes that the Originium hadn't completely smashed. Those were the ancestors of Route Zero.

It wasn't until after the First Great Migration, when settlers from outside brought in manpower and technology, that those dirt tracks got repaired and linked up. That's when the name "Route Zero" came about.
Even with people maintaining it on their own, though, the road's condition still suffered from the Catastrophes.
Later on, Originium industry developed, small nomadic platforms multiplied, all-terrain transporters came into use—and this beat-up old road wasn't needed anymore.
These days it just points the way.
Points the way?
That's right. Great Springs is Route Zero's northernmost starting point, and its far end is in the Far South, where hardly anyone sets foot.
Nobody knows why they ran the road out to such a remote place back then.
The Far South... that's where Rhodes Island built its Originium concentration data collection station...
Building something in the Far South? Hoh, your company must be quite something, then. The last outfit to build things all over Rim Billiton was Meridian Red Earth.
Meridian Red Earth... I think I know them. They operate Rim Billiton's long-range comms technology, don't they?
They do. Last summer they put up comms towers everywhere. There's one in Great Springs too.
At first none of us knew what a tower that tall was good for—truth be told, some of the older folks, and the ones who don't get out much, still don't know what long-range comms are good for.
Not that it matters now, anyway.
Doesn't matter? Is that because of what you mentioned before—
Ah, I remember now! Angelina, didn't you say you were here looking for somebody?
I did! Do you know someone named Peta? She's a data analyst at the Rhodes Island office.
Hmm... Can't say I do.
I see... Thank you anyway.
I can get you some chilled carrot juice, though.
Is offering people carrot juice a Great Springs custom?
No, no, what I mean is, there've got to be fifty Petas in town if there aren't a hundred. You'll wear your throat raw.
Ha...
Though maybe I could ask my little niece for help? She's the finest switchboard operator in Great Springs...
Never mind that for now—we're almost there! Angelina, look out that way!
Backed by towering red crags, a serene, snow-white town appeared before their eyes.
Swaying flowers and berry-laden thickets filled the gaps between the buildings, warmly welcoming every family member and guest who came from afar.
A red waterwheel turned lazily, carrying crystal-clear blue lake water endlessly into the town behind it, and rising steam curled around the two of them.
Is this lake... a hot spring?
Hahahaha, why else would we call it Great Springs?
We've got no minerals here, but springs we've got plenty. Spring, summer, autumn, winter—jump in and you've got yourself a nice hot bath.
Riding on the springs' fame, our town became a well-known health resort, and plenty of holiday centers opened up around it.
If it weren't for having so many kids that what I earn in town can't cover it, so I've got to work the mines to get by, I'd want to stay here my whole life.
Yes... it looks like the most perfect home there could be...
It does have one flaw, though.
Ah! My packages—
The floral scent and the moisture on the wind make it easy to forget, but the wind of Rim Billiton still has the power to carve the wastes.
The off-roader, which had kept to every safe-driving rule the whole way, began to tear along under the hands of a Rim Billitonian.
Wind and speed do not ask whether the letters in the back might like to check that their own "seat belts" are fastened tight.
They fluttered through the air in a panic, and in the sunlight the names on every envelope glittered...
Would they vanish into these wastes before ever speaking their "heart"?
Fortunately, their reliable Messenger happened to be able to bring them all back...
Hold on—!
Hahaha, I had no idea your Arts could fly letters right back into your hands! Does that mean you can fly yourself, too?
Flying's no trouble at all!
But even flying, I'd never be as fast as you drive!
Hahahahaha!
Hello, Great Springs Switchboard. Who would you like to reach?
Tani, put me through to him again. I have to have this out with him today!
(Sighs) Ms. Mela, I really don't see what difference it makes whether you light ten candles or a hundred on your anniversary.
Tani, you're young, you're not my age yet. If you knew the story of me and Rock, you'd understand exactly how I feel!
I do know. You two have known each other since you were little, and he confessed to you for the first time when you were twelve, on Shopping Street.
Then he went off to Iron Carrot City for the family business, you waited five whole years for him, and right after those five years you got married.
And since the wedding you've had a little fight every five days and a big one every ten, and the louder you fight, the sweeter you are once you make up.
(Takes a quick sip of water) Anyway, Ms. Mela, I'd really appreciate it if you could keep it short—
Oh, I just mean these ten years the two of us have spent together really haven't been easy. When do you think would be a good time for me to call him?
After you get off work.
No, no, that's far too late! What if this time one of us can't let it go and we get divorced in a fit of temper?!
...That's not going to happen.
Tani, say what you like, I'm still your aunt's brother's cousin, and Rock is your aunt's brother's cousin's husband!
Ugh, now that I think about it, why were we fighting over how many candles? Rock has a point, too—they never lit that many even for his grandmother's birthday...
But I just kept thinking, even if it's our tenth anniversary, I want us to keep each other company much longer. Twenty years, thirty years, a hundred...
Darling... is that how you feel?
Rock?! Tani, wh-when did you put him through?
(Sighs) Don't ask. This is the fastest way to settle it anyway.
Mela, whatever happens, my dearest, I understand everything you're feeling. We'll do it your way—not ten candles, a hundred!
All right...
Darling, you've had a long day. You hang up first...
No, last time I hung up on you in a huff, so this time you go ahead...
Have either of you been listening to me at all—
No, you hang up first...
It's fine, you first...
Thank you for your call, and have a lovely day!
Ugh, when is this ever going to end...
Tani flopped back down onto the desk. The call was over, but it still felt like two fowlbeasts were chirping away nonstop inside her head.
Come on, Tani, hang in there.
This is your last day as a switchboard operator. The last day!
(Takes a deep breath) Hello, Great Springs Switchboard. Who would you like to reach?
Tani, how've you been lately?
...Fine.
Let your uncle tell you something fun!
The boys at the mine taught me all kinds of exercise routines this time around. I figured with your little cousin just born I ought to spend more time with her, so I hiked home from the mine on foot—
Uncle Barnett, this is the switchboard room.
Ah, would you look at me. I'm getting to the point, though, right away, right away.
Anyway, outside town I ran into a Messenger whose car was stuck. Funny name, it's... uh... huh? You'll do it yourself? Sure, sure, no problem—
It is getting late, so I should head home too. If you get a chance, help me think of a name for our little Tim, please!
Hello? Is anyone there?
Hello, Miss Tani. I'm Angelina.
Miss Angelina, who would you like to reach?
I'm looking for Peta. Peta from the Rhodes Island office.
Tani tilted her head back and thought for a moment, then sighed and pinched her own nose.
There's a whole pile of Petas on the switchboard. Going through them one by one is a real chore.
What does Rhodes Island do?
It's a medical organization. They specialize in the treatment and prevention of Oripathy.
Great Springs is packed with sanatoriums and medical outfits that claim to relieve Oripathy. Any other information? What does this Peta look like? Which district does she live in?
Um... I'm not really sure...
Ugh.
Tani's foot started tapping the floor without her noticing. Squinting, she searched the switchboard line by line for the words "Rhodes Island."
Miss Tani, I heard from Mr. Barnett that there's been something called a "Great Disconnect" recently—
...Found the Rhodes Island Peta. I'll put you through.
Thank you so much, Miss Tani!
Don't mention it.
Phew...
...Ugh, I'm stomping again. Mom just got mad at me for stomping the other day.
It's fine, though. After today I'll be eighteen, and I can say goodbye to the switchboard and the switchboard room—
Huh? Didn't that Angelina ask for the Rhodes Island Peta? The plug is clearly in "Rhodes Island Peta," so why is "Roadblock Bro Peta" the one lighting up?
Weird. Let me listen in...
...That's right, besides the decryptor there's also a batch of medicine—
Then we're good, we're good! We've been waiting ages for that stuff, bring it over quick, quick!
Um... okay?
*distinctive weird shriek* It's finawwy here, here here here, shpishy bo'ltree powbah, my shpishy bo'ltree powbah...
(Shpishy bo'ltree powbah?)
Th-then I'll head over now.
Ooh! See ya~ soon!
—Oh no!

eps.name: Addressee: The End of the Line

lines.x: Hoho, an unfamiliar little Vulpo. First time I've seen you—you the new one bringing the medicine?
Uh, I suppose... so?
Why're you so wishy-washy! Don't underestimate us, hurry up and hand over the shpishy bo'ltree powbah!
Shpishy bo'ltree powbah?
Come on, spicy bottletree powder! This stuff right here! Look how pure the spicy bottletree powder in big sis's hand is—one snort and the top of your skull blasts clean off!
Hey, little Vulpo, you don't know how things work around here. Where you from? Siracusa?
You got anybody in Siracusa as impressive as us? Any tattoos as terrifying as ours? Take a look at this—a great big tuskbeast across my whole back. Scare you to death!
I'm sorry, I... I think I might have come to the wrong place!
Hey—hold on, what's the idea, leaving the second you get here? You haven't given us what we asked for!
Never heard our names? We're Helmet Sis Amber and Roadblock Bro Peta!
Um... I'm sorry, I really do have something urgent, so I have to—
—Just walk off whenever you feel like it? You're looking down on us! Hand over the spicy bottletree powder!
You two...
Hey!!
Huh?
You... you...
The girl came sprinting up and couldn't catch her breath. Once she stalled, she had no idea where to begin, and in her agitation she couldn't help stomping her foot.
It sapped more than half of her momentum in an instant, but she did succeed in drawing the two youths' attention.
Hey, Tani, what are you doing here? This is no place for a good kid like—
Stop!
Spicy bottletree powder isn't a drug at all! Every time you snort it up your nose and screw up your face and tear up, that's not the effect—that's just how spicy it is!
Nonsense!
And what you're holding isn't "super pure spicy bottletree powder" either. It's turnip and chili ground up together—and you had to beg everyone you know just to get a secondhand grinder!
...Ngh! Tani, that's—
Everyone in town knows!
And you! That isn't a back covered in tattoos, those are temporary tattoos you can buy five hundred of wholesale for one caleti!
...Agh!
Tani, you just wait! You'll regret this someday!
Pff, what's with those two?
...A couple of oddballs trying to stand out. The town's probably just too boring, so they started imitating characters from Siracusan movies and ended up like that—neither one thing nor the other.
I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Tani, a switchboard operator in Great Springs!
I'm so sorry for the trouble... But this problem really is strange. The line was connected correctly and the person was wrong. The town switchboard has never had that happen...
Sorry. I'll be sure to check the lines when I get back. Are you—
Are you a Messenger?
I am.
Th-then you must have been to a lot of places? Places outside Rim Billiton?
Hmm... Victoria, Siracusa, Higashi, Yan, Leithanien... quite a few, yes. Though I don't come to Rim Billiton often.
(Quietly) That many places... Whoa!
Could I trouble you to ask around for where the Rhodes Island office is? I have something very important to deliver.
All the Oripathy sanatoriums in town are clustered around Hot Spring Plaza in Great Springs, and a new batch rotates in every so often.
A stranger would take ages to find it. Let me take you—
Um, I mean, let me help you look!
"Spring Cure Gardens," "Natural Heat Therapy Hall," "Wellness Hydrotherapy," "Better-Than-Medicine Springs"...
Um, the Rhodes Island office should be more official than this, and they're supposed to be building a data analysis site too...
But every outside organization that deals with the Infected is right here.
Great Springs doesn't mind doing business with the Infected, but...
...Mm, I understand.
That person over there—doesn't the bag in her hand say "Rhodes Island"?
I can't quite make out the writing on the bag—
No, no, of course she's a Rhodes Island Operator!
Hello, I'm Angelina! Do you happen to know Operator Peta from the Great Springs office? I'm Angelina, a Messenger from Rhodes Island HQ!
I'm Peta. Hello there, hello.
I'm the one who lost the decryptor that should have been sent to you, which left you unable to continue your research. I'm so terribly sorry!
The decryptor... unable to continue my research?
Oh... right, you don't know about the Great Disconnect yet.
Because of the Great Disconnect, long-range comms along Route Zero are all down. The data from the Far South can't be sent through at all, so ten decryptors wouldn't do any good.
So what actually got "disconnected" was long-range comms along Route Zero?
That's right. More precisely, the long-range comms system set up by "Meridian Red Earth."
I think I've heard a similar name before, but it wasn't Red Earth...
Mm. The company's from Trimounts in Columbia, and it's called "Meridian." They give every overseas branch a different name.
In Bolívar it's "Meridian Canopy," in Kjerag it's "Meridian Summit," and "Meridian Red Earth" is Rim Billiton.
Normally, thanks to the line they ran from this town of Great Springs all the way to Rim Billiton's capital, Ultimate Big Ironton, everyone along the route could use long-range comms.
Rhodes Island chose to connect to Meridian Red Earth's line as well, so data could go from the Far South to Big Ironton and then on to us.
For data confidentiality, any data that isn't processed within the time limit is automatically destroyed and waits for the next transmission cycle.
But right after I sent HQ that reply saying the decryptor never arrived, long-range comms along all of Route Zero went down... Around June, I think.
June... So if my package hadn't gone to the wrong place last time, you would have had enough time to decrypt the Far South data...?

In theory, yes—but let's not dwell on unhappy things. You brought me medicine too, and that's a huge help! Let me see—
forty doses of acute Oripathy onset suppressant,
ten Originium dust protection suits,
one box of "Ah~ To My Beloved~" handmade chocolates—
Huh? My beloved?
...On the way here, the letters in the off-roader's cargo area got scattered by the wind, and I was in such a rush repacking them that some of the parcels ended up in the wrong places.
Now that I think about it, I checked before I set out. The parcels should all have been strapped down tight... Why did they all fly out at that exact spot?
Ah, there's something you don't know.
They say that in the land of Rim Billiton there's a creature that "steals" the words people haven't said out loud.
Steals... words? How is that possible?
Miss Peta, do you mean the legend of the pouched musbeast?
Pouched musbeast?
Mm-hm. In Rim Billiton, the pouched musbeast story is a bedtime story every child has heard. The version my grandma told me goes like this...
Back when Rim Billiton had no nomadic platforms, no Route Zero, not even Messengers...
Catastrophes struck the wastes again and again, scattering families who had lived together and forcing them to live in different villages.

There was a brave Rim Billitonian who grieved that people could not pass their feelings to one another, so she became the first Messenger of her own accord, carrying words between relatives, friends, and lovers separated by great distances.
Setting out alongside her was a clever creature shaped like a musbeast that could also fly.
Because it had a pouch on its chest and always liked to hide the things it treasured inside, they called it the pouched musbeast.
Their journey was a happy one, until one day the pouched musbeast refused, no matter what, to deliver another letter for her.
The brave Rim Billitonian discovered that the pouched musbeast had peeked at the letters. The letters had gone blank—the musbeast had taken every feeling and every word inside them for itself.
Before the pouched musbeast could flee, the brave Rim Billitonian struck its head with her walking staff, making it forget how to understand and read words.
Conspicuous fuzz grew where the pouched musbeast had been hurt, so it could never fully hide itself while stealing words again, and in the end it could only go live in the Far South.

The brave Rim Billitonian told this story to everyone she met, reminding them to tell the people who mattered the words and feelings they'd left unsaid as soon as they could, so the pouched musbeast couldn't steal them away.
Hmm... You're quite the storyteller, Tani. I can practically picture what a pouched musbeast looks like—
It's my grandma who told it well—
No, no, but this isn't just a story!
Every Messenger in Rim Billiton knows to hang an herb sachet on their parcels to drive pouched musbeasts off, and there's a "No Pouched Musbeasts" warning sign right outside my switchboard room!
Although the pouched musbeasts on those signs are all drawn any old way. Apart from all having a pouch, they don't have much in common.
Oh? So most Rim Billitonians have never seen one?
Pouched musbeasts run away incredibly fast. Unless it wants you to, hardly anyone can see one—and if you can see it, that means it's already stolen something of yours!
...Don't look at me like that, Angelina. Grandma told me all of this, and Grandma never lied!

All right. For now the data is all sitting in the storage unit of the collector down in the Far South, so we can only wait for the long-range comms tower to be fixed. Why don't you relax a bit—take a soak in the springs?
And when will the long-range comms tower be fixed?
No telling. The line's so long, and nobody knows what went wrong, so Meridian Red Earth's people are probably scratching their heads too.
I could go to the Far South and bring the data back myself!
What?!
Absolutely not! Hardly anyone sets foot in the Far South, because the road there is simply too brutal!
You saw Route Zero, didn't you? Nothing but deep craters and Originium crystals—and following it is the only way to reach the Far South.
When Rhodes Island set up the collection device down there, they were held up again and again. Just getting to the Far South took them several months.
Several months? I thought Grandma said it didn't take her that long?
Between Big Ironton and the Far South there's a stretch where conditions are extremely harsh. There are only a handful of days a year when you can pass through normally.

First, that stretch has heavy sandstorms all year round, with fast-moving sandstorms appearing in the middle of them. An ordinary person who gets caught inside one loses all sense of direction fast and can't get out at all.

Second, even if you're lucky enough to catch a moment when the storms are weaker, the concentration of active Originium particles in the air there is extremely high. Going is no different from going to die!
But the people from Rhodes Island still got through, didn't they?
By rights, reaching the Far South means waiting on the weather—finding a day with no sandstorm and a lower active Originium concentration... and days like that are far too rare.
The reason the Rhodes Island engineering team made it through is—
However the original Rhodes Island engineering team reached the Far South, I'll get there my own way.
I know going to the Far South is extremely difficult. But when you make a mistake, you should make up for it yourself. At the very least... let me try, all right?
...I take it I can't stop you?
Mm-hm♪
I am curious, though. Why are you so set on this?
To keep my mistake from causing everyone any more trouble than it already has. It's what I ought to be doing anyway.
Besides... this is something within my power, after all.
Angelina's voice was firm, and yet there was a trace of melancholy in it—though the other two clearly didn't catch it.
Tani least of all; her eyes were full of admiration as she watched Angelina.
Th-that's all there is to it.
Let me take a look at the map...
Great Springs is here. Mm, first stop is Artichoke Village over this way. I remember a Messenger mentioning the dried carrots they make there are delicious, so I could take some along for the road...
I'll have to think a bit more about the route to Solar Valley...
So, um... Tani, thank you for helping me find the office all this way. But it's almost dinnertime. Aren't you... going home?
I'm not going home yet! Angie, there's something I want to ask you...
Could you take me with you to the Far South?
Hm?!
Hold on, this isn't something you can just decide on the spot...
I-it's like this!
Tani hurriedly dug a candied carrot stick out of the little red bag she carried and held it out to Angelina.
Angelina took it without thinking.
Today is my birthday. Once today's over I'll be eighteen, and Mom and Dad promised that once I came of age I could travel far away on my own—just like my grandma!
Your grandma...?
Mm-hm! Grandma was amazing.
She always wore a pocket watch. She said that if you pointed the hour hand at the sun, you could tell which way was south.
And not only that—the pocket watch was her Arts Unit too. Grandma had a real gift for Originium Arts, and she could always solve a problem with ease.
While she traveled all over Rim Billiton, Grandma did so many incredible things with that watch. She even made it to the Far South at the age of sixty!
It's just a shame she lost the watch on that trip. Afterward she came back to Great Springs and never set out again...
Wow, she went to the Far South by herself?
She did. Grandma was an explorer—or, in our words, a veteran pathfinder.
A pathfinder?
Tani rummaged through her bag, fished out a piece of haw candy, and held that out to Angelina as well.
Angelina hesitated, then took it anyway.
Here in Rim Billiton, settlements often grow too crowded and have to find a new place to settle. That's when pathfinders set out, walking into the wastes to look for a new place fit to live.
Back then Grandma set out from the settlement where she'd been living, followed Route Zero north the whole way, and found this place.
When I was little, Grandma was always telling me about the things she saw along the way.
A sun inside a valley, pouched musbeasts that fly all over and almost nobody has seen, nomadic vessels taller than mountains, mines deeper than rifts...
I've always wanted to go see the things Grandma talked about.
So I've been getting ready for this journey all along. Every day I'd put a little something I'd need on the road into this bag, and move it into my big backpack when I got home at night.
My big backpack is completely ready now—I can leave anytime. Once I've had my birthday with my family, I'll go to the Far South with you tomorrow!
The sun slowly went down.
Seeing that Angelina had finished the haw candy, Tani started rummaging through her bag again, then happily held out a sweet cherry cake.
This time Angelina managed to suppress the urge to take it—though against Tani's enthusiastic offensive, such token resistance was clearly useless.
Thank you for the snacks. Tani, I think I should...
Heheh, you should find a place to stay and get something proper to eat, right? Snacks won't fill you up!
I've never been outside Great Springs, and I want to hear your stories about the outside. Why don't you come have birthday dinner at my house?
Well...
Um...
Heheh~

eps.name: Addressee: The End of the Line

lines.x: Hop, Skip, Jump! Stop milling around the kitchen getting in my way—go hide your little sister's birthday presents properly!
Far, Farther, Farthest—could I trouble you to borrow five more sets of dishes? I only just remembered my cousin's family is coming too.
Hunter, it's your daughter's eighteenth birthday and you're still watching cricket—wait, that's not right. Didn't our town's long-range comms break two months ago?
Madison, dear, don't fret. The match will be over in another twenty minutes.
The long-range comms are down, sure, but today it's our home team—the Great Springs Ironfeet. If it weren't Tani's birthday I'd have gone out to the edge of town to watch in person.
And you've got the nerve to say that...
Besides, Tani supports the Ironfeet too. If they make the finals today, I'll give her the good news as a present. And if they lose...
If they lose, you'd better think first about how to keep Tani from stomping. Have you forgotten where the name "Thumpy" came from?
Aw, it's the nickname my mother gave her. The kid loved stomping so much that "Thumpy" is just thump-thump-thump—
Don't you start stomping too!
Haha—
Tani's back! Quick, hide!
Uh... shouldn't somebody open the door for Tani?
Never mind, forget hiding. The second the door opens we pull the poppers! Three, two, one—!
I'm ho—
Happy birthday!
Come on, I'm this big now, you don't have to do the birthday-surprise thing anymore!
And I saw Dad sneaking off with my key this morning, you know!
Heheh, my daughter's so sharp!
Oh? Is this your new friend? What a cute girl. You're here for our Thumpy's—no, no, Tani's birthday party, right?
Look at you. She's this grown and you're still using the nickname. You'll confuse our guest.
Aw, now she knows! What's your name, dear?
Hello, sir, ma'am—uh, big brother... big sister? Hello, I'm Angelina...
Mom and Dad look young, but they're actually almost forty.
They say Grandma looked young at forty too, so maybe it runs in the family. I don't look eighteen either...
Oh, people only grow through experience. Don't you worry.
Angelina, I'll get the guest room ready in a bit. Stay with us tonight.
Thank you! But I do have a place to stay in Great Springs—
It's fine, we've got room.
Then I won't stand on ceremony. Thank you, sir, ma'am!
Don't mention it! So which cricket team do you support? No, wait, by the look of you, you're from out of town? What ball sports do folks play where you're from?
All right, stop crowding Angelina. Where are my birthday presents? Today's a big day! Once today's over, I can set off tomorrow!
No wonder this birthday party is such a grand affair... That's wonderful, Tani. So many people here to wish you off—I'm really happy for you.
Right? I have waited so, so long for this eighteenth birthday!
I haven't told you yet, have I? I actually started asking Mom and Dad if I could leave Great Springs and go exploring when I was fourteen.
Fourteen... That does seem a little early, no matter how you look at it?
That's what Mom and Dad said too. The Rim Billiton wastes are too dangerous, so I had to wait until at least sixteen.
But... right before my sixteenth birthday, I caught Oripathy. Luckily the infection is very mild and the acute onset periods are short.
Once my condition was stable, I asked again whether I could go. Mom and Dad said that once you leave Great Springs, it's hard to find anywhere the Infected can live as freely.
But I still wanted to go, to become a great pathfinder like Grandma. Mom and Dad agreed—they said that when I turned eighteen they'd definitely let me set out...
That's why I've got such a grand birthday party today! Mom, Dad, and all the relatives who came to see me off—thank you!
The air in the room seemed to freeze for a few seconds, but it quickly turned as merry as it had been the moment Tani came home.
Let me open the presents first... Thank you for the gift, Uncle Far, Aunt Farther, Aunt Farthest!
What a huge box. What's inside? A portable anti-tuskbeast tent? A twenty-four-hour wilderness alarm system?
Er, what we got you is a massage rocking chair! We figured, since you sit indoors for such long stretches, it'd make work a lot more comfortable...
Um... Even though I won't be sitting indoors from now on, thank you all the same!
Cousin Hop, Cousin Skip, Cousin Jump, what did you get me?
A "Terra Pilgrimage" gift box of thirty kinds of throat lozenges. You have to talk all the time, so we wanted to give you something practical.
...Thanks anyway. Once I'm out in the wilds I might have to shout my lungs out too!
Little Thumpy, we...
Mom, Dad, you really didn't have to get me a present. Running around the house getting the party ready was hard enough.

I'm setting off soon, and thinking about not seeing you for a long while, I do feel a little...
I shouldn't cry now, of all times!
The shape of this package—could it be... new headphones? Amazing! With these, traveling out in the wilds won't be boring at a—
Huh? Why are the headphones attached to a switchboard unit...
Well, you'll be promoted before long, so you ought to have equipment that suits you better!
But what I wanted isn't the kind you use in the switchboard room...?
Oh, let's drop it. We'll talk about the present later—let's eat first—
That's not right, is it? Why do you two act like you have no idea I'm leaving Great Springs? You promised me two years ago. Don't tell me I'm the only one...
Am I the only one who remembers...?
Sigh... Little Thumpy, we haven't forgotten. It's just... it's just that you're doing fine as the town's switchboard operator. There's no need to run off and suffer out there.
That's right. Being a pathfinder is no joke. You need plenty of experience in the wilds and you need to know how the world works before we can let you go with any peace of mind.
And those adventure stories you go on about all day—your grandma probably never imagined you'd swallow them whole...
Wait, are you saying Grandma lied to me?
Those were stories, after all. They can't be exactly like the facts. If you took the parts she made up to amuse you at face value and went out there—
Mom, you... you really think that?
Dad... what about you?
Calm down, calm down, all right? It's your birthday, and our little Thumpy gets to make a wish, doesn't she?
Dad, you'll agree?
I... I agree! Just wait two more years. When you're twenty, your mom and I will let you go exploring on your own, all right?
So that's... what you really think...
You don't believe in Grandma's glorious deeds, and you don't believe I can become a pathfinder on my own.
You think wanting to leave Great Springs is some whim I came up with on the spot, and that Grandma's stories were only to keep me entertained...
Nobody nodded. Nobody shook their head.
If you can't understand how I feel, then I don't need your approval either, do I?
I'm not waiting anymore.
Tani!
Ma'am, please don't panic. I'll help you go bring Tani back!
Hold on, miss.
Sir? If we don't go now, Tani will get too far away.
Sigh. Angelina, let her go. Tani will be back tomorrow morning.
What?
Tani is the smallest-framed Cautus in Great Springs. Her mother and I used to worry she wouldn't be able to do physical work when she grew up.
Maybe because she couldn't do it herself, she was especially fond of the stories my mother Inara told, and wanted to become a pathfinder like her grandma.
But we know Tani. She's not like my mother.

Mother was forthright, and capable in everything she did. She wasn't Infected, yet she had a real gift for Originium Arts. She spent most of her life coming and going alone in the wastes, because she had what it took.
Our Tani has no strength, and no gift for Originium Arts.
She's been clamoring to go out and see the world since she was small, and she's run away from home no fewer than thirty times—but she always gets as far as the town gate and comes back frightened.

Last time it was a pack of tuskbeasts out foraging. The time before that, she mistook the string of turnips a neighbor had hung out to dry in the wastes for a ghost... She's better suited by nature to staying in town as a switchboard operator!
But Tani looked so upset...
Sigh. If that girl sees the whole family coming after her, she'll only hide longer to save face. Still, I really am worried about her health...
Mrs. Tani, I'm from Rhodes Island. Rhodes Island is a medical company, and I know a bit about treating Oripathy myself.
If the whole family going would only backfire...?
Then I'll leave it to you.
I've always known Tani has good taste in friends. With you there, at least we won't worry quite so much...
Even if you and your husband hadn't asked me, I would have gone. Please don't worry.
...Also, maybe it isn't my place to say this, but two years, two years, and then two more years... it's a little strange. I understand Tani quite well, actually.
Sigh...
Huff, huff...
I-I can't stay here another minute! So what if I go out alone? I... I can do it!
Waaah! I'm done for, I'm done for, I'm done for!
All I wanted to do was fix it—how did the circuit board go wrong?!
Boo hoo... The fault might have spread to the town's internal comms already. I can't stay any longer. I'd better head to the next comms tower site...
(Sniffles)
This town really is impossible to stay in...

Dragging her enormous backpack the whole way, Tani finally couldn't run anymore. She picked a spot at random, plopped down, and, looking out at the vast expanse of wasteland before her, she couldn't help starting to sob.
In the night sky, a pale pink star twinkled.
Grandma, I-I don't dare—
It's all right. Look—grab the branch up there tight with both hands, then give a good hard push with your feet, and you'll be up here!
It's t-too high...
Then why didn't you play with the other children? Why did you drag your grandma all the way out here?

...Because... because they said I'm short and my ears are small, like a little doll... and climbing trees and swimming are too dangerous, little dolls can't do that... But I want to play like that too!
I don't want to be just a little doll! I want to be a pathfinder, a pathfinder like you, Grandma. I want to be someone amazing who can cross mountains and ridges!
Well then, what does Grandma's little Thumpy think an amazing person would do?
Um, they'd keep at it and climb up—I can climb up too... Hup!
—Ah, I-I fell! Waaah, that hurts!
All day long, little Tani kept climbing that tall bottletree. She'd fall, have a good cry, and then, with her grandma's encouragement, start climbing again.
By the time the stars filled the whole night sky, she was finally sitting in the highest crown of the tree, side by side with her grandma, looking up at the beautiful stars.
Among them was a pale pink star, twinkling on and off.
A pale pink star. It's like me... So that one is my star!
Grandma, which one is your star?
Grandma's star?
Let me see... Grandma's star is up ahead.
Inara pointed at a star higher up and farther away.
Why is it so far away?
It's not far. Little Thumpy's star is following behind Grandma's star for now, but soon—very soon—it'll catch up.
Little Thumpy will become someone just like Grandma, and go to lots and lots of faraway places, and then nobody will call you just a little doll anymore...
You're Grandma's most amazing granddaughter. I know you'll be able to fly this high and this far too.
Mm...
Fly high and far like Grandma...

Back then, Grandma gave up exploring the Far South, where nobody had ever set foot, to find her settlement a peaceful home. Once everything had settled, she wanted to set out again, and her family stopped her...
My choice is the right one... If we'd listened to our families, neither Grandma nor I would ever have set out for the Far South.
Even if they get worried, even if they get angry when they find out I'm not running back home like I used to, I... I won't care!
I'm going to the Far South. I'm taking my own first step!
Hahaha, good. I've already left Great Springs, I've already—
Huh? Who's there?!
Surround the Great Springs town gate.
Sir!
Surround it? Wait, I'm trying to leave town. Why are you stopping me?
No one leaves.
Wh-what's going on? I haven't done anything, I—
...Agh!
Tani, you just wait! You'll regret this someday!
Don't tell me those two delinquents snorting spicy bottletree powder actually joined some dangerous outfit...
Wh-what do I do? All I wanted was to go to the Far South!!!
Ngh... So bright...
*Rim Billitonian swearing* Where's that light coming from? It's blinding me!
Tani! Get in!
Angie!
I've been looking for you forever. I heard a commotion at the town gate and came over. Who are these people surrounding you?
They're the mysterious organization behind Helmet Sis Amber and Roadblock Bro Peta! The one standing in front is probably their boss!
I saw plenty of people dressed like this in town too. We can't go back—let's get out of here first!
R-right!
Captain, what's the situation?
They're acting suspicious. After them!
Sir!
Are they still behind us?
Right on our tail. At this rate we'll never shake them! But Route Zero is in terrible condition and it's even harder to drive at night, so maybe we can lose them that way—as long as—
As long as we know the road too! There's a big crater up ahead, there's no time to swerve!
Heeeelp—!
Tani?
Aaaaaah—huh?
Next time you get in the car, remember to put your seat belt on first, okay?
Huh?
—Now, hold on to my hand!
Before Tani could react, Angelina gripped her hand tight. She didn't understand why she had suddenly drifted out of the car, or why the ground suddenly looked so very far away.
The dust kicked up by the wheels was left behind, and the hot spring flyers the warmhearted townsfolk had stuffed into the trunk seemed glad to be leaving Great Springs themselves.
They scattered into the night sky and danced around Tani, and only then did Tani realize—gravity was gone.
Tani felt she had never been so light, like a fowlbeast, or a soft flower drifting on the wind.
The Rim Billiton wastes spread out before her, and though her back was to the night sky, she felt as if she were already among the stars, with Angelina's hand as the gravity holding her fast.

She had shaken off the dangerous organization on her heels, shaken off the Great Springs that had penned her in for eighteen years, shaken off her anger and hurt at her family, and shaken off the small fear and self-doubt hidden at the bottom of her heart.
Like a pink star, she went streaking across the night sky.

eps.name: The Chaos of Meeting New Friends

lines.x: Oh no, I didn't control the direction of my Arts well enough—the car spun way too many times in the air!
The supply crate in the back seat should be fine, but... Tani, are you all right?
No...
Feeling sick? Quick, I've got motion sickness pills!
No... not "all right"—amazing, incredibly, unbelievably amazing! This is the best day of my eighteen years! This is adventure, this is the life I wanted! Wow, what a rush!
Um... I'm glad you're not feeling sick, at least. Back when I was practicing my Arts, the Operator who practiced with me got carsick—usually three spins and he'd throw up.
Urp—
Yes, exactly, that's the sound—
Huh? Where is that coming from?
I'll find it! Grandma always said my ears may be small, but they're sharp!
(Perks up her ears)
Urp—
It's inside the supply crate!
Don't open it! I am the fiercest pouched musbeast in the wastes! I'll eat every one of you!
Wow, so scary.
Wow, so scary.
...You two sound like you're barely trying. The least you could do is—urp...
Pouched musbeasts don't eat people, and they don't get carsick. Come on out, mysterious miss.
Ugh... Introductions later—f-first give me one of those motion sickness pills...
What? You're the daughter of Mr. Campbell, Rim Billiton's famous mining magnate—Jacinta Campbell?
Phew— Miss Messenger of Rhodes Island, that herbal tea of yours is quite good.

Thank you. Our Operator Lena pressed it on me before I left. It has a calming effect—
No, wait, we've gotten off track...
Why were you hiding in my off-roader's supply crate?
Well, because my parents only let me take holidays around Great Springs!
It's a famous resort town, and I've lost count of how many times I've been. I've even memorized the geyser eruption schedule...
So I used a little trick to slip away from my bodyguards and find my own fun.
And this little trick was stowing away in my supply crate?
Are these bodyguards you mentioned in league with Helmet Sis Amber and Roadblock Bro Peta?
What on earth are you talking about...
So the people in black I saw inside Great Springs and at the town gate were all your bodyguards, Jacinta. Which means nobody's going to give Tani trouble if we go back to Great Springs now, so—
—Wh-wh-whoa, Jacinta! Since your bodyguards are in Great Springs looking for you right now, shouldn't we not go back just yet?
Of course not! It took me forever to get away. Nobody's sending me back!
Besides, my home is Big Ironton in the south, and my holiday is over, so it's time I headed home anyway.
But if those people aren't villains, and they're bodyguards hired by your parents—
No, no, no, no, no, no. Angelina, you have no idea how overprotective my parents are.
Even when I cross the street, those bodyguards form a human wall to cordon off the crosswalk. With them around I can't do anything!
Well, Angelina, it looks like we have no choice but to keep heading south!
We're not that far from Great Springs yet anyway. Jacinta can wait here while I take you back first, Tani.
How could that work?! This is the middle of nowhere, and Great Springs is at least two hours there and back. You can't leave Mr. Campbell's daughter out here alone!
Can't I?
Can't... she?
O-of course you can't! Because... because...
Grandma told me there are no streetlights on Route Zero, so once night falls, a traveler's tent becomes the only light in the wastes.
To a traveler, that's the comfort you've earned after a whole day on the road. But to the savage tuskbeast packs out in the wastes, it's the same...
(Gulps)
Miss Jacinta, have you ever wondered why we haven't seen a single traveler, or a single tent, by the roadside?
Wh... why...

Because when tuskbeasts eat,
they never spit out the bones.
Messenger of Rhodes Island, I-I'm hiring you to protect me! Especially at night—you are not to leave our tent!
Sigh... Tani, stop scaring Jacinta.
Th-then are you still taking me back?
I'll follow the road south, stop at the next village, settle Jacinta there, and then take you home.
(Quietly) We'll see about that when we get there.
What was that?
I said no problem at all!
Sigh...
The bottletrees on Route Zero~ their bellies are all full of water~♪
All full of water—!
Mine carts loaded with Originium~ whatever you do, don't overheat~♪
They'll explode—!
A Cautus's ears~ aren't afraid of being bent by the wind~♪
Ooh-woo-oh—!
Angelina, why aren't you singing with us!
You said it yourself before you started—this song is a childhood memory for Rim Billitonians. I don't know it...
Oh, right. This feels so much like a graduation trip with classmates that I forgot you're Siracusan.
What does being Siracusan have to do with it? The tune is simple, just follow me—
Ooh-woo-oh—!
...Ooh... woo-oh...
Louder! Sing it like you're proud of those long ears of yours!
Short ears are worth being proud of too!
Then sing it like you're proud no matter what your ears look like. Ooh-woo-oh—!
Ooh-woo-oh—!
Hahaha, nice! Angie can sing our song now!
Pff... All right, check the map, Tani. Didn't you say you have a pathfinder's theory down cold? See whether we're nearly there?
Right!
Ahem, attention please! What we just passed is a little-known landmark on Route Zero, and a place my grandma told me about—the Originium Forest, made entirely of Originium crystals!
By my meticulous calculations, the nearest settlement, Artichoke Village, is one, two, three, four fingers' width ahead. That's right—four hundred meters.
Artichoke Village isn't far from Great Springs, but because of the terrain, even this small, sparsely populated village had a long-range comms tower built in it. It should be quite visible—
Oh! I think I can see the comms tower up ahead. On top of it...
Is there something moving up there?
All three of them squinted, trying to make out the swaying shape in the distance.
It looks like there's a person on the tower, and she's shouting something...
A few minutes earlier
Don't come any closer... Come any closer and I'll act!
Your car smashed my wall to pieces! Half my living room is your engine hood right now!
Stop backing up, you're about to hit our carrot rack! This is the best batch of dried carrots I've ever made—don't knock them down!
I'm truly sorry about the wall, I'll find a way to make it up to you... But this structure really isn't a carrot rack. It's a comms tower my company built!
These towers carried long-range comms for the whole Route Zero corridor for nine months, right up until... until the technical accident two months ago cut it off...
But the two people inside told us when they left that from now on it's ours to manage, and there's no problem at all with drying things on it!
What?!
The people inside said that?
Of course! Everyone remembers it clearly!
First a crew came around here banging and hammering and put up this tower. None of us knew what it was for.
Once the tower was done, two people came in every day on shifts. You could tell they had foul tempers just by looking, so we didn't dare ask what they were doing.
Two months ago, the two of them stormed off.
Before they left, I worked up the nerve to ask what the tower was actually for. They said: "Do whatever you want with it! It's yours to manage now—go dry your carrots!"
And they never came back!
(I'm done for, done for, done for... Now there's no explaining this at all...)
(What do I do, what do I do? Do I... do I flee to the next comms tower site again? But...)
The Anaty in front of them kept backing away, and the equipment on her was about to sweep the golden drying carrots off the rack behind her.
The anxious villagers hurriedly pulled out long homemade farm tools, meaning to move the carrots somewhere safer—but to the flustered girl, the gesture was unmistakably an "attack."
And at this point, there was only one path left—
Steeling herself, the Anaty scrambled up the comms tower.
Hey! We're polite to you and you take it as an invitation to climb! Every step you take could crush this quarter's harvest, and you can't afford to pay for it!
I-I'm not running away again! I'm going to repair Artichoke Village's comms tower no matter what anyone says!
Get down here, daylight hours are precious! I competed with my neighbor at "tail-tag" for a whole month just to claim the best spot on that carrot rack.
My family has made the tastiest dried carrots in all of Artichoke Village five years running. I'm not about to let some sniveling kid ruin it!
I-I'm not coming down. I'm afraid of heights to begin with, so now that I'm up here, I'm absolutely not coming down until the tower is fixed! B-but...
But what?
It's so scary, boo hoo hoo—h-help, somebody help me!
You're calling for help? The nerve!
You're the suspicious person who drove into our village shouting "Comms tower! Comms tower!"—and now you've made it look like we're the unreasonable ones!
What kind of people gang up on one girl like this? This is completely unreasonable—put down your weapons!

I may not have my grandma's command of Originium Arts, but I foresaw that we'd run into people who needed help on the road! I've got plenty of emergency spray in my backpack, more than enough for all of you!
Boo hoo hoo, save me! I-I only came here to do my job, and I'm never working again, boo hoo—!
Stop shouting! I told you people would get the wrong idea if you carried on like that. The reputation of our Artichoke Village, aaargh!
Where did you lot come from—read one too many knight novels?
Everyone, please calm down. I'm a Rhodes Island Messenger passing through, and these two are companions who caught a ride with me.
We all came from Great Springs, which is the northernmost node of the Route Zero long-range comms network. We can confirm that your "carrot-drying rack" really does have long-range comms functions.
And if you doubt the identity of the girl currently crying her heart out... Jacinta?
The Campbells have a partnership with the company that developed long-range comms—Meridian Red Earth. All the equipment on that girl carries their company logo.
What's more, Meridian Red Earth put a lot of effort into promotion in order to monopolize the entire long-range comms industry, and the logo is treated with a special coating.
If we can see the logo on that girl from this far away, then she's definitely with Meridian Red Earth!
In that case, she's an engineer dispatched by Meridian Red Earth, not some suspicious character. There's no need for anyone to be so tense.
By all rights, as soon as one comms tower is repaired, the comms signal for Artichoke Village and the villages around it should come back. That's good news for everyone.
But even if this carrot rack does have comms functions, nobody in our village has any use for it. Broken comms or not, life goes on the same, and the carrots dry the same.
And if fixing the tower does our lives no good at all, and ruins our dried carrots on top of that...
The villagers looking on muttered among themselves.
They seemed convinced that the Anaty on the carrot rack wasn't a suspicious character, but their devotion to the harvest made them unwilling to hand over the right to repair the tower so easily.
Hmm...
Huh? Why's there such a crowd here today?
Well, that sniffling girl up there says our carrot rack isn't a carrot rack, it's some kind of long-range comms tower.
And this Vulpo girl here says that fixing the comms tower won't help with drying carrots, but it'll restore comms with the villages around us.
I mean, it's only a forty-minute walk to the next village, so who needs to go to the trouble of using a terminal? Am I right?
Our saviors—!!!
Huh?
This carrot rack—no, this carrot tower! Can it connect us to my wife's hometown, Turnip Town?!
So you had a fight with your wife Ailsa, and she's gone back to her hometown in a huff. Is that right?
That's... right...
But looking at the map, Artichoke Village and Turnip Town aren't very far apart. Why not go see her?
Well, I'm afraid she might still be angry...
Tch. No guts.
Now that's not fair, miss. My wife isn't a needlefly. How can going to see her be measured in guts?

Since we married last year we've had a fight almost every two months. I used to at least be able to send her a few kind words, and back then I could catch up with her before she was even halfway there.
But the others say they didn't know what the comms tower was for.
I traded three crates of carrots to a passing caravan for the comms device. They never told me the thing needed a carrot rack—er, a comms tower—to work.
I only found out from listening to you all argue!
Um... sir, are any of the carrots on this rack yours?
Sure, that row near the top of the tower. My wife and I grew those carrots together...
Could I borrow two carrots?
I suppose so, but what for?
Hello up there—Miss Engineer from Meridian Red Earth—!
A-are you calling me? Just call me Amelia... I really haven't done anything bad, I only wanted to fix the comms tower, I—
I know, Amelia. Do you see that row of dried carrots to your right?
Dried carrots? Ah, I see them...
Tani tells me Artichoke Village always grows its carrots big and sweet. I got two dried carrots from the gentleman beside me—why don't you try one?
I... eat dried carrots right now? But my legs are shaking...
Tani says the dried carrots here have a special effect—they settle the nerves. It might even help you fix the tower.
R-really?
Hold on, Angie, I never said that.
Shh.
(Chews the dried carrot) Mm... It really is sweet. And... and my legs feel like they have some strength back?
Huh?
(Quietly) That girl's face is deathly pale. She probably is afraid of heights, but her legs giving out is likely low blood sugar.
Amelia, if the comms tower is repaired, will comms between Artichoke Village and Turnip Town come back?

O-of course they will! The villages around Artichoke Village had no signal coverage to begin with. When Meridian Red Earth built the long-range comms towers, it solved the intercity comms problem too.
So as long as the comms tower gets fixed, I can call Ailsa?
As long as it's fixed... y-yes!
Friends of the village! My happiness with my wife rests in your hands!
Please let the engineer fix the comms tower. If she accidentally tramples anyone's carrots, I'll pay for them.
Oh, we can't have you paying. You're already worried sick about your wife as it is.
Since Meridian Red Earth and the Campbells have something of a partnership, I'll cover whatever damage Engineer Amelia causes.
Whoa.
What's with you two!
Boo hoo hoo...
Hey, why are you crying again? Has something else upset you?
No... I only wanted to say thank you... Apart from my family, I've never met anyone as kind as you, anyone willing to believe me, boo hoo...
This time I'm definitely going to f-fix the comms tower! Boo hoo hoo...!
...Angie, is that girl... really dependable?
Here, look up. She may still be crying, but the little robots beside her are already at work.
The robots flitted lightly through the air like little insects after a summer downpour.

They circled the comms tower hung all over with dried carrots, monitoring signal data and tuning modules, while their operator, who had only just dried her eyes, tapped nimbly at a panel to install the comms core.
Beneath the strings upon strings of carrots, Angie's group and the villagers couldn't make out Amelia's expression, which was a kind of luck for her.
Amelia didn't dare imagine what would happen if the people below discovered that the "engineer" they spoke of currently had a face full of nerves—
It's fixed!
H-how is it...?
Why is it taking so long to dial? Don't tell me...
Amelia just retested everything and the signal is connected. There won't be a problem.
It connected! Hello, Ailsa, just hear me out—!
Phew...
Wonderful—everybody wins!
Th-thank you all. If you hadn't stepped in for me, I'd surely still be stuck on that tower crying...
Your technical skills are this solid—how can you still have no confidence? Look, even the villagers who were upset with you before are busy figuring out how to tune the radio!
Amazing work, miss. All of a sudden we can hear anything on the radio! If someone had said fixing the comms tower came with this, who'd have stopped it? No more being bored while we work, eh?
I-I'm just glad you're happy...
"Miss," nothing—show some respect! She's a technical expert the company sent specially to solve our problems—
No, that's not right. She's a Director! She's the Engineering Director! Without that rank, how could she have pulled this off, restoring our signal and giving us the radio too!
Haha, hahaha...
Director, don't just laugh—say a few words!
Th-that's right, I am the Engineering Director the company sent! With my experience, repairing a comms tower is a trifling matter. As long as you're all satisfied, th-that's what counts!
S-sir, did your talk with Ailsa go well? Has Meridian Red Earth's technology resolved your domestic dispute?
...I said Meridian Red Earth's Engineering Director had fixed the tower, and she said, "What's the Director fixing a tower got to do with you," and hung up...
Hahahahahahaha!
I-it's all right! Miss Ailsa is sure to come back in the end!
Oh, she'll come back all right... I'm just afraid her grandmother in Turnip Town will come with her. That grandmother's scolding is really something to behold...
(Grandmother... that's right!)
Actually, do any of you know someone named Inara?
Inara? You mean Inara who founded our village? That fellow who just slunk off—I think his grandmother was Inara's older cousin... or was it younger?
Huh?! Then doesn't that make him my, um... cousin? But he looks about the same age as my dad?
No, wait, it's that Mom and Dad look too young—never mind, please go on!
Inara led a great crowd of people north back then, and our Artichoke Village folk were among them.

There were Infected and healthy people both in that party. Inara said there was a big stretch of hot springs up north, suitable for the Infected to live in, but by the time they got near here, a lot of people truly couldn't walk any farther.
The ones who left the party here were Artichoke Village's earliest residents. They say Inara picked this site with her Originium Arts and her pocket watch!
R-really?! Then do you know about Great Springs up north?
Didn't you say where you were from when you arrived? It was such a racket at the time that I wasn't sure the town up north was called that, so I didn't look into it.
Now that I think about it, my grandfather did often go on about a town up north founded by relatives of his. He's been gone many years now, though.
So Inara didn't just pick the site for Artichoke Village, she founded Great Springs too?
That's right! Inara was my grandma! She founded Great Springs too!
Ha, now this is getting interesting!
Excuse me, is there anything here that my grandma left behind? I'm retracing her journey—she lost her pocket watch somewhere along Route Zero!
Hold on, I'll go ask around—everyone, go ask around!
So, um, cousin? The thing my grandma left behind... is actually in your hands?
Calling it "left behind" is generous—it's more like she forgot it here. Even my grandmother put it out of her mind eventually.
That's wonderful, wonderful! Thank you, cousin, and thank you to your grandmother too!
And thank you, Angelina, thank you, Jacinta, thank you, Amelia—I'm about to become a caster as amazing as my grandma!
So then... the keepsake Grandma left behind, it couldn't be—no, it must be...
Clever Arts for Tasty Dishes: 100 Home Recipes!
Huh?!
Boo hoo... a hundred home recipes... but I can't cook and I can't use Arts...
Don't lose heart, don't lose heart. Your grandmother crossed the whole of Route Zero back then, so it's perfectly normal that her pocket watch isn't here.
I know, sniff...
Phew... I'm finally out. I'll never get used to being surrounded by that many people...
Amelia, you're out.
Could I ask you about the comms tower?
Y-yes?!
I'm from Rhodes Island, and I'm a Messenger, so I've heard a few things about long-range comms technology.
I hear the long-range comms lines in other countries need very powerful casters working Arts to maintain them, and the villagers just said there used to be people inside the tower.
So why is it that after you repaired the tower, you don't have to stay inside?
Oh, that's what you were asking. I thought... er, no, no, let me explain right away.
Ahem. Long-range comms like this were completely unimaginable just a few years ago.
For one thing, the radio waves used for comms get absorbed by the Barrier Layer, and how far waves travel along the ground is quite limited...
For another, even if you avoid Catastrophes, whether you lay cable underground or raise a base station up high, transmitting information gets disrupted by shifts in the Originium environment.
But a dozen or so years ago, technology advanced, and at the same time, research into engineering-related Originium Arts deepened...
I know this one! They say Kazimierz and Columbia both put up mobile base stations!
That's right. Those stations have enormous output, and they only work with a caster who's studied engineering-related Originium Arts very deeply stationed inside.
This is what Ange... Ange...
It's Angie!
Right, right. This is the kind of base station Angie just mentioned, the kind that needs a powerful caster to keep it running.
Base stations consume enormous power, hiring casters is very expensive, and the people working inside them have a higher chance of contracting Oripathy...
So this kind of long-range comms had very limited applications. Basically only the wealthiest and most powerful could use it.
So... Amelia, your job is to let everyone on this land enjoy long-range comms?
M-more or less. Meridian's vision is to cut costs while maintaining comms quality.
And we at Meridian Red Earth, as Meridian's Rim Billiton branch, have gone the furthest in that direction.
Using a semi-automatic Originium-adaptive system, at the cost of the stations being immobile, we succeeded in greatly reducing how much long-range comms depends on a caster's ability...
Immobile? But what if a Catastrophe hits...
Th-that, well, semi-automatic stations really are too heavy. But we've taken all sorts of measures to avoid that problem.
For instance, choosing sites carefully, or using a special underground design in areas where we have to take the risk, or even mounting them directly on nomadic cities!
In any case!
As long as there's a caster of average ability, the station keeps running, which drastically cuts the labor cost of hiring casters.
Average ability... sniff...
D-did I say something I shouldn't have?
No, no. I was just thinking about how amazing you are, Amelia.
I-it's really nothing. In any case, it's the core technology behind the first long-range comms network open to the public in Rim Billiton... no, in all of Terra, which we built along Route Zero!
Question!
Go ahead...?
You still haven't told us why the stations don't need a single person inside anymore.
For that I have to talk about my improvements to the technology.
The first-generation semi-automatic system inside the comms towers has already been upgraded to a fully automatic second-generation version. The towers can now truly operate unmanned!
Whoa...
Though I only just heard that the two casters who used to work here lost their jobs... I feel so guilty...
No, Amelia, technological progress is a good thing!
I know, but...
At the very least they don't have to worry about catching Oripathy in that cramped tower anymore!
And casters are scarce talent, engineering casters especially. Even at average ability, they won't have trouble finding work.
Thank you... you're really kind...
Have you not been a Director for very long?
Wh-what do you mean?
It feels like you haven't held the Director's post that long. Your technical skills are more than qualified, but your mindset hasn't caught up, so other people's words affect you too easily.
You need to temper your mindset more, until in the end it's as solid as your skills!
Heheh, I'm—I'm not that impressive...
Still, didn't your company assign anyone to travel with you? They let a technical staffer set out alone like this?
Y-yes, well...
I have to keep heading south, repairing the comms towers along Route Zero until I reach Big Ironton—which is where our company's headquarters are.
That's odd. Something as important as repairing every comms tower, and they send just one person?
Don't tell me... you've been frozen out?
Huh?
Um, put that way, it wouldn't be wrong. They really did...
Meridian Red Earth looks like such a proper company. How could they do something like that?
Once a company gets big there are all sorts of power struggles, even at the most advanced firms. My dad used to say it all the time.
Wait, if that's the plot, then maybe even the Great Disconnect...
L-let's drop it. Let's not talk about the company for now.
Well said!

A truly good company may have internal struggles, but it would never mistreat genuine talent. If Meridian Red Earth is freezing you out like this, they clearly don't take you seriously as a Director at all!
Why go back to a company like that? You're so talented—I can invest in you directly on behalf of the Campbells and let you develop something entirely your own!
Th-that's still much too far off for me...
Right now I just hope to find a way south. There are several comms towers I still haven't repaired.
Although, after my car hit that villager's wall, they took it apart to patch the wall, haha...
We could give you a ride?
"We"?
Angie, me, and Jacinta were heading south anyway. I'm going to the Far South with Angie, and Jacinta is going back to the Campbell house in Big Ironton. Want to come along?
I-if that's all right... then I...
Angie's the kindest person there is, so she's bound to say yes, right?
Of course I can take Jacinta and Amy to Big Ironton. But you are going back to Great Springs!
Why?! Does Angie think my goal of becoming a pathfinder is a joke too? Do even you think Grandma's stories were only to keep me entertained?
Of course not.
I've never thought there was anything wrong with setting out on the road to your dream because of one word of encouragement, one story, one bit of longing.
You already have the resolve to leave Great Springs. But if you're not doing this to go farther, and you're still sulking at your parents, then I shouldn't take you to the Far South.
...Angie, you heard it just now. Artichoke Village was founded by Grandma too.
That's true, but...
It came back to me while I was searching for the pocket watch with the villagers—Grandma actually told me the story of Artichoke Village too.
The village's name, its location, its layout... I heard all of it, and I forgot all of it.
If I don't set out, then as I slowly grow up I'll forget Grandma's stories one by one, and I'll forget my dream of becoming a pathfinder too.
And in the end, even Grandma's pocket watch—the thing I wanted most as a child, the thing I admired most, the thing that could make anything happen—will stop mattering.
Angie, from the moment I left Great Springs, I stopped sulking at my family. All I want is to retrace Grandma's journey and find the pocket watch she lost by accident. That's all.
All right, you've convinced me. But remember, if you run into danger on the road—
I take the spray out of my backpack, or shout for your help!
And once I find Grandma's pocket watch, everything will be fine! It's the Arts Unit she made her legends with. I'm definitely going to find it!
Sigh. I somehow feel like you've talked circles around me again.
Come on, before we set off for our next stop, Solar Valley, let's take care of some of the dried carrots the villagers pressed on us—
—Delicious!
It's rare to find dried carrots this good. I feel like turning them into a hot dish would make them two or three times better...
Showing off your cooking?
...If I showed off my cooking everyone would get a stomachache. Better not... Jacinta?
I didn't bring a personal chef and I've never earned a culinary certificate, but I can assist! How about Amy takes the pan?
The only thing I can make is reheated frozen pizza... If it's just shredding dried carrots I might manage. I'll try not to cut my hand—
All right, all right, I'll do it...
Wow, even a stew of just dried and fresh carrots can turn out this delicious! Even a pouched musbeast would want to steal your recipe!
Don't twist the story your grandmother told you. Pouched musbeasts only steal the words that haven't been said out loud.
I've actually wondered since I was little—what exactly counts as words that haven't been said out loud?
Things you hide?
Ngh, the stew's so hot, so hot—
Lies you tell?
Ah, this is so much better than frozen pizza, boo hoo...
Or knots in your heart?
All right, stop guessing. We'll find out when we meet a pouched musbeast, won't we?
Mm, true enough.
Amy, do those "Little Bugs" beside you need a rest too?
"Little Bugs"?
Ah, you mean these signal emitters? They're detecting comms signals nearby. Even when a comms tower is somewhere unmarked on the map, we can find it.
How interesting...
Hey, Jacinta, with the Campbells' means, you must have seen plenty of little robots like these?
I've seen them, sure. But it's the first time I've seen someone use them for comms engineering work—and while looking completely un-self-congratulatory about it.
Huh... s-so I should be congratulating myself?
A young lady like Jacinta talks in circles. She just wants to praise you but is too embarrassed to come out and say it.
Wh-who asked you to translate like that!
Heheh, are you looking for an excuse to say a pouched musbeast stole the praise you didn't say out loud?
Has anyone ever told you that you're really good at spoiling a moment?
They have. At least ten relatives have said so—want me to list them for you?
A pair of clear, dark little animal eyes reflected the four noisy girls. It twitched its nose, catching the scent of food, but restrained its instincts and didn't come closer.
It crouched in a corner by the tent, stuffing the things it liked into its precious pouch while quietly observing the humans in front of it.
Waiting for a chance to commit its next theft? Or trying to read the minds of the four before it?
Perhaps neither. Perhaps it had simply caught a scent it liked and couldn't help feeling drawn to them.
The legendary creature didn't move. Only the fuzz on its head swayed a few times in the wind...
Huh? Look, isn't there something small moving over by the tent?
...It really does look that way. Amy, can you see it clearly?
I can't make it out. Angie?
It looks like some creature I don't recognize... Could it really be a pouched musbeast?
...There's no way. Even Grandma only saw one after untold hardships, and we're just camping here.
I suppose that's true... Still, better safe than sorry. I'll go take a look over by the tent.
I'm coming too!
...Before any one of them could fix it precisely in their sight, it vanished into the wind, like the words that were never said out loud.

eps.name: A Sun Rises in the Valley

lines.st: To Rhodes Island, to this land, to Angelina the Messenger... where exactly do I belong?
I don't mean "belonging" in the sense of rank within a family. It's just that more and more I feel... like someone who has always been drifting on the outside.
There are so many remarkable people on Rhodes Island. They handle their work with room to spare, and others place great hopes in them.
And there are many who simply do their own work steadily, burying themselves in their duties day after day for decades, trusted wholeheartedly by everyone.
I've become friends with quite a few people, and together we've accomplished things. I've received more kindness than I ever imagined.
And yet... I still feel that what I've done isn't enough. Not nearly enough.

lines.x: Hm-hm, riding my little burdenbeast, bumping and swaying down south♪
From the map, Solar Valley is right ahead.
Amelia, is the next comms tower to repair here?
That's right.
So Solar Valley Mechanical Industries doesn't just do industrial manufacturing—they have an Originium mine on this scale too...

Plenty of foreigners think the "Rim Billiton Mining Industry Alliance" is a behemoth controlling every mine in Rim Billiton. These days, though, it's more like a unified signboard the country's mining industry shows the outside world.
There's no way Solar Valley Mechanical Industries would let go of a mining district as big as Solar Valley.
But it just looks like an ordinary valley mine... It's big, sure, but I don't see a sun inside it.
Huh? There's really a sun in Solar Valley? I've never heard that...
Tani, did your grandma tell you some story about Solar Valley?
She did!
They found it so funny to have guessed what Tani was about to say that easily that they couldn't help exchanging looks and laughing.
"There was a golden, glittering sun in the valley. A little Cautus saw it and wanted so badly to touch it that she dug a tunnel deeper and deeper, until she was accidentally trapped inside..."
