"That little Cautus was like you—she loved stomping her feet. But she'd never learned how to stomp a distress signal, so all she could do was stomp frantically at random, and nobody up above realized she was calling for help."
"Grandma pressed her ear to the ground, heard that sound, and knew there was a little Cautus just like you trapped down below."
Tani imitated her grandmother's tone with the ease of someone who had told the story a thousand times.
The more she told it, the more excited she got, until she couldn't help standing up and acting it out—
When nobody else knew what to do, Grandma raised her hand, opened up a path, and rescued the person trapped down there!
That's why I've always wanted to find Grandma's pocket watch!
Speaking of which, I think Tani's parents mentioned your Originium Arts are actually... not very good?
...Ahem. No need to be delicate—they're bad. Very bad.
I borrowed your Arts Unit on the road, remember? I tried, and I couldn't manage a single one of the Arts in that Clever Arts for Tasty Dishes.
...Th-that is indeed not very good.
But Grandma's pocket watch is different! Grandma did so many great things with it—they say even a petty thief who got hold of her watch became hard to deal with!
I'm Grandma's granddaughter. If I had it, I'd become amazing too, wouldn't I?
Tani's already amazing, but I think you're right!
The people in Solar Valley might still remember Grandma. If I ask enough people, maybe I'll even find it here!
The girl's head, stuffed full of dreams, bobbed up and down with the jolting of the vehicle as it crossed one hill after another.
I have some letters and parcels to deliver. I can bring you along and ask while I'm at it!
Mm-hm!
All right, the mining district is right ahead. There are miner's earplugs in my bag—put them in quickly, or the sound of the landship running will rattle your head senseless.
When I first got to Rhodes Island, I once forgot my earplugs while the landship was moving, and I thought my ears were going to break!
Angelina, you've lived on a nomadic vessel too?
Wow, how interesting. I've seen so many new things on this trip—I'm so glad I met all of you!
Haha...
Angelina gave the horn two cheerful taps.
You'll get to see Solar Valley Industries' vessel soon enough, too.
We're almost there—over this slope, and Solar Valley is right in front of us!

Angelina floored the accelerator, and the vehicle struggled up the slope, trying to get over the mountain of mine tailings ahead and on to the open mining district and that enormous Solar Valley Industries vessel.
Even through earplugs, the sound of mechanized mining grew clearer. The others got excited and poked their heads out the windows, eager to see what lay beyond the slag heap as soon as possible.
(Ugh, I'm getting carsick again...)
(Boo hoo hoo, I'm begging you, Solar Valley, please let me repair the comms tower without any trouble...)
(I've come this far. I'm amazing! I'm definitely going to find Grandma's Arts Unit!)
But when the vehicle finally crested the slag mountain, what greeted them wasn't the magnificent nomadic vessel they'd imagined—it was—
Angie, there's someone up ahead!
Where did he come from?!
—Aaah! Where did that car come from?!
A few minutes earlier
Fetch the ball, fetch the ball, fetch the ball again...
...I've already fetched a hundred tennis balls...
Again! Good, very good! That shot was a big improvement over the last one!
Come on, serve, swing! Two more days of training and we'll have a real shot at the top three in this year's cricket tournament!
Urgh... ngh, ngh...
If long-range comms weren't broken, I would never be out here playing ball with you lot—!
And it's a cricket tournament, so why are we training with tennis balls?!
All ball sports connect to each other. Tennis lays the foundation for cricket! Once the foundation's solid, I'll call the boys over for cricket drills!
Come on, keep it up, good, hold that form! One more set!
Run, get running!
Aaargh! This is exactly why I hate coming back to headquarters!!!
The poor, scrawny Cautus went running across the mining district again. He'd almost convinced himself this torment would never end—but then he spotted his way out—
Hm? A car's driving in?
An unfamiliar car—which means... I can fake getting hit?
Heheh, this will be the last ball of my special training!
—Aaah! Where did that car come from?!
Yikes...
I've never seen one built that big...
A Cautus!
Hsss— So you're telling me those four drove that car that's about to fall apart down off the slag heap and sent you flying while you were fetching a ball?
(Nods) Owwww, owwww... My arm hurts, my leg hurts, nothing feels right. There's no way I can keep training!
You're the one who was driving? With these kids in the back?
I'm very sorry for hitting this gentleman... But I was watching the road, and there was nobody in front of us, and I didn't feel us hit anything either...
Owwww! You still hit me!
Er... Should I have them compensate you somehow?
No need for compensation. Just give me two days off.
Time off? That's not something I can approve—
Who got hit by a car?
Me, it's me, owwww, owwww... I'd like two days off...
Aren't you already off? Since the Great Disconnect you can't reach your clients in northern Rim Billiton, so all you can do is wait for news here at headquarters.
And you haven't been working this whole time either.
Not work—I mean tennis... Owwww, owwww...
It's fine, exercise rehabilitation is my specialty. You weren't hit hard anyway, so more exercise will get the blood flowing and clear the bruising right up—
Owwwwwwww...
Anyway, you girls—what brings you to Solar Valley at a time like this? Visiting relatives? The terrain around here is complicated; it's impressive you found your way in.
We came because of the Great Disconnect! This is Miss Amelia, Engineering Director at Meridian Red Earth, and she's here to repair the comms tower!
(Nods hard)
Ah, so you're here to fix the tower—
Hm? Repair the comms tower?
Er, weren't you hit by a car—
Oh, it's fine, it's fine.
Miss, you should have said right away that you're here to repair the comms tower!
I'm Solar Valley Industries' liaison, and dealing with outside parties is my specialty. Please, stay close and I'll take you to the supervisor right now~
Huh? Ah, all right.
But aren't your arm and your leg and all the rest of you in terrible pain...? Are you sure you're all right like this...
It's nothing! Just the thought of being of service to you cured me on the spot!—Ah, but I still can't play tennis. No cricket either, haha.
Amy, I'll come with you. I've never watched a comms tower being repaired up close!
Certainly, ladies. It's a pleasure to serve you both~
We're off, then. You two go deliver your letters and we'll meet back here later!
Right!
Oh, and I've met you before at New Rhodes Island, Miss Angelina.
I've helped your friend this time, so on my next order with Rhodes Island, you'll have to get Miss Closure to give me the friends-and-family price~!
Er... Since he isn't going to pursue it and doesn't seem to want that time off anymore, I'll be going.
One moment, please. My friend here would like to ask whether a woman named Inara came here some ten-odd years ago?
Something that long ago, I couldn't say...
You'd do better to ask inside the mining district. Here are your visitor passes—hold on to them~
Repair the comms tower? Meridian Red Earth never notified us about that.
Still, given how poor comms have been since the Great Disconnect—show me your repair certification, and then go ahead.
Eep!
What's the matter?
Th-th-th-that is, I-I don't have my certification on me...
Then that won't do. If you can't even prove you're a certified repair technician dispatched by Meridian Red Earth, how could I let you touch our comms equipment with any peace of mind?
Miss Amelia, if your certification isn't on you, where did you leave it?
I-I did have it, but remember the pouched musbeast that came? It stole my bag...
And by the time I found the bag again, everything made of paper inside was gone. It may have eaten them, just like those letters...
A pouched musbeast? But didn't we just see wrong—
No, no, we did! Pouched musbeasts exist! Sir, I even have photos of her repairing a comms tower!
A legend like the pouched musbeast, plus a few photographs, is hardly enough for me to let someone without repair certification work on our comms tower.
Now now, Mr. Barton, isn't there something I could do about this?
You? All you want is to get out and do business somewhere so you can dodge the cricket tournament.
(Lets his ears droop in displeasure)
If you can't produce the certification, I'll have to ask you all to leave.
Excuse me! I wanted to ask whether you know my grandma? She had ears just like mine, and she was a very powerful caster—she could split open a mine shaft with a single Art!
You remember her? Oh, the miners over there would know better? All right, thank you!
Hold on, Tani. You never asked about the name properly.
Oh, right... Heheh...
Miss Miner, do you know my grandma Inara? Back when Solar Valley Industries had just made its name abroad, she took part in an underground rescue here!
That's wonderful, you remember! Could you tell me about it?
Hm? You'd rather not talk about her? Ask someone else?
A-all right...
That's strange.
Maybe someone with a similar name did something bad.
Mm, I think so too.
—Excuse me, do any of you know a Cautus named Inara?
Huh, what...?
Tani?
You're saying Grandma was sent by another group of miners in the company to cause trouble...? To fight over a good vein they'd just discovered?
So you're Short-Ears Inara's granddaughter?
"Short-Ears Inara"?
Hmph, I needn't have asked. Your ears are exactly like hers.
With ears that short, what else would we call her—Long-Ears?
Um...
Never mind, never mind. Looking at you, you clearly didn't inherit that one's rotten insides. Stop asking around and go enjoy yourself.
What did you say?
...Listen, kid, I'll say this upfront: I've got nothing against you. But if you absolutely must know, I'm not going to put in any good words for your grandmother.
Say it, then! What's so bad about saving someone?
Back then we Gantleys had just found a new Originium vein—high grade, easy to extract. That was a good thing, wasn't it?
Er... it was.
Well, the McCartys, who'd always been at odds with us, insisted they'd found it first. So the two sides fell out and made a racket for a long while.
But what does that have to do with my grandma...
Your grandmother? Hmph. Short-Ears Inara had nothing to do with any of it. She was just passing through, same as you.
At the time some kid had burrowed underground on her own. If we'd waited a bit, someone would've gone down to get her. But your grandmother—hmph, for a few of the McCartys' filthy coins...
...she made a huge scene down there, showing off those sorry little Arts of hers!
In the end the kid was rescued, all right, but the business drew the compliance department down on us, and they came down equally hard on us and the McCartys. Neither side got the extraction rights.

Some people said back then that the old woman might not have been hired by the McCartys at all—that she was sent from above to muddy the waters, since they can't stand to see a vein that good in one family's hands...
Tani, it's time to go.
But Grandma's story is still—
Let's go.
What... what does that mean...?
"There was a golden, glittering sun in the valley. A little Cautus wanted to touch it, so she dug a tunnel deeper and deeper, until she was accidentally trapped inside..."
"The little Cautus was like you—she loved stomping her feet, but she'd never learned how to stomp a distress signal..."
When nobody else knew what to do, Grandma raised her hand, opened up a path, and rescued the person trapped down there...
Isn't that how the story goes...?
Tani's ears slowly drooped. "Why have they gone limp like dried-out cauliflower?"—she remembered her grandmother comforting her that way once.
Were all of Grandma's stories... really just made up to put me to sleep?
Why believe that person instead of your grandmother?
My family always thought Grandma's stories weren't entirely true, that some were made up to put me to sleep... And now that person says so too...
And you? Do you think so as well? Do you think your grandmother was a show-off, or an industrial spy?
Grandma wasn't like that at all!
Exactly. You ran off following in your grandmother's footsteps. Why take one side's word for it?
And think about it—what that person just described is actually a lot like the story your grandmother told you. The two sides simply read it differently, don't they?
So all we have to do is find the child who was rescued back then...

eps.name: A Sun Rises in the Valley

lines.x: Huh? She went down the shaft? But there haven't been any extraction jobs these past few days, have there?
It's because there are no extraction jobs that she had to go down. What she went down isn't a mine shaft—it's the conduit shaft our internal comms system runs through.
A while back we all switched over to Meridian Red Earth's wireless system, and then the Great Disconnect hit and we had to haul the old equipment back out of storage.
The old system's many years old, and after sitting unused for a while it's nothing but faults. She went down to sort out those old problems.
Then could you tell me where she went down, and where she's headed?
I could, but have you ever been down a mine?
My uncle Barnett works in the mines, and he took me down a few times when I was little. I only need to find someone—I won't linger...
...Would you like a carrot candy?
Pff. Little miss, how old do you think I am, trying to bribe me with candy?
Heheh...
...Tsk, tsk. This carrot candy is quite good.
She didn't go down that deep anyway. It's just that the paths down there are hard to read. I was crawling around in them every day when I was seven or eight.
See that entrance over there? The red X on this diagram is where she's doing the inspection. Remember—in quick and out quick.
Here, take this walkie-talkie too. It runs on the old internal comms system.
I have my own comms device—
Even Meridian Red Earth's equipment needs special signal boosting for Solar Valley. Your own comms device is useless down the shaft.
Thank you!
Hello, hello, Angelina, can you hear me?
I can, I can. Signal's stable!
I know how to get to the old system's base station now. Don't worry, that route is perfectly safe! Wait up there for my good news!
All right. I'll call you every five minutes, so remember to keep in contact!
No problem~
Phew—
You can do this, Tani!
Ten meters, twenty meters. With her headlamp wobbling, Tani walked alone deeper into the pitch-black tunnel.
Mm, this is going pretty smoothly.
It's just so dark down here... I'd better be careful not to miss a step...
...Finally got the line connected. Now if the power test comes back clean, I can call it a day.
Come to think of it, this place looks oddly familiar... Déjà vu?
Hmm...
...So this is where it was.
Oh well, it's fine. It's been so many years—they must have reinforced the weak spots long ago...
A cave-in?!
Argh... my arm!
0030 calling headquarters, 0030 calling headquarters...
This is bad. I...
What am I supposed to do...
Hello, hello, Tani? It's been five minutes. How are you doing?
Tani? Tani? Can you hear me?
Something's wrong—!
S-s-sir, look, this whole bundle is my comms cores. See how carefully I've protected them? These are all things I genuinely need for the repairs along the way!
You're in charge of a comms tower too, so you must be able to tell these aren't props for a con. I... I really am an engineer here to repair the signal tower!
As I said, none of that proves your identity.
(Quietly) No no no I absolutely can't stop here maybe I should just set off their fire alarm and slip in while they're panicking?
(Quietly) Yes, if I sneak in that way I'm sure to get my chance to repair it—
(Quietly) Don't be absurd! What matters right now is identity! Do you have anything on you at all that proves who you are?
(Quietly) This really is all I have...
(Quietly) Then even I'm starting to have doubts! What exactly are you—
That's right! Mr. Barton!
What is it?
My name is Jacinta Campbell, and I hold shares in Solar Valley as well—may I vouch for Amelia as a shareholder and let her repair the comms tower?
...Identity fraud is a very serious crime, miss.
I know my shares don't amount to much in Solar Valley. But surely you've heard of Mia and Liam Campbell?
Quite the opposite—they're so famous that every would-be swindler tries to claim a connection to them. We're not aware of any shareholder named Jacinta.
Y-you're not?
(Quietly) If you're going to con someone, at least act tough about it! Going soft all of a sudden kills the whole effect!
No, I'm not conning anyone!
You can look me up in the shareholder register! My name will definitely be in there!
The supervisor eyed Jacinta suspiciously, but the girl in front of him was being altogether too solemn about it.
Hm, she really is here. Jacinta Campbell. The photo is of a small child, but... grown up, she'd certainly look like you.
Phew...
Why am I so relieved, honestly... Never mind. Mr. Barton, does this mean Amelia can go fix the tower?
...I'll need to discuss the matter with the others.
In any case, I apologize for my earlier discourtesy. The two of you are welcome to stay in the mining district for a while until we reach a conclusion.
Stay for a while? Does reaching a conclusion take that long?
Because this also touches on our negotiations with Meridian Red Earth in Big Ironton, and with long-range comms down, it takes time for Messengers to travel back and forth.
That does complicate things. Miss Angelina, who's traveling with us—
A-a-a-absolutely not! Can't we go fix the tower right now, Jacinta—Mr. Barton!
Er... Is it th-that urgent?
It really is urgent—and Angelina is in a hurry too!
And yet the one in the biggest hurry right now seems to be you.
I really am in a hurry, and I can't help it—the truth is, I ran off without telling my company!
What?!
I... I never told you before because I was afraid you'd—
worry about me—
—The truth is, Meridian Red Earth's Engineering Director isn't a field technician to begin with, but a research and development staffer. That's why I don't have an engineer's certification!
Surely you have certification as an R and D staffer?
It—it's right here! This is my employee badge. My name and employee number are both on it!
(Quietly) ...Didn't you just say those tools were the only thing that could prove your identity? What's this, then?
(Quietly) I-I'm so sorry! I panicked and said a pouched musbeast stole my paper documents, and then producing a badge that doesn't exactly match, I was afraid it would...
(Quietly) You've got quite a knack for quick thinking under pressure... Once the tower's fixed, any interest in coming to Sargon to do business with me?
(Quietly) S-Sargon? Sir, please don't distract me. I'm already falling apart here...
(Quietly) All right, all right.
It is the same style as the badges of the people who came to install them, and the color's different too... It looks legitimate enough. Though your company doesn't put positions on its badges?
The company—the company favors flat management, so...
Fine. So what is this all about, Miss Amelia?
I... I was in charge of developing the long-range comms system. It went into operation smoothly, but upper management still felt the books didn't balance and wanted expenses cut further!
So I iterated on it and made the fully automatic second-generation system! B-but my colleague... um, Mr. Ashton, he's dreadfully careless in his work!
The data he submitted to me had plenty of errors, and he didn't run the tests properly. Everyone was in a rush, so the Gen-2 system went live in a great hurry...
The result was the Great Disconnect, and the company insists on holding me responsible—compensation, liability, all of it. But it clearly isn't my fault!
Meridian Red Earth... Companies that started out in Columbia do all seem to have this problem to some degree. Our Rim Billiton companies never do that sort of thing.
But by running off on your own like this, aren't you still cleaning up after the company?
That's...
...They're putting all the compensation and liability from the disconnect period on my head. The sooner it's fixed, the less they can squeeze out of me...
And I—I'm not doing all this only for the company! The truth is, I've always had a dream—
Jacinta, Amelia? Why are you still here?
And you are... a Rhodes Island Operator? I'm Barton, the supervisor here. What's happened?
Mr. Barton, there's been an accident down the shaft. One of your employees and our friend Tani are both trapped in the tunnel!
Suspected cave-in at conduit shaft K3, connection down below, two people trapped...
That conduit shaft sits right in the mining subsidence zone. We reinforced it a few years back, so by rights there shouldn't have been an accident.
But Originium mines all over Rim Billiton are ramping up output right now. Some bastard blinded by money probably cut into the support pillars nearby, and that's how this happens...
Never mind, assigning blame comes later. Right now what matters is rescuing them. Better the conduit shaft goes first than the mined-out area.
The supervisor let out a heavy sigh and looked over each of the three faces in turn.
I know a Cautus thinks nothing of going down a shaft or burrowing into a hole, and the cause of this accident has nothing to do with Miss Tani. But she is trapped all the same.
As her friends, every one of you has a more impressive background than the last. So tell me—what do you intend to do now?
We're lucky enough that Solar Valley isn't holding us responsible. I doubt Rhodes Island, the Campbells, or Meridian Red Earth would turn around and press other matters.
As for what to do...

Thanks to Amelia's modifications, all four of our terminals can connect to the long-range comms system, and I heard from a miner that the comms tower had its signal specially boosted for the mine shafts—
Please allow Miss Amelia to go repair the comms tower right now. Then we can reach the people trapped down there!
...All right. I'll send some people to show you the way.
Mr. Barton, we've heard about the situation.
Good. Then I don't need to explain.
Which one of them is the Engineering Director here to do the repairs?
That's me—
—Waaah, I-I-I can run on my own, don't carry me over your shoulder, I-I-I'm afraid of heights!
(Loudly) —If there's anything else I can help with, just come find me, ladies!
Huff—huff—Don't panic, don't panic, Tani! The path ahead just caved in. You're fine, you're not hurt!
Wh-what should I do right now? Right, contact Angelina first. She's up there, she'll tell the others and they'll help figure something out!
What do I do, what do I do? Why would it break down now of all times? Ah, and that repair worker! She must be trapped down there!
In her agitation, Tani couldn't help starting to stomp her feet again.
Until then the quiet underground tunnel had held nothing but her own sounds, but now, as if answering her stomping, a jumble of noise came faintly up from below.
—Hold on, I think I heard something...?
Thump-thump, thump, thump-thump-thump!
It sounds like stomping... all jumbled up, really frantic...
Is that the repair worker making it...?
Tani stood in the pitch-black tunnel, a little tense.
She couldn't help starting to wonder: if Grandma were here, what would Grandma do?
Grandma would use her incredible Originium Arts to open a path in one go and pull them out! But I'm not amazing like Grandma. I can't do anything...
The only part of me that's like Grandma is my ears... Huh, ears?
Thump-thump, thump, thump-thump-thump!
The faint stomping sounded like urging, and like encouragement too.
Tani perked up her ears sharply, concentrating on where the sound was coming from.
..."That little Cautus was like you—she loved stomping her feet. But she'd never learned how to stomp a distress signal, so all she could do was stomp frantically at random"...
"Grandma pressed her ear to the ground, heard that sound, and knew there was a little Cautus just like you trapped down below."—She must be so scared down there all alone!
I-I'm scared too... but isn't wanting to actually accomplish something exactly why I ran away from home?
My backpack can protect me, and my hearing is good. Comms are down right now, but maybe I can find where she is!
Tani, believe in yourself. You're capable of accomplishing something!
Y-you can go find that repair worker first, so she won't be so frightened!
You need the toolbox? Here!
Can't reach the screws up there? I've got it!
No cracks or bending in the main mast, antenna securely mounted, lightning-grounding resistance within the specified range...
Faster, I have to go faster—
I absolutely cannot make a mistake this time...!
Amelia worked with quick, sure hands, and the minutes and seconds ticked past.
There, the new comms core is installed!
Wonderful, Amy!
Good. I've passed the news to the miners handling the rescue. They're already trying to get into the conduit shaft.
It's just that the comms haven't been tested yet, so it might not be very stable...
Tani, Tani, please, pick up...
That's odd. Why are there so many forks down here...?
The sound came from this way, I'm sure of it. Following this path down should lead to where the repair lady is!
Huh? Why is there a pit here...
—Krrsh, krrsh... Tani! ...where... are you?
Angelina?
It's me! Tani, how are you doing?
...It's through? Get her to come back, there are a lot of forks down there...
—Go back? No, I—
Hold on, by the scan... the path she's on is the right one!...
Heheh, see!
She just needs to go a bit farther down... tell her to keep going down and turn left at the fork, and she'll find that repair worker...!
Farther down, then left...
Tani, did you hear that? I'll be waiting for you up here... and Jacinta—and Amy!
The emergency exits from the conduit shaft have all been cleared so it's absolutely safe, and the medics and rescue team are here too!
You can do it, you can do it! We believe in you!
Mm!
Thump-thump-thump, thump, thump-thump!
As if it had heard the voices from above, the stomping below suddenly sped up.
Found it, this is the place!
Ngh, what a narrow gap—it's fine, it's fine, I can squeeze through!
Sigh. Sounds like the noise up there stopped again. I knew it—that must have just been the collapse...
Comms are down and my arm seems to be in bad shape, so I'd better just wait quietly for rescue. Maybe someone will find me...
Sigh. Will someone come pull me out this time too, the way they did when I was little...?
That kind, dashing grandma...

Ah, there you are—the child who never learned to stomp a distress signal.
Let's have a look. How did you get all the way down here by yourself?
...Oh my, you dug quite a long tunnel.
Inara reached out and stroked the mud-covered little Cautus in front of her. The rough calluses on her palm brushed the girl's skin, and she burst into tears again.
Digging a tunnel this long at your age—you're quite something.
All right, climb onto my back. I'll carry you out.
The little Cautus squirmed about on Inara's back, then grabbed hold of Inara's ear and, as if finally reassured, stopped sniffling.
Haha, that's fine. Hold on tight, then—don't fall off!
Those short, fluffy ears...
I-I think I'm seeing those ears again... they really are exactly the same...
Ah, there you are—the repair lady who never learned to stomp a distress signal!
Have I passed out from the pain and started dreaming...? How are even the w-words the same...!
Heheh, come on, I've found the way out. Follow me!
—Huh?
Wait, aren't you a repair worker? What's this big power drill...?
It's... it's my lucky charm...
Let me see... your arm is pinned, but... it's all right, there's room to pry it up...
I'll try to lever the earth and rock off!
Huff... huff...
Hss... Wh-where have we gotten to?
Almost there! Miss, all we have to do is follow this path upward and we're sure to get out!
All right...
Huff... huff...
I'm so sleepy... Is there not enough oxygen down here? Are we going to...
N-no we're not! I'm shorter than you and I'm fine, so it can't be the oxygen!
Can we... stop for a bit? I'm so tired, and I'm scared, and it's so dark here...
We can't give up halfway! If you're tired, lean on my shoulder!
I don't want to be a burden on you...
You're not a burden, and besides... besides, we're going to make it! This was only a minor cave-in—
Tani suddenly remembered something from when she was small.
Back then she had been just like the person beside her—tired, hurting, and afraid.
What had Grandma done then?
Grandma... she told me a story.
...A story?
Yes, a story.
Let me tell you a story. As long as you have stories and company, however long the road, you can walk it in the time of a few stories!
Waaah—Grandma, my ear hurts so much!
That's because you've got prickly burrs tangled in your ear again. Here, let me get them out.
No, no, no, it hurts!
If we don't get them out they'll knot up, and then you'll lose the whole ear. If you'll let me untangle them, I'll tell you a story. How's that?
Mm... all right...
This time I'll tell you about a valley with an enormous, dazzling sun in it.
Because that sun was so big and so beautiful, everyone wanted it. But there was only one sun, so every day people argued and fought over who would have it.
Oh no, what happened then?
Did you use your pocket watch to smash the sun in the valley into pieces and turn it into stars scattered all over the ground?
Haha... If only Grandma were really that impressive...
...But however it came about, people really don't fight over it anymore, because now every one of them has a beautiful star of their own.
A valley with a sun... a valley strewn with stars...
Grandma, is there really a place called Solar Valley? Is there really a sight like that there?
Of course there is. When my little Thumpy grows up, she can go see it with her own eyes.
The sounds underground were terribly noisy in Tani's ears. Sand and gravel kept sliding away underfoot, machinery rumbled in the distance, and up ahead there seemed to be the buzz of people talking.
She shook her ears hard, trying to shake all of it—including the question that had just surfaced—out of her head.
Fussing over the sounds underfoot, hesitating over which way to go, always wondering whether the stories were true or false...
No, no, no. None of that matters now!
Grandma was right—"go see it with your own eyes"... I'm going to see for myself!
There's only one thing I have to do right now, and that's get the repair lady out of here!
There's no rush. When you're grown and walking your own road, Tani...
you'll find your own "pocket watch" along the way.
My own pocket watch?
But I want your pocket watch, Grandma. With your pocket watch I could be amazing like you and turn a sun into stars!
Where on earth did she drop it?
Hmm... where did I drop it? Maybe Big Ironton, maybe Solar Valley, maybe the Far South...
Mm... where did she drop it? Maybe Big Ironton, maybe Solar Valley, maybe the Far South...
Mm... mm! We'll find it, we're sure to find it...
...Over here!
Is that other people's voices?!
...Outside! Almost there! Keep going!
Thank goodness!
Here, where is this... so bright...
Inara...
D-don't separate me from Short-Ears Inara... boo hoo, when can we get out...
Uh, haha...
Ah, I-I can see outside! One more step, miss, just one more step!
A strong gust laden with sand swept past, and Tani, already covered in dust from the shaft, was instantly filthier still.
Hah—!
Goodness, look, miss!
Fresh air rushed into her nose, and Tani couldn't help opening her mouth and taking a huge breath of air full of sunlight.
The body beside her, which had been trembling nonstop with fear, slowly relaxed once it felt the sun.
In the glaring sunlight, the friends she had known for only a handful of days crowded around the shaft entrance, worried and anxious, unsure whether to rush forward or let the rescue team work first.
Phew...
Miss, the story's over... We're out!
We're out!
...We're out?
We're out!
Tani gulped down the fresh air outside the tunnel, and suddenly the pocket watch came to mind again.
If she could have opened up a path with the watch, the way Grandma did, would she have been spared all this scrambling?
Probably. Most likely so.
But here and now, even without a pocket watch, she had gotten someone out—she had done the same thing Grandma did.
Did that make her half as amazing as Grandma already...
...or a quarter?
Today was so embarrassing. My arm wasn't even hurt that badly, but I was scared out of my wits and caused you all this trouble...
They told me you actually came looking for me to ask about your grandmother, back in the day. Sigh—here's what really happened...
Things inside Solar Valley weren't very harmonious then. The family heads spoke up about it, but everyone still fought over the extraction rights to the good veins, openly and behind closed doors.

At the time I was following my mom to the canteen for a meal, and partway there the mining area looked interesting. I loved digging holes, so while the adults were talking I snuck over and dug myself a hole to play in...
That's way too dangerous—
Pff. You went down a shaft by yourself. You've got some nerve saying that.
Heheh.
Anyway, once I was down there I dug deeper and deeper, and by the time I came to my senses and noticed how hungry I was, I had no idea where I was.
My mom told me it was Miss Inara who heard my stomping, thought something was off, and pulled me out by herself without asking anyone's permission.
She was a very powerful caster. Since it was urgent, she used Originium Arts to open a shortcut down the shaft.
That caused such a stir, and it involved the safety of a worker's family, so it eventually drew the compliance department down from above.
As a result, both sides fighting over the vein came to hate Miss Inara—each of them thought the other had sent her to cause trouble.
Especially after headquarters discovered they really would stop at nothing... falsified records, brawls...
Solar Valley's people noticed I was trapped not long after it happened. By rights it shouldn't have come down to waiting for Miss Inara to rescue me.
But they were all shoving the blame onto each other, trying to dress my accident up as the other side's fault to win the extraction rights, and that cost time...
So in the end nobody got the extraction rights!
Ah... So that's how it was...
So it really was just me playing around and trapping myself... Sigh. Embarrassing.
Not at all! I did plenty of embarrassing things when I was little. The first time I went for a soak I was so excited that I kept stomping, and I broke the drain—nobody in the family got to bathe.
Haha...
Come to think of it, even though I don't have my grandma's amazing Originium Arts—
—Oh, that's right! Miss, did my grandma leave anything behind in Solar Valley?
Something she left behind? Miss Inara did leave one thing...
Tani's eyes lit up.
Really? What is it?!
This, right here.
The technician patted the enormous power drill on her back.
My lucky power drill! Miss Inara didn't take it with her, and she never came back for it, so I ended up using it!
To handle this drill properly, I trained my arm muscles for ages!
Miss Inara said back then that digging a tunnel that long at my age was impressive, and that I'd surely grow up to be someone amazing at digging!
She wasn't wrong, was she!
We're done talking! I still haven't found Grandma's Arts Unit, but I know now that she wasn't the "villain" those people made her out to be!
Huh, your grandmother's not a villain? What are you two talking about?
Right—we've been busy all day and this is the first chance we've had to talk!
I'm exhausted... Oh, it's nighttime already!
With the sun no longer shining on it, the Rim Billiton night turned cold all at once.
A gust of wind blew through, and Jacinta couldn't help shivering.
Ngh...
Cold? Come here, come here, let's huddle up—a Cautus's favorite way to stay warm!
Me too, me too...
Wow, look at that—
Angelina pointed down below the deck.
Night had fallen, and yet the mining district only grew brighter, as if a sun really were about to rise. The girls clung together and shouted with excitement.
I'm so happy, so happy! We did something big together today!
I brought someone out, and Amy fixed the tower!
Mm-hm!
Honestly, though, Amy's more amazing. Without her I might have ended up crying in the tunnel waiting for someone to rescue me.
No, no... I'm not that amazing...
You clearly are!
While they were talking, patch after patch of light came on in the darkness, and before long the whole mining district was lit up.
Mr. Barton told me that thanks to the long-range comms system being fixed, starting tomorrow they can run a large-scale inspection of all the problems and hazards in the district.
Then the lights right now are for...?
Um, maybe a test run? Or maybe they just want to celebrate?
Mm...
What you do is genuinely amazing.
Y-yes... I think so too... Letting people who are far apart talk to each other... is an amazing thing.
Don't talk about it like it's someone else's business. You're the one who developed it, aren't you?
...Mm. That's true.
Once you've fixed all these towers for Meridian Red Earth, what are your plans?
I only wanted to go home and see Mom and Dad at first, but now I feel like... I don't want the journey to end in Big Ironton.
Angie, can I go to the Far South with you and Tani?
The night was deep, and yet Jacinta's eyes were shining.
I heard about the Far South on the road. I want to go see it.
But...
Angie, when you decided to go to the Far South, Miss Peta tried to talk you out of it too. You didn't listen either, did you?
Something like that happened?
...It's true that going to the Far South is a responsibility I chose to take on. But you're all different—none of you did anything wrong...
So we can't go to the Far South unless we've done something wrong?
Think about it. Jacinta helped Amy solve the comms tower problem, you helped me save someone, and I confirmed my grandma's story... We work really well together!
We'll be your support, not an obstacle!
Exactly! Think of Tani, think of Amy! Amy's skills are sure to help everyone—
Er, sorry, Amy. I'm not trying to force you to go to the Far South...
No, I-I want to go to the Far South too!
Amy?
Once... once I've fixed the rest of those towers... I won't owe the company a thing!
They—they treated me so badly, and I don't want to work for them anymore... I want to go to the Far South and test my technology!
The truth is, I didn't just bring replacement comms cores—I brought a miniaturized portable comms station too!
If my technology can transmit data reliably even with that dangerous zone between the Far South and Big Ironton in the way, then I...
Then I could leave the company behind entirely... and do it on my own!
...Exactly!
Amy, in Mr. Barton's office, I remember you said you had a dream—
Y-yes...
To use my technology... to connect this whole land... all of Terra!
Jacinta was so moved that she threw her arms around Amelia.
Amelia, I'm so happy for you... truly!
That company that only knows how to pass the buck can go to blazes! Our Amy is the one who's going to connect this whole land!
Y-yes! I'm going to connect this whole land, and I... I want you, I want all of you, to come with me to the Far South and see my dream through!
Angie... how do you feel about it now?
Then it's settled... we all go to the Far South?
We're all going to the Far South!
What do you mean... What do you mean they're starting a cricket match tonight to celebrate the long-range comms being fixed?
I only just got hold of my clients. I was planning to head out tonight and do business now that comms are back. Now I'll have to move it up even further, and dodge all these cricket-obsessed—
Time for pre-match training, come on, come on!
You did quite well last time! A few more sets of practice and you'll make real progress!
Owwww, owwww, my injuries from getting hit by that car...
Mr. Barton says you're completely healed! Weren't you running around helping while that girl was rescuing someone? Let's go!
This is exactly why I hate coming back to headquarters!!!
Ladies, so this is where you were!
The heroes who fixed our long-range comms and rescued our technician! We'd like to sincerely invite you to join our cricket tournament—what do you say?
Our team is still a few players short!
Join us, join us!
We've just been waiting for you to bowl the first ball!
Haha, let's go, all of us! Who knows, maybe we'll take first place!
Th-that's a fast delivery?!
Waaah! I can't run that fast, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!
Eep! Wh-wh-wh-where did that ball come from? It nearly hit my nose!
Using Originium Arts on the pitch... probably isn't very sporting, is it?
Match over!
Ugh...
What's wrong, Jacinta? We left Solar Valley days ago and you're still upset about not winning the cricket tournament?
I've never missed a single broadcast of a cricket grand tournament, and I even hold a certificate in cricket coaching! And we couldn't beat a few amateurs using cricket to get out of work...
M-maybe it's because those Solar Valley employees really, really didn't want to work...
Or maybe it's because you were the wicketkeeper and didn't move a single step from in front of the stumps.
That's because the wind on the pitch was too strong and I had to mind my skirt—
What Tani means is that fourth place is actually quite good for us.
Exactly. When you froze up on the pitch, I was worried you might be feeling ill... Now that I know you were only maintaining your usual "ladylike composure," I'm relieved!
Er, right...
Krrsh... krrsh...
Ah, we're picking up the disordered signal from a comms tower. We must be quite close to the destination now.
Here...?
The wind howled.
They tried to spot some trace of a comms tower out in the wastes with their own eyes, but all that met them were enormous Originium crystal clusters piercing the earth.
There's nothing here... Could something be wrong with my signal emitters?
I don't think it's the "Little Bugs."
I remember you telling us on the road that when Meridian Red Earth built the comms towers, they accounted for Rim Billiton's geography and used a special design in disaster-prone areas?
Ah, yes...! To avoid the effects of Catastrophes, comms towers can also be built below the surface. As long as they're fitted with signal boosting equipment, they run normally.
In that case, going by the strength of the disordered signal the "Little Bugs" picked up, plus the bearing the map gives, the comms tower must be located—
Over there.
An unremarkable little town came to rest at the Vulpo's fingertip.
The wreckage of buildings lay all around it. It might once have been one town among a cluster of them, but now it alone remained, caked in sand, standing isolated in the wastes.
"Redsand"... The comms tower is most likely there.
But the town doesn't seem to show any sign of residents moving around. How did you find it so quickly, Angie?
I came here once with other Rhodes Island Operators, and we traded supplies with the townspeople. That was... more than half a year ago now.
But Redsand was quite lively back then. How could it—
Krrsh... follow... me... krrsh...
...What Originium brings... krrsh... is death...?
...No... krrsh... it is happiness... it is... eternal life...
Someone is transmitting a signal... speaking through the "Little Bugs"?
Hm, judging by the dust on the shelves, Redsand's residents may have moved out only recently.
Moved out... So there really isn't a single person here? Then who was making that transmission just now? Don't tell me...
Boo hoo, o honored ghost, I didn't overhear your whispering on purpose, please forgive me, boo hoo...
Tani, stop scaring Amy.
If the "Little Bugs" really can pick up what ghosts say, wouldn't that give you even more to stand on when you strike out from the company?
"The bridge of communication between the afterlife and this world"—I could put together an entire promotional campaign for you!
The afterlife and this world... Friends, do you too wish to pursue happiness?
Who's there?!
Ma'am, are you a resident here? We've come to repair long-range comms. Do you know where Redsand's comms tower—
Child, is that an Originium crystal on your wrist?
It is. I'm Infected, but we're only here to fix the comms tower and we'll be leaving soon—
...Does it hurt?
Huh?
It's—it's all right. It doesn't hurt often, and there's medicine, so it's not so bad.
Medicine... How could medicine ever solve our problem?
Are you... Infected too, ma'am?
Rather than call us Infected, it's better to say... we are the ones Originium has chosen.
Child, you don't have to force yourself to act as though nothing is wrong. Becoming Infected has its own meaning for us. I hope you can understand that.
But being infected means having a very serious illness. What meaning could there be in getting sick?
Would you be willing to hear me out, just for a moment?
Um... j-just a moment, please!
(Quietly) I only half understand what this lady is saying...
(Quietly) If you ask me, she's trying to sweet-talk you into some dangerous group. I have experience with this sort of thing.
(Quietly) She looks quite elderly. I hope she hasn't been taken in by someone... Angie, you're a Messenger, you've seen a lot. Do you know what's going on with her?
...Krrsh... follow me... krrsh...
...Originium... Catastrophe... seek it...
The ghost is talking again!
It isn't a ghost. That is the voice of the Guide.
She appeared in this empty town, waiting for us to arrive, and gave us direction. Because she exists, I believe I have come very, very close to eternal happiness...
Ma'am... are you serious?
Of course I'm serious... Child, you're Infected too. You ought to be able to understand us.
Then have you heard the name "Hierda"?
So you've heard the Wayfarer's name as well... Wonderful, truly wonderful. Coming to Redsand really was the right choice.
Have you seen her? Can you tell me what she looks like? If we could meet her even once, might we all receive true salvation?
(Quietly) ...Tani, wait here for me. There's very likely danger ahead, and I don't want to drag you into it—
But if there really is a shortcut to happiness, my friends and I would rather like to see what it looks like.
Tani?
Ma'am, please take us to see this Guide.
Tani, that's very dangerous!
Do you think I can't tell you want to help these people who might have been deceived?
Don't tell me your plan was... to send us away and then handle everything alone? Now that would be dangerous.
Besides, the lady really does seem rather pitiable, and she doesn't look like she means any harm.
That's right, and besides...
And besides, the gh-ghost lady seems to have hooked into the town broadcast system.
I looked at Redsand's wiring. Broadcast equipment and comms towers work on different principles, but the cable routes are basically the same, so maybe—
So maybe once we meet this "Guide" who's been frightening everyone over the radio, we can help these Infected and find the comms tower at the same time. Several birds, one stone.
If it really were just a fraud ring, I wouldn't be this worried.
Lately a group of believers has appeared all over Terra. They believe Originium can bring eternal life, and that having Oripathy means you need not suffer anymore.
They regard a Cautus named Hierda as their savior, and believe that miracles occur wherever she goes—that Oripathy sufferers she "blesses" feel no more pain.
And her starting point was Rim Billiton.
So this "Guide" we're about to meet...
That lady just now clearly hasn't met Hierda in person, but this "Guide" may be closely connected to her. We can't let our guard down for a moment.
None of us is a professional combatant. If anything goes wrong, don't push yourselves. Keeping yourselves safe and away from danger comes first.
(Gulps)
Newly joined friends, are you looking for the Guide?
We are.
She is preaching on the engineering platform. There, that way.
Angelina and the others looked where the Infected was pointing.
The underground cavern was lit by only a few mining lamps, and behind the engineering platform stood a comms tower of unusual shape.

A dozen or so Infected were gathered below the platform, looking up at the person seated on the scaffolding. With the light behind her, Angelina couldn't make out her features at first, and she gripped her staff without thinking.
Then the Guide rose to her feet, and they heard the voice that had come through the signal emitters and the broadcast—
It was you who found me.
In an empty city nobody cared for, you raised steel and cable for my sake, and let my voice ring out here once more, day and night alike.
Half a year ago I was driven out to seek a new promised land alone. Once my voice was hated and belittled. Now you call it gospel.
O devout and kindly friends, I have no way to repay you. I can only light the way.
Follow me, and I shall lead you to happiness.
(Quietly) Nice atmosphere. Rowan, cue up the next song for me.
Yes.
Miss Uluru, the newly joined friends have arrived.
U-Uluru? The Guide's name is Uluru?
(Quietly) What a cute name.
(Nods hard)
Didn't I say no more pulling Infected in off the road!
But you said pursuing happiness is a beautiful idea. Shouldn't we be bringing more Infected into our ranks, then?
Our suffering will be taken from us soon, and we will go to an eternally peaceful Originium Realm.
The Originium Realm... the Originium Realm... Could you please forget all that hearsay?
What have I been saying on the broadcast? If you're convinced I'm the "Guide," then leave this place with me!
Sorry for neglecting you all. So you want to pursue happiness too?
Yes, I—
I'm Infected as well. I'd like to know what the shortcut to happiness is, and what it feels like to no longer be tormented by spreading crystals.
Er, I can't promise your condition won't get worse...
So all I get is a false calm—enduring the pain of my illness with hopes for the next life, with no medical treatment at all?
Er...
The Infected, displeasure on their faces, closed in around them.
I-I nearly forgot. You're all new here, so you haven't received your "Happiness Packs" yet, have you?
"Happiness Packs"?
Rowan, take them, would you? Be friendly about it.
As for this young lady—
I'm Angelina.
Angelina, that was a very good question. Once you've got your Happiness Pack, come with me and I'll answer every one of them.
And inside the "Happiness Pack" is...
A dozen fowlbeast eggs, two bags of dried cactus, eight unmatched socks, and one copy of A Guide to Warming Up...
This is just handing out supplies to the Infected.
That's wonderful—Miss Uluru isn't a ghost or a bad person. As long as she agrees to help, Redsand's comms tower can be fixed in no time!
Maybe so, but...
Jacinta found herself looking toward one corner of Redsand, where quite a few Infected had clustered.

They were gnawing on the dried cactus from the Happiness Packs, brows furrowed. Whether the cactus was setting their teeth on edge or they were using it to endure the spread of the crystals, there was no telling.
No wonder we saw almost no sign of anyone moving outside the town—most of the Infected are sitting in this corner. It's almost as if...
There's no "as if." They're gladly welcoming their own deaths.
I asked Angie for some medicine just now and tried to give it to that Infected named Rowan, but he wouldn't take it. He asked me why I wanted to push him away from the happiness of eternal life.
Only the dead can know whether people really go somewhere else after death. And even if they do, that place isn't necessarily better than reality.
Why not treasure the time you have, instead of believing a story like that?
That's... not so hard to understand, though.
Jacinta?
Some of them are already very ill. Originium crystals may have spread into every joint in their bodies, so even breathing causes agony.
For a patient like that, what difference is there between a story and reality?
Being able to say a dignified farewell is happiness enough.
Miss Guide, you've come at just the right time. You still haven't answered my question—
That's not difficult. Come outside the town with me and I'll tell you every answer. Your companions can come along too—
No, they'll stay here.
...Angelina?
I'll be fine. The Infected here are all in serious condition, so if you can help them, please help as much as you can.
Phew. This is the outskirts of Redsand. The Infected almost never come out this far.
Miss Guide...
No, no, no. There's nobody else here, so don't call me that—it's mortifying.
That title was given to me by my listeners—ah, I mean by that group of Infected.

I did want to do something a bit avant-garde, an experimental radio show. But a host called "the Guide" is far too strange. I can't imagine what sort of weirdos would subscribe to a channel like that...
Although... maybe it'd actually take off that way?
Er, Uluru?
Don't—don't look at me like that.
These listeners only care for the theory of Originium immortality. Nothing else gets through. If I hadn't pulled you away just now, they'd have surrounded you in silence until you apologized.
Oh, and what do you think of calling my show "Before Terra Ends"? Does it land? Would you subscribe?
...If you're willing to tell me the whole story of how you became the Guide, I promise I'll subscribe once the comms tower is fixed.
Yes! That makes you my twenty-third fan!
First off, I'm not the organizer of that group of Infected—I'm a podcaster.
Redsand is my hometown. Before long-range comms technology, all I could do was talk to people on the town radio station, and even then they complained I was too loud...
They said part of my ear was missing from birth, which affected my hearing, so I have no idea how loud my own voice is.
Ridiculous! Is my voice loud? Is my voice loud?!
Voice loud... loud... oud... ud...
Ahem. You were saying?
About half a year ago the townspeople complained about my show again, so I left in a huff and didn't come back until a week ago...
"In case your conscience actually catches up with you in the meantime and you suddenly feel like coming home to see me and your father."

"To escape the Catastrophe, Redsand's people and most of the town's facilities have moved onto a nomadic platform—except that broadcast station you love... oh, and the broken comms tower underground."

"There's a platform identification code on the back of this letter. A Catastrophe Messenger will show you the way. You can also keep being a podcaster out in the wastes—we were a bit rushed moving, so your room hasn't been cleared out yet."
"Sigh. Then again, you'll probably never see this note. It would be nice if we could see each other once before the Catastrophe arrives.—From a mother who misses you a little"
Misses me a little...
"There are still some supplies left over from the general store in the warehouse. Take them and use them. Take care of yourself."
I left without a word back then, and you still set aside precious supplies for a child who might never come home... "Miss you a little" is obviously the opposite of what she meant—
Unmatched socks? Sour dried cactus nobody will buy? A Guide to Warming Up?
What am I supposed to do with any of this!
(Residents who haven't evacuated? No—they look like Infected from somewhere else...)
Everyone, are you here visiting family or sightseeing? The Catastrophe will arrive in a few weeks, and Redsand's people have already moved away.
Redsand... a small town on the Catastrophe's predicted path... Thank goodness, we haven't come to the wrong place.
What a lovely voice, miss. Are you the Guide Hierda arranged for us, waiting here especially for our arrival?
You... you like my voice! I have to tell those people in town who complained about me—
Hold on, you knew the Catastrophe forecast and still came here? Then isn't that the same as...
...Seeking death.
At first I only wanted to talk some of them into leaving. I could actually have taken them to Redsand on the nomadic platform to settle in.
I told them there are many ways to make yourself happy, and I even recorded my segments and had the station play them on loop, day and night—
Er, maybe it's because nobody maintained the loudspeakers after you left Redsand, so your segments sound terrifying...
I really was out of options!

The Catastrophe is almost here, and every so often they bring back a few more Infected who also want to "pursue happiness." The group keeps getting bigger. Luckily the ones they intercepted this time were you.
But how can we get them to abandon—or even just briefly forget—the idea that only death brings happiness?
What happiness is there once you're dead?
That's exactly the tricky part.
Angie, we talked with those people just now. They all believe dying is happier than living, and we couldn't say a thing...
Just looking at those Originium crystals tells you how much pain they're in. And that lady was still willing to worry about me... She's really a very good person.
But the Rhodes Island office can provide medicine. They never had to be in that much pain.
...The ones who join them are either completely alone, or people their families cast off as a burden.
Rhodes Island can provide medicine at a price they can afford.
They don't believe that anymore.
After they got sick, the only people they met were swindlers or traffickers, and the family who should have stood between them and those people... were all gone.
As for the power this Hierda of theirs displays, it doesn't seem to be pure invention either.
They say there really was someone in Rim Billiton who received her blessing, died without any pain at all, and even saw something called the "Originium Realm"...
Whatever the truth about this Hierda, she isn't here, and there's no way any of them can die peacefully!
It's all my fault. If only I could have come up with some other way...
No. You were at least willing to give them supplies. Whoever's to blame, it isn't you.
All we need is a way—a way to tell them that death isn't something kind...
A funeral.
A funeral?
Angie, I don't think we can talk them out of it. Uluru has been talking in their ears for so long already.
So you want us to stand in for their families and do what their families should have done?
But wouldn't that amount to... standing by while they die?
No. I don't mean handling their affairs after death—I mean having them attend their own funerals while they're still alive, and say the last things they want to say.
Attend their own funerals...
Think about it. Funerals are held surrounded by family, aren't they? But these people left the ones closest to them to chase after some "eternal life" and "happiness."
Those delusions let them selectively forget the fear of death, forget the loneliness of having nobody to mourn them...
All they can do is... lie.
Lie to their fellow travelers and lie to themselves. They clearly want to blame something, to hold on to something, but they stay silent to keep up the act of having accepted death.
I think Jacinta's idea makes sense. As the Catastrophe gets closer, those Infected really have stopped bringing up their pasts. Now that I think about it, they're probably afraid of—
Regret.
It's a method worth trying.
Better than having the illusion punctured by the Catastrophe and dying in despair. While they can still move... let them do something they want to do, even if it's cursing someone out.
Thank you, Jacinta. If those stubborn Infected can face what's in their hearts at this unusual funeral, maybe we can save them.
Face what's in their hearts, hm...
Jacinta, what's wrong? Did we misunderstand your suggestion?
No, Angie is completely right. We should start preparing as soon as we can.
(Under her breath) It's just... I probably need to get ready to face what's in my own heart, too, and soon...
I can arrange the venue, and I'll notify the Infected.
It's just that most of them are very withdrawn. Even in the form of last words, it may be hard to get them to speak up and look back on their lives.
If someone could set an example, or move them with real tears...
Tears? Hmm...
Hmm...
Hmm...
Huh, why are you all looking at me?
This is the first time I've left home since contracting Oripathy.
When my grandma was alive, I was always pestering her for stories of every kind, telling her that when I grew up I wanted to be a pathfinder like her.
Grandma gave me a glowing bracelet. She said a pathfinder has to be able to find her way even at night, and that this bracelet would light my road for me.
But now, what's on my wrist is an Oripathy monitoring band...
I believe Originium can lead us to the far shore of happiness. At least there, maybe I can tell Grandma I'm sorry, that I let her down, that I never became a pathfinder...
Ta... Tani... don't... um...
(Quietly) Louder—keep going with the lines!
Ah! Tani! Don't ever say that! Think how sad it would make me, your friend!
You can still make your dream come true! Without you, I'd still be stuck up on that carrot rack in Artichoke Village! Without you... um...
(Quietly) "Your parents would be heartbroken too."
Your parents would be heartbroken too!
(Quietly) Amy, squeeze out a few tears!
I... (Quietly) I can't cry...
(Quietly) I'll slip you a bottle of spicy bottletree powder later—that'll bring on the tears. Tani, keep going!
R-right... And my parents too.
When I think of them, and of my favorite uncle, right now they must be... must be...
...When I think of them at this hour chewing salted dried turnip while watching a cricket broadcast, I can't keep acting!
Ahem... So, our two audience members—how was the overall effect?
They'd see right through it?
They'd see right through it.
We're doomed.
I'm sorry! It's all because I couldn't cry...
No, no, Amy, please don't blame yourself. Having you and Tani stir up the Infected's emotions really was a poor plan. I'm sorry...
You don't have to apologize to us, Angie. Amy and I want to talk those Infected out of dying too.
Some of them have conditions about like mine—not that serious... If I get to choose to do what I want to do, I'd like them to have that too.
Mm. I'm sure that among the Infected chasing the Catastrophe, there are people who miss the lives they used to have, or who still have regrets.
Here they come.
Some twenty-odd Infected came out into the wastes to attend their own living funerals.
It hadn't taken Uluru much persuading to bring them along.
All afternoon, the Infected had been picking out bottletrees on the barrens.
They felled the one that was closest to the right size, hollowed out the soft, porous core, and left the curved shell—
This was the coffin they would all share.
Miss Uluru, everyone's here.
Good.
As the Guide, I shall preside over tonight's funeral. Friends, you have come from all over Terra, walking this land in silence, to reach the source of the legend—Rim Billiton.

Before long the Catastrophe will exercise its generosity and its justice, and lead us to the golden homeland of eternal happiness. Tonight's funeral is also a farewell—a farewell to the selves who suffered misfortune in this world.
Every word will remain on these barrens and become food for the pouched musbeasts, and the kin beside you will keep your secrets too.
Now, the first of the departed...
The Infected avoided the Guide's gaze awkwardly. They were hesitating; perhaps it really was too early to ask them to open their hearts.
She looked toward Angelina's group as if asking for help.
We...
(Gulps)
I'll go.
Jacinta?
Young lady, you're not Infected.
Jacinta, the way he's looking at you is frightening, don't...
It's all right, Amy.
Hmm... When I can't show you crystals on my skin and I don't have a diagnosis on me, how should I prove that I'm Infected?
The effects of acute suppressants on seriously ill Oripathy patients vary from person to person. If a high fever won't come down, try plunging into an ice bath—there's a chance it'll save your life.
Between powders and capsules I'm more used to powders. Capsules have fewer side effects but take far too long to work, especially the ones from that Columbian-funded outfit—
Though they'll have a new drug out soon. I took part in their phase three trial just last month.
If you still don't believe me, open my luggage. There's plenty in there you'd recognize—emergency medication and first-aid equipment.
Now, may I lie down in my grave? I need a little privacy to gather my feelings before I bare my heart.
How does Jacinta know so much that only the Infected would know?
Um... Jacinta has always known a lot. Maybe medicine is one of her interests too?
I suppose. That was close. If I'd been questioned like Jacinta was, I'd have just panicked and stomped my feet.
But what will she do next? If the Infected find out Jacinta lied to them, won't they hurt her...
They won't.
Why not?
Because...
It turned out the inside of a bottletree stump wasn't hard at all. Lying in it wasn't so different from a critical-care Oripathy bed at the sanatorium.
But there, you couldn't see a sky of stars like this.
Jacinta thought.
Where should I start...
Ah—actually, I should have died fifteen years ago.

Mom and Dad must have been devastated. Their precious daughter, just five years old, had the misfortune of contracting Oripathy. Even with someone watching over me day and night, they were afraid I wouldn't pull through.
The doctor said my infection was severe and I wouldn't last a month. Mom and Dad took me out to give me a few memories, and ended up frightening themselves badly along the way.
But I survived. Like a miracle. My family was overjoyed.
But a miracle is called a miracle precisely because it happens only once.
Over the next fifteen years I received eight critical condition notices. At first they'd drop their work to be with me, but later they seemed to get used to it all. Or rather, they got tired.
How many people can bear the strain of a loved one hanging between life and death again and again? I don't blame them.
Gradually, though, my outings and activities were strictly limited, and in the end I moved into a sanatorium far from home. It has everything I need, and I'm perfectly safe there.

At the sanatorium I learned cricket, driving, antique appraisal... and earned dozens of certificates. But I never put a single one into practice. All I ever met were instructors and specially hired examiners.
After I escaped the sanatorium, I did think—dying out on an empty stretch of wasteland would be fine. I could accept it. My life ought to end, and I won't become any happier.
But it was only when I lay down in this grave that I clearly realized I'm afraid.
I'm afraid of the crystals of the terminal stage tearing my body apart. I'm afraid of vanishing from this land without leaving any trace. I'm afraid my parents won't know I'm gone. And I'm afraid...
I'm afraid that even if they know I'm gone, even if everyone knows I'm gone, nobody will attend the funeral, and nobody will shed a tear for me.
I don't want to die alone.
The crowd listened in silence to the voice she barely kept steady, and watched in silence as she climbed out of the coffin.
Before Uluru could ask who would like to hold their funeral next, the Infected had formed a line in front of that small coffin.
One broke down sobbing before getting out the first line of the eulogy for himself.
One cursed the lover who had abandoned her, and in the end turned the blame on herself.
One recited a long string of names—his children, the ones he still wanted to remember on the far shore.
One tried to ruin the funeral, denouncing everyone's foolishness and degeneracy, and finally left when some of the others stopped him.
The ones who finished their eulogies and stayed to keep the other Infected company—they'll be willing to leave with me.
We can save at least two-thirds of them.
Yes...
I'm sorry. I didn't know Jacinta was Infected, and quite seriously ill by the look of it.
She only chose to be honest with us just now, too.
Honest... Then you'd guessed her condition?
I often deliver letters to critical patients in Rhodes Island's inpatient ward. I know the look on their faces.
But Amelia and Tani won't accept Jacinta hiding it so easily. She really should have told us more.
Not as someone hitching a ride—as a friend.
The funeral is over, and Uluru has gotten the people who wanted to leave with her settled. You three—
Looks like a pouched musbeast paid our tent a visit. Not one word out of any of you?
Um...
...I really am sorry.
At first I hid my condition only because I was afraid you wouldn't be willing to take me along. I'd escaped the sanatorium before, and the drivers wouldn't take me once they heard about my condition.
So you... have been living alone all this time in a sanatorium near Great Springs.
Mm. My parents come to see me a few times a year, and apart from that I only ever see doctors and that crowd of bodyguards in black. They say it's to protect me, but really it's to keep watch.
So the bodyguards we ran into at the town gate...
It was convalescence, not a holiday, but they really do form a human wall when I cross the street!
They actually do that?
They really do! My parents told them to "protect me in every direction," so they genuinely try to manage "every direction"...
All right. But if everything you said at the funeral is true, then being afraid to tell us at first is understandable...
But afterward we fixed the Solar Valley comms tower together and rescued a technician together. We should have been very good friends by then—so why didn't you tell us?
I looked in your luggage. It's all mid-to-late-stage Oripathy medication. If we'd known you were that ill, we would have—
But what I wanted wasn't the best treatment. It was a chance to go out and see things, a chance to be around other people.
Tani, you of all people understand why I made this choice, don't you?
By the time we reached Solar Valley I knew you were all good people. But once the moment passes, the words get harder to say...
You're going back to Big Ironton to go home?
Yes. I only hid my condition—I never lied to you about anything else.
The reason I escaped the sanatorium this time really was to go home and let my parents see me.
I don't want to be handled with kid gloves. I want to do what I truly want to do in the time I have left.
And I'm close to finding out what that truly is, so don't you dare leave me behind here.
Angie, after all that Jacinta just said...
I was never angry with her to begin with.
The friend Jacinta really needs to comfort is this one, isn't it?
Um... Amy, I'm sorry. But everything I promised you before was true!
I still fully support you leaving Meridian Red Earth to do the work you want to do, and I'm willing to invest in your long-range comms technology!
Aaah—right, the Far South too! Once I get back to Big Ironton and report in to my parents, I'll go with you to the Far South and test the equipment.
I have to see the first technical talent I've invested in take that decisive step with my own eyes, I—
The Anaty flung herself at the pale-haired Cautus all at once.
Amelia's fluffy head pressed against Jacinta's chin, and her tightly wrapped arms squeezed hard enough to hurt.
But before Jacinta could complain, as usual, about her dress being wrinkled, she felt the damp spreading on it.
But, but saying all that doesn't help! You're dying, Jacinta!
Actually, actually not quite that soon—
Why did you have to get Oripathy? Why does someone as good as you have to disappear?!
When I think that one day you'll be gone from this land completely and I'll never be able to find you again, I feel so sad...
What am I supposed to do without you—no, what are the thousands upon thousands of timid, bullied people like me supposed to do?! They'll never get the chance to meet you!
I-I can't possibly help every single person, can I?
Waaah—! This land isn't going to get any better! In my heart it won't, at least!
Amy, you're being completely unreasonable! You're a year older than me—why are you crying like a child...

I'm afraid that even if they know I'm gone, even if everyone knows I'm gone, nobody will attend the funeral, and nobody will shed a tear for me.
I don't want to die alone.

lines.x: Pff... It seems there will be someone to cry for me after all—and enough tears for several people, at that...
What... (Sniffles) ...what are you saying... Huh, why are you laughing...
Because... you've cried yourself all wrinkly, like dried cactus.
Really?! Angie, Tani, quick, take a look! I don't want to be dried cactus!
Krrsh—krrsh—beep!
Mm... Testing complete. Miss Uluru and some of the Infected helped out, so repairing the comms tower went very smoothly. However...
Not all of the Infected decided to leave with Uluru. Some of them are still waiting for the Catastrophe.
Bottletree remains were scattered across the barrens, and several Infected were at work.
Perhaps what yesterday's funeral gave them of the most value was learning how to make a coffin.
Those who had prepared their "resting place" in advance lay down inside the shells, staring straight at the sun, neither drinking nor eating.
They might well die of dehydration before the Catastrophe ever arrived.
(Mouthing) What's wrong with Angie...
(Mouthing) No idea.
...Angie.
Hm?
I wasn't going to ask. Everyone has things they'd rather not talk about. But you look so sad, Angie.
You found Redsand faster than I did with a map in my hands, and you said you came here with Rhodes Island Operators to trade supplies.
And ever since we entered the town, you've been so wary of those Infected who follow Originium immortalism, as if you know something about it...
Did something happen around here?
Before I worry so much that I start stomping every day—would you share your story with us?
If you really don't want to talk about it, that's fine too! I'll try hard to hold it in...
...I just don't feel I'm ready to face it yet.
But this day was always going to come. When I decided to follow Route Zero to the Far South, I'd already made up my mind... I have to go back and look.
Go back? You mean...?
Rhodes Island. The home I used to have.
So your home now... isn't there anymore?
...We have a new Rhodes Island, but the one I know better truly can't house anyone anymore.
I asked the Infected who would talk to me, and Rhodes Island's remains are not far from here. They've been treating it as a kind of "holy site."
At one point they wanted to go there to die, but Uluru talked them out of it, and they no longer had the strength to trek that far, so it was dropped.
So that's what happened...
The person who told me all this asked me to wait a bit longer outside the town. He hopes the ones who believe so completely might still change their minds. I agreed. That's my hope too.
So, to pass the time, let's go see Rhodes Island's remains first.
And if they still haven't come out when we get back...?
Get in the car first.

lines.st: The scenery of the barrens always feels like something you've seen before. Scattered bottletrees, dry, burning sand, small whirlwinds close to the ground, and enormous black crystal clusters...
Angelina remembered that when she left Rhodes Island a little over a year ago, this was not the road she took.
She knew that was because, after she left, Rhodes Island had traveled a long way farther toward the Targangils Prime Vein.
But she couldn't stop herself from remembering how it had been when she left.

There had been Rhodes Island patients beside her then, and other Operators too. Nobody said a word; the only sound in the car was a small patient playing with a pendant bearing the Rhodes Island emblem, clinking it again and again...
Had she cried?
Before she could remember whether she had shed any tears—

lines.x: We're here.
Is that... a ship wrapped in Originium?
The Originium crystals were like thorns the earth had grown. They proliferated around the landship, standing like a merciless barrier.
Someone who didn't know better might be awed by the sight and sigh—
"That ship went through an unfortunate, terrible Catastrophe. I'm sorry for your loss."
But Angelina knew it hadn't been a Catastrophe.
This is the Rhodes Island landship, destroyed. The home I used to have.

lines.st: At first it was only a vague feeling—when I made a mistake in my Messenger work, when my Arts failed me, when I had something to say and couldn't get it out...
But that vague feeling soon turned into a piercing reality because of one thing, one thing I'm afraid I'll never be able to forget.
Rhodes Island was attacked, and the landship that held my memories and so many others' was destroyed. A deeply beloved doctor was gone, and to Rhodes Island's Doctor, she was someone very important.
Even now that Dr. Kal'tsit is back with us, I've wished countless times that I could return to the day I was told to leave Rhodes Island...
To choose to stay. To choose to stand beside the people who matter to me. To choose to do the things that wouldn't leave me with regrets.
I began training my Arts twice as hard, and still couldn't manage them with any ease. I worked twice as hard at my Messenger duties, and still made one small mistake after another.
There's so much I want to say, and I don't know how to begin... That question has been troubling me all this time.

How I wanted to convince myself that I'm just an ordinary patient and apprentice caster at Rhodes Island, just an unseasoned Messenger, and that the things I want to say are only the odd notions everyone has in their head.
But I clearly don't want that. I hate it. I feel like I could have done more, that I could fly higher than this...

lines.x: D-Dr. Warfarin!
Sit.
Yes!
No need to be so stiff. I ran your physical, so I've come to have a word with you.
Is it... are the results bad?
Quite the opposite. Your condition isn't too bad. As long as we intervene starting now, both survival time and quality of survival are assured.
Survival time... quality of survival?
Tch. Patients never react well to that terminology...

opts: She means you can go back to a normal life.

lines.x: And this is...?
Doctor? Weren't you in a meeting with Kal'tsit and the others?

opts: Now you have to come to the meeting too.
We need your opinion right now.

lines.x: Fine, fine. Let me see who in Medical has a free moment—whoever's free can brief the patient—
Tch. All busy...
I'm fine, really! Knowing I can go back to a normal life beats everything else!
Well, that's true. Cheer up. Mental state matters.
Your infection isn't especially deep, yet your symptoms are fairly pronounced. That's actually not a bad thing—it means your immune system is at least still doing its job.
Controlling symptoms is simpler than stopping the infection from deepening, and stopping the infection from deepening is far simpler than reversing the degree of infection.
Only when we develop a drug that can reverse the fusion of somatic cells with Originium will we truly have a proper weapon against Oripathy.
So that day comes sooner, can I... help?
Whether you can is usually up to Personnel, but since the Doctor is right here—Doctor, what do you think?

opts: Rhodes Island welcomes anyone who shares our goals.
Last time I saw her, her condition was stable.

lines.x: I was rushing off to the meeting. I finished the briefing per protocol, but I didn't stress the issue of Oripathy patients using Arts enough...

The patient had no idea what could happen if an Infected uses Arts. She volunteered to help move something, and in the end... what she activated wasn't her Arts Unit but the Originium inside her own body.
It's happened to her many times before, but it never erupted—until just now...
...This is on me.

opts: ...No, I was the one rushing you. We're both responsible.
