lines.x: Now is not the time to compete over who takes the blame.
Dr. Kal'tsit...
To prevent this from happening again, Medical will strictly assess the completion of patient briefings from now on.
...Understood.
In addition, I need you to assess the patient's prognosis.
The short-term prognosis is poor. The Originium in her body is highly active. The degree of assimilation is relatively mild, but the slightest slip...

opts: You're saying that if she gets through this, she can recover?

lines.x: That's right.
You're hinting at the new suppressant we're discussing in the meeting.
I know you've poured a great deal of effort into developing that drug and have high hopes for it, but its clinical effects still require further confirmation.
Even if it works, it is only a new suppressant, not a miracle cure for Oripathy.
...I agree with your judgment, but our time can hardly be called sufficient.
Well, if the Doctor says so, I'll go tell the lab to prepare for overtime.

opts: I will make her well again—

lines.x: Doctor, step outside for a moment.
The sight of a patient lying in bed suffering from Oripathy is indeed pitiable.
But we must never use vague words to build a patient false hope out of thin air.
At first I didn't believe I could truly get better.
In school, I watched a classmate grow weaker by the day from illness. When word got out that he was Infected, the parents descended on the school in a fury, demanding answers.
And watching the chaos on campus back then, half irritated and half sorrowful, I thought: ah, Oripathy after all. No wonder he's weaker every day. There's only one place this can end...
...But I actually did get better.
A few days later, I was moved from the critical care ward to a general room in the inpatient center.
The crystals on my leg, which had been the tiniest patch before admission, had grown plainly visible, and I was told they would never recede again. But honestly, I didn't mind that much.
Because while I was hospitalized, I saw how people whose crystals grew in their throats lost their voices.

I saw how people whose crystals had reached deep into their bones lived in constant dread—ringing the call bell over and over even before the pain had begun, begging the staff, driven by fear, to save one shot of painkiller for them.
The new drug worked the same for everyone, and I was the luckiest of them all.
The day I moved from the ward to the dormitory, I still had a low fever and very little strength, but the staff who had cared for me held a small celebration for me anyway.
Dr. Warfarin came. Operator Medic came. Hibiscus, the trainee doctor who had looked after me, came. Even Dr. Kal'tsit made a brief appearance, though she left again quickly.
They said it was thanks to the Doctor that the new drug had made it out so smoothly.
So I kept waiting for the Doctor to appear so I could say thank you in person—but everyone dispersed and it never happened.
Half asleep, I suddenly remembered that scene in the critical care ward.
Ah. So that was it.
The Doctor really shouldn't have come.
The Doctor gave me unrealistic hope, and that unrealistic bit of hope had somehow become real. Luck like that probably comes only once in a lifetime.
So the Doctor was right not to come.
Just as I had convinced myself of that and decided to make peace with my headache and get to sleep, I suddenly heard a knock at the door.
Miss Angelina, I nearly forgot—candy for you.
Thank you...
It isn't from me, it's from the Doctor.
Procurement brought in a batch of new flavors, and the wrappers are lovely, so the Doctor handed some out to every patient in Medical.
Good thing I remembered you'd moved over here, or I'd have missed someone, heheh.
After Medic left, I peeled back the wrapper.
I can't recall the taste of the candy anymore.
All I remember is that, for some reason, after that day I picked up the habit of folding paper stars.
...See, you're completely in the clear!
Your symptoms have fully subsided and your infection has entered a stable phase. By the standards of us Infected, you're as good as recovered.
Apart from taking your medication on schedule and not using Arts on your own, Medical has no further restrictions for you. Want to arm wrestle to celebrate?
Pass.
Congratulations, Operator Angelina. Your Arts no longer disturb the active Originium in your body. In other words, from now on you may use Arts freely.
As for the parts of the test where you stumbled—gravity manipulation is indeed a rare Originium Art with great potential. It's normal to find it difficult.
Regarding your future training, I recommend consulting the following caster Operators...
That strong?!
No way, no way, no way. Exusiai, add another five kilos!
You do realize you're going up against her Originium Arts with brute strength, right?
Like I'd believe that—
Whoa!
Heheh, no matter, no matter. Next time a newbie shows up, I'll egg them on to a weightlifting contest with Angelina. Then I just put everything on Angelina...
Whew, safe landing.
Thanks to your Arts we cut out a lot of detours. Now we'll have plenty of time to reach the safe zone.
Hm? Barely keeping me from getting hurt isn't enough? You wish you could make the whole car fly?
Haha, nobody is born a master of Originium Arts. Relax, relax.
Judging by how familiar you are with the work, this isn't your first mission with a Catastrophe Messenger, is it?
Ah, Provence... no wonder you're so practiced. She's got a real sense of responsibility. On responsibility alone, she might even beat Ayers...
Have I not told you yet why Ayers stayed on the landship this time? Come, come, let me tell you. It all starts with the power outlet in his dorm room...

Doctors who put themselves in their patients' shoes, instructors who think of their trainees' needs first, friends who can laugh alongside you whether you're Infected or not, colleagues with wildly different temperaments and each with their own strengths...
I am Angelina the Messenger. A Messenger of Rhodes Island—Angelina Ajimu.
Just remembering that, even after threading through cold wind between buildings all night, I'd always keep a thread of warmth in my chest.
Rhodes Island really is a place that's almost too warm, I thought.
Rhodes Island was even willing to negotiate with a difficult family for the sake of one Messenger not yet qualified to forecast Catastrophes, one Operator still strictly in a trainee status...
What is it—nervous about going home after so long?
Of course I was.
I clutched that filled-up notebook—the one Lisa gave me—and couldn't speak for a long while.
Naive as I was, I wanted to put the letter explaining why I'd left home into our mailbox with my own hands, and yet I could never quite bring myself to face my parents.
It was the Doctor who pointed out that the two things didn't have to happen at once. Telling my family I was safe mattered more than anything.
I took the Doctor's advice, and my parents' reply came faster than I'd imagined...
No, I'm only regretting that I put this off for so long.
By the way, is the family difficult to deal with? Did Rhodes Island lose out at all, dealing with them?
Ah, rather than worry about that, you'd do better to think about what you'll say to your parents and how you'll spend these few days.
Look, there's a fruit stand over there. We Yanese always bring fruit when we visit our parents. How about buying something too?
I stood in front of the fruit stand thinking for a long time.
Grapes? Apples? Pomegranates? Figs? Olives?
Fruits full of auspicious meaning spread out before me like jewels, and still I couldn't decide.

What fruit could be sweet and sour, soft and coarse all at once—enough to stand for the haste of leaving, the desolation of searching, the glimmer of kindness, and the thrill of a reunion about to happen?
...In the end I picked up a plump lime.
I don't know what a lime is supposed to mean. I only noticed the faint scent of lime on my own lips, and remembered that the balm was the last thing I'd brought with me from home.
It's me. Mom and Dad will know—it is me. I'm home.
Yes. I was home.
I hid behind the door, not daring to look at my parents' faces, until I heard the low sob rolling in my mother's throat.
When I was first infected, that sound often echoed through the house once my mother thought I'd gone to sleep. The sound now was exactly the same, but the feeling it carried held nothing but...
the joy of reunion.
I cried, I laughed, and I poured out apologies and longing in a hopeless jumble.
I couldn't really make out what they were saying, but I knew we felt the same.
A reunion after long separation is more precious than any treasure in this world, and it was beating there in our chests...
...And all of it was so perfect that it wasn't even a dream.
And all of it...
wasn't a dream, and yet somehow the moment of waking came all the same.
So... I really can't opt out of field duty?
It's not that I don't understand how you feel, but this really is for the safety of every Operator.
You're one of the Messengers Rhodes Island trusts most. It's just... Rhodes Island does have a very thorny problem to deal with.
And if something really does happen, you'd be able to carry word immediately to wherever Rhodes Island needs it.
After something happens... you mean?
It's not that something's definitely going to happen! And... this really is about taking responsibility for your safety, nothing more. Don't take it to heart.
...Right.
Then... may I ask which Operators get to stay on Rhodes Island?
Let me think. Most important, of course, are the Operators who keep Rhodes Island's basic functions running.
The people I respect.
Elite Operators.
The people I look up to.
And then Kal'tsit, Warfarin, me...
The people I know full well I can't stand beside.
...That's about everyone, I think? This situation really is unusual. The landship going so quiet all at once—I'm not used to it either.
And the Doctor...
Mm, right, that one too, of course.
...Of course.
Look on the bright side—it's a chance for a change of scene. How about another trip home, or the office over in Siracusa?
No. I'm already happy that Rhodes Island let me spend that time with my family. This time...
...Please assign me wherever is closest to the landship.
But when word came that the Rhodes Island landship had been destroyed, there was nothing I could do.
All I could do was... make up for it.
To become one of the people who could stay, I worked twice as hard, hoping to control my unusual Originium Arts—the ones everyone had such hopes for, and that I could never quite stabilize.
So that disaster would not repeat itself, I took on more work of my own accord, hoping every letter I delivered might become some potential strength for Rhodes Island.
Did I manage it?
Perhaps.
Perhaps Angelina has become the most reliable Messenger, and no letter or parcel that passes through her hands ever goes astray.
Perhaps Angelina's Originium Arts have reached true mastery, and one light wave of her staff lets her handle gravity at will and set everything spinning around her.
Like right now—perhaps if Angelina gave it everything, she could invert the up and down, the light and heavy, of this whole town.

Perhaps she could pour cement into flesh, gather rebar into bone, push a beating Originium into its chest, bring this weathered town back to life and stand it up in the middle of the Rim Billiton barrens.
Perhaps she could have the town cradle those despairing people in its palm and carry them, even if they'd resolved to die, out of that forbidden zone about to be ravaged by the Catastrophe.
Perhaps afterward they too would recognize their own obstinacy, and would, like her, see a hand reaching toward them in their despair...
But that isn't now.
All the Angelina of now can do is stand outside Redsand and wait. And wait. Wait until even she herself despairs.
Angie... it's time to go.
I went with Jacinta to the entrance of Redsand just now. The Infected guarding the gate said a lot of very ugly things, and it nearly came to blows at the end.
At the very end he said... the Infected inside have already prepared weapons, and if we dare force our way in, they'll make us "atone" with our lives...
Uluru just left with the Infected who changed their minds. She was urging us to set off quickly too.
Angie...?
I bit my lip and looked at that town one last time, and the town answered me with silence.
A pouched... musbeast?
A pouched musbeast? It's already dangerous around here—where is it?
It flew too fast for my eyes to follow, but it must have gone south.
Thank you. Thank you for appearing here and stealing the words I was about to say, so I wouldn't break down sobbing in the car and worry my friends.
Tani took my hand, worried, and I walked to my car in silence.
This is rare. We've been driving on and off for over ten days since we left Redsand, and this is the first time you're all awake while I'm at the wheel.
I took shifts with you, you know.
Right, don't make us sound so heartless. Amelia and I set times to keep you company too...
It's just that it's very rare for everyone in the car to be awake at once.
Well, going by the distance on the map, we should be reaching Big Ironton soon. Jacinta, how does it feel to be home?
It's only a trip home. There's nothing for me to be nervous about.
Tani didn't say you were nervous. That's a confession if I ever heard one.
The last time I went home to Big Ironton was three years ago, and I don't remember the scenery along the way at all. I'm just a little curious!
You're the one to talk about, Amy. Meridian Red Earth's headquarters is in Big Ironton, isn't it?
Fixing the comms tower here amounts to showing your black-hearted employer who's who. Have you thought about how you'll bring up your resignation?
R-resignation...?

Yes, you said it yourself. And I support you resigning.
If you don't, who knows what else they'll do to you!
I-I'll explain things to them properly.

You have to watch out for their sweet talk. You're Meridian Red Earth's Engineering Director, their key technical staff. They'll know that when you bring up resigning, they'll offer you a high price to stay. Don't you dare give in!
(Quietly) If only that were how it went...
What was that?
N-nothing. If that's how it goes, I won't give in either!
Sigh. Looking at you all flustered like this, I can't help worrying... You're not too embarrassed to bring up quitting, are you?
Don't worry, I'll go see management with you!

No, no, no, really, there's no need! The truth is, I've already brought up resigning with management many times! I only stayed because I wanted so badly to keep developing long-range comms technology.
All right, then.
Amelia, Jacinta, look ahead.
We're here.
This is my first time in Big Ironton.
It's not a nice thing to say, but apart from Great Springs, isn't everywhere your first time?
Hmph, you can only tease me now. Once we get to the Far South, let's see who still calls me a little bunny who can't explore, can't leave home, and won't grow any taller!
The last one is a fact, though...
(Stomps anxiously)
Hm... The comms tower seems to be on the tallest "branch" in Big Ironton? It's certainly conspicuous.
Mm. When long-range comms first rolled out, the company deliberately chose the tallest platform in all of Big Ironton to boost publicity and its own influence.
There are staff assigned by the company guarding the entrance at the base of the platform, to keep anyone from stealing the technology...
They treat their own badly enough, but they certainly know how to put on a show.
Come on, let's go fix the tower.
We can't!
W-we can't go yet. I-I haven't applied to the company for repair authorization...
True. That's what dragged things out with Mr. Barton back in Solar Valley...
And you've seen how things are—I've already fallen out with the company...
But... but don't worry! Give me two days. I'll have the comms tower sorted by tomorrow evening, and then the morning after, we all set out together!
All right.
In that case I'll go home first too. It started out as going home, but now it's become reporting in to my parents, haha.
Before that, though, let's look over the route to the Far South. Once the comms tower is fixed, we'll be on the road right away.
Conditions on the stretch from Big Ironton to the Far South are complicated, and the weather is changeable. In this season we may run into fast-moving sandstorms carrying Originium dust.
Grandma told me about those. But doesn't the Originium concentration in the sandstorms on the Far South's outskirts drop during certain periods?
It does. Even if we're unlucky enough to hit a sandstorm, as long as we're in the window when active Originium concentration drops, our exposure to Originium dust will be far lower.
That still leaves one problem to solve, though—
...Navigation.
Exactly. A sandstorm blocks your view, and without long-range comms support it's easy to get lost—and easy to have an accident. That's also why so few people ever reach the Far South.
But we have Amy! As long as she can fix the comms tower within the window, everything will be fine.
What's the latest day we can set out?
According to the Big Ironton forecast, active Originium concentration will rise after the day after tomorrow. In other words, the window is these next few days.
Good! Once Amy settles things with her company and Jacinta reports in to her parents, we have to set out within three days.
All four of us together.
All four of us together!
...Together.
Right.
Then we meet back here tomorrow evening?
Mm... I'll be there!
Goodbye for now, then, friends.
It's gotten so quiet all of a sudden...
It has. But we'll see each other again soon.
Hm. The security downstairs still opens with my badge...
If I can just fix the comms tower in secret before anyone notices, I can... I can...
Make up for every mistake you've made, is that it?
M-Mr. Ashton?!
How many years have you been at the company? And still jumping at shadows.
Your absence has already exceeded your approved leave, Amelia. It will show up in your performance score—
Oh, no, wait. Your performance score has already been wiped out by "causing the Great Disconnect."
I-I'm sorry, Mr. Ashton...
It's genuinely hard for me to put in a good word for you with management.
The semi-automatic Originium-adaptive system is the product of Meridian Red Earth seizing an opportunity of its era.
After Ursus's veins ran dry, Originium demand outstripped supply, and Rim Billiton ramped up extraction enormously. For a long-range comms project, that was the perfect moment to expand.
The company poured huge funds into erecting comms towers and promoting the achievement, and we saw returns.
B-but I explained to you that the semi-automatic system greatly increases the chance of operators contracting Oripathy...
Yes. A girl with no backing, who contributed almost nothing of value to the semi-automatic system's development, suddenly popped up sniveling about safety issues.
N-no, that's not it. I realized that since the company had forced the stations' output up, the part the casters handle could also be addressed by corresponding means...
I don't understand the technical side as well as you do. All I know is that in Rim Billiton, energy is cheaper than people.
On top of that, the project we pushed has already drawn the attention of Columbia's Scientific Ethics Consensus Committee... Meridian's headquarters is in Trimounts, after all.
In any case, when you proposed the concept of the fully automatic Originium-adaptive system, the company gave you your chance. And the result?
Your solution was theoretically viable but insufficiently validated in implementation, and when it went into large-scale use it suffered a fatal fault, causing this Great Disconnect.
You cost the company an enormous sum. That the company didn't fire you on the spot is something you ought to be grateful for.
What? Did I say something wrong?
...No... but!
...I repaired three comms towers before the company's engineering crew got to them. The one above our heads is the fourth, and I'll fix it too. I can do it.
You can?
As I recall, your leave request said you were going to Great Springs to convalesce. That's where Rim Billiton's northernmost comms tower stands—and we still haven't received its signal.
Don't panic... don't panic... I can fix a comms tower by myself. How long have I practiced on my own?
Wait, no. This module has been modified. I can't wire the circuit the way I practiced!
I can't do this. There's no way I can do this... I'm just a junior employee who sits in an office. Why did I get worked up and go out to fix towers...
I'm finished...
There was a small accident while I was repairing the Great Springs comms tower...
Then how can you guarantee the three towers you fixed afterward weren't "accidents" too?
I can prove it... I'm leaving the company...
Striking out on your own, is it? Do you know how many employees come to me every month saying they can't stand the atmosphere here and want to start their own thing?
Want to guess how many of them end up begging me to take them back?
People who fail inside the company go on failing outside it. I thought you understood that, Amelia.
I interviewed you myself. I know your family background wasn't good, and that you got into university through your own effort.
I admired your perseverance, which is why I recommended you for the first-generation comms technology project.
I know perfectly well that you're a young person with potential and ambition. You could become someone who stands on her own—but you still have a long road ahead.
And standing on your own isn't as fine a thing as you imagine. On your little unauthorized tower-repairing trip, I'm sure you collected some praise. Did it feel good?
...I've never received any praise inside the company.
But have you considered this: if you told the truth—"I'm the one who broke this, and now I've fixed it"—would the people who benefited still be grateful?
They...
You're an employee of Meridian Red Earth. Isn't fixing towers your job? You're only making up for your own mistake. That hardly counts as a virtue.
But if you're content to be an ordinary screw in the company's machine and don't go near those people, you never have to show them your ugly side.
As long as the company makes no mistakes, you make no "mistakes." What's wrong with enjoying the benefits of the company's reputation forever?
Never making mistakes... never disappointing anyone?
Of course.
Wait, are you saying I can come back to the company, as if nothing happened?!
You'll receive the appropriate disciplinary measures, but the company won't dismiss you.
You're a technical talent we value. We're willing to make an exception—we'd even let you rejoin the second-generation long-range comms project team.
That was my technology to begin with...
If it's your technology, then you go and take responsibility for everything it caused.
The reason you slipped away was precisely because you knew how much economic damage the Great Disconnect would cause, and you wanted to quietly paper over it, wasn't it?
Say you really did fix a few towers. How do you intend to compensate for over two months of disconnection, and how will you explain it to our partners up and down the chain?
Have you got the compensation ready? Have you prepared what to say at the apology press conference? Have you worked out how the culprit behind the Great Disconnect is going to make a living?
But choose the right path now, and you won't have to carry any of it.
The new Engineering Director takes office shortly. Resolving the Great Disconnect caused by the technology upgrade will be his first assignment, and your job will be to "assist" him.
And this comms tower?
We need to prepare the promotional campaign for the second-generation technology, which will take at least a week. Repair work will begin once he takes office.
Your unauthorized repairs have already disrupted our original plan. Interfere any further and even I can't save your job. Understood?
Yes...
Now, go back to your desk. Nobody's going to finish the work you let pile up while you were on leave. Get to it.
Th-then shouldn't I organize the earlier materials and design drafts, so the handover to the new Engineering Director goes smoothly?
That's not your concern. We'll take care of it. You just do the work you owe us, like a good employee.
Rim Billiton's capital really is something else. Still this lively at this hour.
But after asking around this whole circuit, nobody's seen Grandma's pocket watch... We've been searching for over a day since we got into Big Ironton yesterday, and not a single lead.
We're leaving tomorrow morning. Does that mean I'll never...
At least Big Ironton isn't the end of our journey.
Right! The watch might be in the Far South! Achieving the feat of reaching the Far South alone—even someone as worldly as Grandma would have fumbled once or twice.
Let's talk about something else. Here, want some carrot pizza?
Carrot... sliced... on a pizza?
Yes. The guidebook says it's the hot new way to eat it. A local told me the owner trained in Siracusa, so the technique is absolutely authentic! Take a look.
..."Authentic" indeed.
Huh? The guidebook also says "Carrot pizza—the perfect gift for friends and family. Even enemies make up after a slice"...?
I-I did not buy it because of that slogan!
Still not planning to message home and tell them you're safe? Call it a test of Amy's comms tower repairs?
Not sending it, not sending it! The Great Springs tower hasn't been fixed, so even if I sent one they wouldn't get it.
Huh? Come to think of it, we met Amy in Artichoke Village, right? Artichoke Village isn't far from Great Springs, so why didn't she fix the Great Springs tower too?
I don't know. Maybe there was a technical reason...
Sorry I'm late.
You're not late, you're not late. Amy isn't here yet either.
How was it, Jacinta? Were your parents surprised and happy to see you home?
More or... less.
So tomorrow morning we can all head to the Far South together?
Jacinta, did something happen?
It's nothing! I already told Mom and Dad about going to the Far South. We'll set out together tomorrow.
Wonderful!
Hm, now it's only Amy who hasn't shown up. Could she have run into trouble fixing the tower?
If she's just running late because of the repairs, that's fine. But if the company's people have gotten hold of her...
Let's go find her at Meridian Red Earth.
If she's fine, it's a nice surprise for her. And if they really have gotten hold of her, we'll go back her up.
Heheh, I like that idea. Let's go!
So this is Meridian Red Earth... What a grand lobby...
Let's hope the money for it didn't come from squeezing pushover employees like Amy.
Ha... In a company this big, how are we supposed to find Amy's desk?
I remember Amy's title was Engineering Director...
How may I help you?
Hello. We're friends of Miss Amelia, the Engineering Director. Do you know how we can reach her?
The Engineering Director?
Do you mean the Engineering Director of the long-range comms department? He doesn't take office until next week, and as far as I know, he's a "mister."
He hasn't taken office? A mister?
All I know is that the long-range comms department did once have an Amelia, but she was an ordinary staff member. Her desk is in the cubicles on the tenth floor... assuming it's still there.
They demoted her?!
She can't stay here any longer... Let's take her with us. We'll leave for the Far South tonight!
Let's go!
You don't protect employee information?
Given this lady's seniority, her confidentiality level at the company isn't high.
Since you're here to see her, please register as visitors. Including the two who just went in.
Rewrite it.
I checked the data against the records. There's no issue with its accuracy...
This report isn't for me, it's for the Engineering Director. Whether the data is accurate doesn't matter to him.
It doesn't matter? But without this data, how is he going to repair the comms tower?
That's what you're for, isn't it? He's only here to lend his name and do a few promotional events, and then he'll be transferred up to higher management.
Don't worry, he won't interfere with our work.
But...
But your behavior right now is already interfering with Miss Amelia's work.

Jacinta, Angie, Tani... Goodness, what are you all doing here—
No, wait, what time is it?
I missed the time we agreed on...!
I'm sorry, I'll explain the situation later, I really am sorry, I'm so sorry... Could you please leave for now?
I'm not leaving.
I can see things have gone badly between you and the company. Do they think you're hard to control, so they're pushing you out and bringing in an Engineering Director who's easier to handle?
No, I...
I've heard plenty of stories like that. But if you're not the Engineering Director anymore, why won't they even approve your resignation?
A confidentiality agreement? A non-compete? Or do they still intend to make you take the fall for the Great Disconnect?
Ashton, was it? Approve Amelia's resignation now, or I'll find a way to make you approve it.
No... that's not it... oh no...
Amy, whether or not you're hiding something from us, come with us. We're going to the Far South together—we agreed.
Well, well. Mr. Campbell's daughter, Miss Jacinta Campbell, isn't it?
I saw you three years ago at a reception your father hosted when you came back to Big Ironton. Unwell as you were, your bearing was full of the poise of a great family. Most memorable.
But the company has never demoted Miss Amelia, and as for the Engineering Director, that has nothing whatsoever to do with her. Might there be some misunderstanding?
Amelia, care to explain?
Amelia?
Mr. Ashton... I... I can't...
Goodness. You mean you didn't tell this group of friends that you were repairing comms towers to make up for your own mistakes?
You didn't tell them that the company was dragged into this and became the culprit behind the Great Disconnect precisely because it respected your design?
What...?
Please stop... I'll explain to them myself...
Angie, please, I'm begging you, take them and go.
I—
Amy, he's lying! You clearly said the Great Disconnect was this Ashton's fault—
My colleague... um, Mr. Ashton, he's dreadfully careless in his work!
The data he submitted to me had plenty of errors, and he didn't run the tests properly. Everyone was in a rush, so the Gen-2 system went live in a great hurry...
The result was the Great Disconnect, and the company insists on holding me responsible—compensation, liability, all of it. But it clearly isn't my fault!
Why did this Ashton look nothing like a man who had made a mistake, and instead, from the very start, exactly like Amelia's direct superior?
A chill ran through Jacinta.
Ashton, did you... take part in designing the second-generation system?
I'm afraid not. Whether first generation or second, I've never been responsible for the actual technical development—only for coordination and management.
You don't suppose I stole Miss Amelia's position as "Engineering Director," do you?
Amelia, you...
You li—
No. What I want to ask... that isn't what I want to ask.
Just answer one question for me, Amelia. Any deception, any hidden reasons... we can talk about all of it later.
Right now I only want you to answer this one question honestly. Just one.
Tell me. When you said you wanted me to go with you to the Far South and see your dream through—was that true?
...I'm sorry, Jacinta. The company has given me a rare opportunity, and I need to catch up on the project progress I fell behind on.
As for all that dream talk about the Far South, please... forget it.
...Dream talk?
You're saying everything we said along the way... was just dream talk?!
That's not what I meant! I mean—I mean it was never going to happen, it was only, only...
Only something to say? Only because the mood was right, so you went along with what everyone else was saying... and said it?
You don't believe that! I don't need you to be honest with me—what you need to do is be honest with yourself! Amy, you obviously—
Stop pressuring her, miss.
I don't know what being honest with oneself means, but if she stays, she can at least be honest with her wallet and her stomach.
Not everyone can be like you, never lifting a finger and never wanting for anything—
Ashton, this is between the two of them. Please be quiet for a moment!
(Spreads his hands) Heh.
Amy?
Amelia didn't say a single word, and forced her gaze back to the screen of her terminal.
Her fingers began tapping stiffly at the keyboard, as if she really had something urgent to do.
Do you think that if you never speak again, you'll never say the wrong thing?
Amy, look at me!
Fine... Fine!
Jacinta!
Amy, you...
Sigh... Take care of yourself, and don't work so much overtime...
I know you must have your reasons. But... but still, think about what we promised each other...
Even if it's only thinking about it... all right?
Going to the Far South... just dream talk... Ha.
Why are so many people telling me I'm dreaming today...
Mom, Dad, I'm home!
Jacinta! Aren't you supposed to be at the sanatorium? Goodness, how did you get back alone—not one bodyguard with you!
I wanted to surprise you. The last time I came home was three years ago, and I missed you—
So you do know the last time was three years ago!
Father...?
Tell me yourself. In three years, how many times have you snuck out of the sanatorium, and how many times have you been taken to a hospital?
Your father and I know your condition, which is exactly why we worry...
Worry? Hmph. The moment she's in good spirits she goes around telling strangers her life story—
All right, don't work yourself into such a temper—
How can I not?! How many times is this now? Well?
Once or twice I could overlook. But now even foreigners know I have a daughter who runs around everywhere and won't be managed!
...So the reason you're this angry is... that people found out about me?
Oh, your father's been busy dealing with trade representatives from other countries lately, so his temper's gotten short. Don't take it to heart.
What would you like for dinner? I'll have the chef make it, or we can eat out. Get a good night's sleep at home, and in a couple of days I'll have someone take you back to the sanatorium. All right?
But I don't want to go back...
What's wrong? Still angry with your father?
The sanatorium isn't my home at all. Why do I have to stay somewhere that isn't home?!
Sweetheart, it's all for the sake of your health. If there's anything you want, your father and I will send it to you.
I got the photos you sent me recently. You earned two more certificates, and your burdenbeast riding looks quite accomplished. A true daughter of the Campbells.
But there are other things I want...
What is it you want?
I want to play cricket with someone other than my bodyguards. I want to hitch a ride from the northern end to the Far South. I want to come home whenever I want to see you...
And I want to help my friends make their wishes come true. I want—
You want far too much!
Your mother and I have never demanded anything of you. We know that every minute and every second you've lived from the age of five until now hasn't been easy.
We've never asked you to make something of yourself, or expected you to contribute to the family. Just be a daughter of the Campbells and don't tarnish the family name. That's enough!
Not tarnishing the name is enough?
So in your eyes, I've always been a stain that has to be hidden away?
Your father doesn't mean it that way—
Then what am I, exactly?
You say nothing. Should I take that as agreement?
Then let me be a stain! I don't want to hide anymore. I just want to go out—I know I don't have long to live!
...Your mother and I know that too. That's exactly why we have you recuperating at the sanatorium.
Is the sanatorium where I recuperate, or where the Campbells hide the daughter who has Oripathy?
Enough! As long as you stay at the sanatorium, do whatever you like. But if you want to do as you please, then make it happen in your dreams!
Huff... huff...
I... I took my medication on schedule. An attack shouldn't come on this fast...
Jacinta! What's wrong? Wait, I have suppressants—
Hey! What are you doing?
Who are you? Let go of Jacinta!
Miss Rhodes Island Operator, please step aside.
Rhodes Island's suppressants may be effective in composition, but we are the Campbell family's long-retained physicians. We know better what dosage suits Miss Jacinta.
The Campbells sent you? And you arrive this promptly?
Ever since Miss Jacinta came home, the madam assigned us to stay near her in case anything happened.
Miss Jacinta is stable. Let's take her home. She's been out on her own for so long that she needs a more thorough examination.
Excuse us.
...They followed her the entire way.
Come have a look—fresh carrot pizza! The finest specialty of Ultimate Big Ironton!
Hey, miss, you came by my shop last night, didn't you?
Ah, you remember me?
Of course I do! Didn't you say that if it was good, you'd bring three friends to give me your business? What, the pizza wasn't to your taste, so three became one?
The carrot pizza was delicious. It's just that some things happened yesterday...
A quarrel between friends? Then you need our carrot pizza all the more. Look at our sign—"Even enemies make up after a slice"!
...It wasn't the two of us who quarreled.
Then gather your friends together, eat a pizza, and talk it out!
Gather them together?
Today was supposed to be the day we all set out for the Far South together, but Amy and Jacinta...
No! Rather than break up in this muddled way, I'd sooner drag both of them back into the off-roader and go to the Far South together!
Here's the plan: I'll bite through the company's security cable, and you use your Arts to fly up to the tenth floor and snatch Amy out!
As for Jacinta, as for Jacinta... I'll keep her parents busy, and you grab a whole set of medical equipment and install it in the car—
Tani, calm down!
Look, the line behind us stretches way back. Let's not hold up the owner's business—come over here and we'll talk.
...In other words, we don't actually know whether Amy and Jacinta still want to set out.
How could they not want to go? We all agreed on the way to Big Ironton!
Never mind Jacinta—on Amy's side, I don't trust that Ashton one bit! Every word he said was pressuring her. Who knows how much of it was true?
But even if Ashton is a swindler through and through, what if Amy simply can't give up her job so easily?
...What?
Then what about Jacinta? She already spoke with her parents—
Right. Did she really get their approval?
When she came to find us last night, she looked awful. It's hard to say how that conversation with her parents actually went.
And she was so upset with Amy before. If Amy still wants to stay at the company...
Aaargh! It's all complicated grown-up logic! Are we really going to do nothing and just set off?

lines.st: Infected with Oripathy, forced to leave Siracusa—I could do nothing.
Rhodes Island destroyed, assigned to field duty and sent away—I could do nothing.
The Infected in Redsand set on dying, whom I couldn't lead away—I could do nothing.
And now? Faced with my friends' burdens and misunderstandings, can I still do nothing?
Even if I'm not an Elite Operator of Rhodes Island, even if I haven't mastered Originium Arts, even if I'm still not used to farewells...

lines.x: Angelina turned her head toward the road they had come by.
Even without the power to stand against a family...
Even if, as a caster, she still can't stand on her own...
Even if she can't steer things to an ending where everyone is better off...
...Angelina is already a Messenger.
Even a Messenger who makes mistakes ought to carry people's feelings.
For those who doubt themselves, those trapped in difficulty, or simply those being stubborn—to carry the words from the deepest part of their hearts that they truly want to say to someone.
If she hesitated over even this...
(Quietly) ...then how could I call myself a Messenger?
Angie?
(Takes a deep breath) Tani, I was overthinking things just now—
You agree? Good, let's go rescue them from the company and that medical team right now!
No, that's not what I—at least, that's not the first step!
What I mean is that their true feelings haven't been spoken aloud yet. They're still buried deep in their hearts.
If people's hearts naturally understood one another, the job of Messenger wouldn't exist.
People always have to say what they think out loud before they can find out whether their hearts truly align, and then choose how to face it.
Right now, we're the ones who haven't said what's in our hearts.
Maybe once we do, we'll find out those worries were for nothing... or maybe their minds will change.
What's in my heart is... the four of us reaching the Far South together! Angie, what about you?
The same.
After a journey this long, we became a group that can't be pulled apart. As long as you want to go to the Far South, I will get there with you.
Let's push our departure to tomorrow. I'll go change the application paperwork for the Far South first, then go to Meridian Red Earth to find Amelia.
I'll go straight to Jacinta. Her house is on the outskirts of the city, so it's a bit of a trip.
But... what if Jacinta's parents won't let me see her? What if Meridian Red Earth shuts you out?
As long as the feelings get through, I don't mind whether it means biting through the company's cables or hauling away every piece of medical equipment in Jacinta's house.
Every now and then, a Messenger has to have a bit of a temper!
Haha... Right!
By noon tomorrow at the latest, let's meet at the checkpoint from Big Ironton to the Far South.
I hope there'll be four of us then.
I hope there'll be four of us then.
As if nothing had happened.
The same stifling cubicle, the same solitary overtime, the same cycle of being scolded and doing it over.
She pulled open the locked bottom drawer on her right. It was stuffed with envelopes—resignation letters she had never handed in.
As long as she stuck it out, life would stay stable, and her material needs would be secure.
It's only a job. You were never supposed to ask more of it than that, were you?
Were you?
No... my choice is right. Being forgiven by the department head is already so, so lucky.
I was the one who rushed, who used a crude approach to solve the upgrade problem. If something went wrong, it should be on me.
My ability still isn't enough, my effort still isn't enough... I can become someone who stands on her own—just not now!
Not now.
S-sir... since I joined the company I've written more than a dozen proposals and experiment reports. Is there really no project at all you could put me in charge of?
I've told you. All the existing projects are saturated right now. We don't have time to launch new ones.
"Underground comms conduit laying and adjustment"—I heard Grace is in charge of that new project...
...It seems your workload still isn't enough, if you have time to ask around about other people's projects.

I know the underground conduits were your proposal, but I need someone with more experience to see the project through. You have potential, I know that. But you're not yet capable of leading a project alone.
Out you go.
Develop a fully automatic Originium-adaptive module? Not now!
I-I know we're still in the early stages of developing the semi-automatic technology... But based on our current approach, the staff operating inside...
Sigh. Now I see why Mr. Ashton warned me you weren't much of an employee.
What...
Have you read the company's promotional plan? Have you followed the recent news coverage of Meridian Red Earth?
Every tech company is fighting over the long-range comms operating rights in Rim Billiton. Only the first to release a product can corner the market.
How long would your fully automatic solution take to test? How much revenue would the company lose in that time? Can your salary fill that hole?

lines.st: I should have given the idea up then. So why did I keep refining the proposal in my off hours?
Was it pride acting up? Goodness—I thought I'd thrown that little scrap away long ago.
Or maybe I simply insisted too firmly that my technical concept was right, and that what is right will one day be discovered.

lines.x: Sir, you asked for me.
As I recall, when you were on the semi-automatic long-range comms project, you put forward an improvement proposal?
Ah! That proposal was t-too naive. It didn't consider the company's overall interests at all. The project supervisor already criticized me for it...
Bring it to me.
Y-yes...
Mm, not bad. From today, you're in charge of the second-generation technology.
Wh-what?!
Headquarters says a number of companies in Trimounts have started developing technology that could replace Meridian's comms towers, and some ethics committee is sniffing around.
And the rumors of Ursus's veins running dry are essentially confirmed. Rim Billiton will be running at full speed, and demand for long-range comms will be incalculable.

Implement your existing proposal directly, and it has to be fast. We've taken the lead in the long-range comms market—we can't fall at the final hurdle now! Two months. Upgrade the entire comms system.
Two months?! But the data in my report are theoretical values calculated for a laboratory environment. Field tuning alone would take at least six months...
And isn't that exactly where your ability comes in?
Your performance in entry-level positions has always been unremarkable. This may well be your only chance to stand out. Take hold of it.
Phew... Everything's finally updated. Tomorrow the second-generation comms technology officially goes into service.
My letter should have reached home by now. I've had so much overtime lately that I've barely been in touch with Dad... As for the other letter, I'll just read it to you, Mom.
It's thanks to this tower being built so high that I can be this close to you.
Mom, you always believed Amy was a capable child. And when I graduated I promised you I'd make sure you saw my name in the papers.
Now I've done it... It's only a shame it came a little late, so you couldn't see it with your own eyes.
You'd be proud of Amy, wouldn't you?
If one day I could invent a comms tower that reaches you, how... sniff... how happy I would be...
Every comms tower is down?!
The second-generation technology couldn't withstand the load of large-scale use when it went live. It simply collapsed...
Mr. Ashton, your office phone hasn't stopped ringing, and calls are coming in from partner firms and reporters!
(Takes a deep breath) Hold them off for a moment. I'm going to find Amelia.
Amelia? She's the project lead, yes, but—
Why do you think we put Amelia in charge in the first place?
A junior researcher with no backing who wants to get ahead. If it goes well, we pay out a little more bonus. If it goes wrong, what better shield could there be?
Where's Amelia... Where is Amelia?!
It's my fault... it's my fault... but it can still be saved, it can still be saved...

As long as I can tune them in the field, the comms cores and fully automatic modules will run normally... If we wait for the company to form an engineering crew, train them, then repair, it'll take far too long.
All those people who should have been able to reach their families far away... how anxious they must be.
I have to make up for my mistake... for my job, and for them...
I've already fixed three comms towers, and this one in Big Ironton will be repaired under the Engineering Director in a week.
I kept my job and most long-range comms are back. This is the best possible outcome...
Amelia looked out the window. The night sky to the south was deep, like a dream nobody had ever set foot in.
This is fine. This is fine.
Luckily, hardly anyone came looking for me during the days I slipped away. Only a few simple questions to answer, and since it's not my responsibility anymore, a standard template reply will do.
That's... a third of them answered. With a bit of overtime tomorrow and the day after, I should get through them all.
Amelia stretched and looked around the office, long since empty.
Mr. Ashton said I needn't organize anything, but... I'll help anyway.
Time was so tight that a lot of the Gen-2 design drafts are sloppy. The new Engineering Director won't be able to read them.
Why should he be able to read them?
The thought flashed through her mind, and she stamped it out herself.
She searched the company system for her own name, trying to file all the design drafts together—
No results found? Did I spell it wrong?
A... me... li... a... The spelling is right.
Try again... Still nothing. My name isn't there.
...My name isn't there?
Amelia shivered. She realized she'd been so dazed when she returned to her desk today that there was a great deal she hadn't checked.
She looked at the corner of the desk where the nameplate went.
No name...
She took out the employee badge she'd had reissued that afternoon.
No name!
Working up her nerve, she woke the terminal screen of the colleague next to her.
It's on... Let me see...
The name "Amelia" still turned up no results at all.
Everyone else's name turned up traces, more or fewer depending on access level. Only her own name had been erased completely, without a trace.
So this is... the price of coming back to the company? Erasing my name entirely?
Attention, citizens. Tomorrow, a fast-moving sandstorm will appear along the stretch from south of Big Ironton to the Far South, expected to last around two weeks.
Wind speeds in this sandstorm will be high, and the active Originium concentration within it will rise rapidly after approximately one day and night.
The long-range comms towers developed by Meridian Red Earth remain under repair and cannot provide long-range navigation...
A sandstorm?!
They're setting out tomorrow. Without the comms tower there's no way they can get through! I have to stop them—
Wait, two weeks... which means...?!
Amelia had no time to think it through.
The low-Originium window closes tomorrow, the company repairs the tower in a week, and the sandstorm lasts two weeks—I have to tell Mr. Ashton right now!
Pick up, pick up...!
Hello? Amelia? It's late. Finish what's on your desk right—
Mr. Ashton, could you let me—let the new Engineering Director fix the comms tower today?
Have you lost your mind?
My friends are going to the Far South, but there's going to be a sandstorm south of Big Ironton, and without our company's comms tower they can't get through!
And starting the day after tomorrow the Originium concentration there will rise. We can only fix the tower today or tomorrow, otherwise—
I don't know how you got in with that Campbell girl, but she's clearly given up on you.
Stop playing games and do your work, or you won't even keep the job you have.
I only want Jacinta and the others to be able to go to the Far South—
If I were her, you wouldn't have to bother. I'd set out the moment I heard about the sandstorm.
Give it up.
The room fell abruptly silent, and only then did Amelia realize she'd forgotten to ask about her name.
She stared at the empty search results on her terminal for a while. She could feel the blood surging from her heart out through her body, and it made her deeply uncomfortable.
She thought of the promise she'd made to her mother. The blood surged harder toward her hands.
She smacked the desk on instinct, but it did nothing to ease the fierce discomfort in her hands.
So this time she put everything she had into it and slammed both fists down on the questionably built office desk.
But they aren't you, Mr. Ashton.
I only want Jacinta and the others to be able to go to the Far South...
And I'm the only one who can make that happen.
One moment, Miss Tani. I'll inform Mr. Campbell and return shortly.
All right.
What a beautiful house... It's even more ridiculous than I imagined...
A house like this is enough to make you marvel? That's exactly why I say she'll only receive the best care here with us, rather than running around with the likes of you.
You're Mr. Campbell? I'm here to see Jacinta—
Thank you for your concern. Jacinta is quite well. Please leave.
Um... visiting someone isn't just about knowing how their health is.
Then what else do you want to know?
Miss Tani, you're Infected with Oripathy too. Wouldn't your family worry about your condition? Or did you also sneak out of your home?
Hmph. Foolish children. You don't treasure the settled life in front of you, and instead you run off.
You will never know how much your families love you, or the price they paid to raise you this far!
Then what should children like us do to repay that price?
Obey. That's all.
Obey, and stay at home like a piece of property that mustn't be damaged. Is that it?
Property... What nonsense are you spouting!
Isn't it? By what you said, the costlier the child, the more obedient they should be, right?
I don't know how Jacinta sees your "sacrifices," but I know how I feel. I'm grateful to my family. I know they care about me and protect me.
But as I grow up, what I want is bound to clash with what they think, and of course that hurts—because I love them, and I also love the life I planned for myself.
If being a proper daughter means matching my family's wishes in everything, then I'd rather be a bad child. I'd rather not have their approval!
Mr. Campbell, when you emphasize how much you've sacrificed for Jacinta and how much you love her, have you ever thought about what she argues with you for?
I don't need a lecture from you.
She argues with you because she wants your approval. Because she cares so much about you and Mrs. Campbell, and hopes for support from the people she loves!
You're unwilling to support her, but she'll keep meeting more people who are willing to. And those people don't have to be her family.
...Willful young people pay the price sooner or later. I won't let you see her. Show her out.
...If Angie hadn't told me over and over to mind my manners, I wouldn't have needed your permission in the first place, Mr. Campbell.
Miss Jacinta, you can't go downstairs.
I heard something down there...
It's late. Nobody will be coming. Please rest—it's the middle of the night.
Angie... Tani... and... sigh...
...Who's there?
Stop sighing and come open the window for me!
Tani?! How did you get up here?
Whoa, this is your room? It's just a hospital room. How is there not one thing of your own in it?
...After I got sick, this room was converted into a ward for easier treatment.
How are you feeling?
It wasn't the Oripathy at all. The doctor said it was because I hadn't eaten yesterday, plus Amy upsetting me...
You... you're still angry at Amy.
Of course I'm angry!
She did lie to us. Making her write ten sappy apology letters and broadcast them citywide wouldn't be too much.
But you could tell too—that Mr. Ashton definitely said something to her. She's easily swayed to begin with, and she has no confidence—
That's not what I'm angry about!
Huh?
Do you really think everything she said on the road was just to deceive us?
Did you see her face when she said it? What kind of swindler grins like an idiot after deceiving someone?
She was clearly talking about things she wanted to do but didn't have the nerve to—and she clearly can do them! Who in their right mind believes that Ashton!
I used to wonder why she was always so meek. Now I finally know—it's all the result of Meridian Red Earth grinding her down!
So what you're angry about is...

She's far more capable of shouldering things than she believes, and far more ambitious. She'd even worked out that she'd go to the Far South to collect data and develop cutting-edge comms technology entirely her own!
She has no idea how much I... envy her...
Jacinta?
After I got sick, my parents gradually stopped letting me go out, and eventually they sent me to the sanatorium. To pass the time, I started learning all sorts of skills.
Right. Earning that many certificates in that situation is impressive on its own.
But all I have is a stack of certificates. I've never practiced any of it!

I got my driver's license on an operation simulator. I learned burdenbeast husbandry on a wooden mechanical burdenbeast. When I did pastry, I wasn't allowed to stir the batter myself or go near the oven...
Those certificates are only good as conversation pieces at my parents' receptions. Maybe Father does understand me—what I'm best at is playing the well-bred young lady of the Campbell family...
Let me stop you there. Jacinta, want to drive?
Huh? Now?
Because it looks like someone's spotted us—
—Even if it shouldn't be now, it has to be now! We need to get outside the city and lie low!
A-are you sure? I warned you, I've never touched a real steering wheel, I—
I know. I'll be right here with you, don't worry.
(Gulps)
Her eyes swept over every part of the off-roader, trying to match them to what the operation simulator had shown—honestly, hardly anything matched.
But she closed her eyes and thought.
She remembered how Angelina and Tani looked when they drove, and remembered how badly she'd wanted to hold a steering wheel herself—
Her hands were trembling. The whole off-roader was trembling.
She took a deep breath and pressed the accelerator. The off-roader crept forward, and she turned to Tani in disbelief for confirmation.
Tani only smiled and gave no further instructions, but Jacinta was encouraged all the same.
Clutch, shift, accelerate, clutch again, shift, accelerate...
Jacinta Campbell was driving down the road. The wind flipped her ears back, and she listened to the sound of herself moving across the land.
She let out the wildest, most wholehearted laugh of her life, then let the speed she was making carry it away behind her.
Jacinta—I knew it—you can actually do anything well—!
Now—I know it too—hahahaha—!
So what—do you want—to do next—
I want—Amy—to apologize to us—!
Yes—!
I want—to go to that company—and drag her out—of that boring office—!
Yes—!
I want—I want to go with you—to the Far South!
Yes—!
At this hour, I wonder if Amy's still working overtime...
Huh? Why are there so many people?
Why didn't the alarm go off? Someone's inside the comms tower!
Who knows why! She caused the Great Disconnect and made all this trouble for us, and now she's showing off again?
Haven't you heard? Everyone's saying it behind closed doors—that Mr. Ashton deliberately used that girl's technology as a trial run so the blame could be shifted if it failed...
Enough. Mr. Ashton has already gone over. Let's call people in quickly—we can't let her fix the tower before the Engineering Director arrives, or the whole promotional campaign is wasted!
Inside the comms tower? ...Amy?
The sky was growing light.

The Anaty, who should have been sitting in an office sending the same email back and forth a few hundred times, was instead sitting on the upper walkway of the Big Ironton comms tower, her whole attention on the circuit board in front of her.

Big Ironton is close to the Far South, and changes in atmospheric Originium concentration there are complex. She had spent nearly the entire night measuring data, and when she lifted her head she hadn't even noticed the sun had already risen.
Mm... so bright. The module's finally tuned. Now I just connect it to the comms core and put it—
Amelia! What on earth are you doing?! Do you not want your job anymore?!
Come down this instant and don't touch that comms tower, do you hear me?!
M-Mr. Ashton!
This is bad... I'm still too slow. I have to finish what needs doing before they come up and grab me.
Angie and the others might be setting out soon. Faster, a little faster—
Otherwise I won't make it in time, otherwise I climbed this whole tall tower for n-nothing!
Tch. Why hasn't security arrived? Are they all sitting around eating dried turnip?!
Never mind. Can't I handle one girl who bursts into tears at the drop of a hat? I'll go get her myself—
Hold it.
Mr. Ashton, what are you planning to do?
Me? I... Sigh. I'm only trying to stop Amelia from doing something foolish!
Foolish?
That's right. I went to great lengths to save her job from management. I felt for her—her mother has passed away and her father is far off, and it isn't easy for her making her way here alone.

And what does she do? She grants herself security clearance without permission and spends the night in the comms tower. I worry she's about to do something against Meridian's—against her own future...
You're her friend, so you must know Amelia is afraid of heights. She's up there alone with no help. It's pitiable. Please coax her down.
Coax her down?
Angelina looked up.
The newly risen sun shone on Amelia's hair, which never would lie flat, making her look even smaller and thinner than Angelina remembered.
She sat motionless on the tower's upper walkway. Perhaps, just as Mr. Ashton said, Amelia was frightened right now.
But Angelina knew her friend.
Throughout this journey, this clumsy, panicky girl had shown a back that resolute and that focused at only one kind of moment—
When she was working.
And that meant the question Angelina hadn't yet asked Amelia—whether or not she was still going to the Far South—already had its answer.
I see.
Excellent. Don't worry, security will arrive shortly. If you'll just coax her down first—
Hm? My legs...
My arms too... Why are they suddenly so heavy? A stroke?!
Ashton turned and found that it wasn't only him—the first wave of employees and security personnel who had arrived were all held fast by some unknown force.
Meanwhile the Vulpo in front of him leapt lightly onto the metal handrail of the stairs and smiled.
Don't worry, Mr. Ashton. You're a long way from a stroke.
Though I imagine that over these years you've gotten used to drifting weightlessly around Meridian Red Earth?
How about feeling the true force of gravity for a change?
It's fully light out. I wonder if Angie convinced Amy...
Hmph. If even Angie, the most reasonable of us, can't get through to her, then you and I each grab a sleeve and haul the whole girl into our off-roader!
I like that plan!
Who's that? In more of a hurry than we are?
The markings on the back look like Meridian Red Earth's, and they're headed toward... the comms tower?
Wait, isn't there someone on the upper level of the tower?
Amy?!
That's right, that big fluffy tail... it's Amy!
Why would she be fixing the tower at this hour? Don't tell me...
There's no "don't tell me" about it! I don't care why she's fixing it, but if she's up there and Meridian Red Earth's people are rushing over, that means Amy wasn't sent by them!
So... those people racing to the comms tower are going to give Amy trouble?
Give Amy trouble?
J-J-J-J-Jacinta—!
You've been driving for how long, and you dare floor it like that?!
Don't worry, Tani. You have no idea how many times I've rehearsed this scene in my dreams!
In your dreams—does that even count?!
The orange off-roader kept accelerating and quickly caught up to the rear of the security convoy.
The guard in the last truck of the convoy yawned out of sheer boredom, then saw two bright young faces grinning outside his window.
Before he could react, an orange off-roader suddenly cut across in front of him—and gave him a faceful of exhaust for good measure.
The second, the third, the fourth... Like some ill-omened star, the orange off-roader forced every vehicle in the security convoy to a stop.
The last thing the drivers remembered was an orange off-roader ringing with delighted laughter, slowly vanishing into their chorus of complaints.
Jacinta... you might actually have a talent for racing...
I think so too! Once we're back from the Far South, I'm going to take a couple of laps at a proper racetrack!
But right now, let's get to the comms tower!
Angie held off Mr. Ashton and the others?
I lied to her, and she... she's still helping me... sniff...
Phew... All right, Amy. Now isn't the time for crying.
The comms core is replaced, and the fully automatic module seems to be running without much trouble...
An error?! Did I set a parameter wrong? That can't be right.
Wait... This is the largest tower. More of the circuitry may have burned out in the disconnect than I thought...
She looked toward the tower's spire, and a charcoal-gray panel confirmed her guess.
Good. As long as I reconnect the sensor, the tower will run.
But from here to the spire... it looks like the only way up is the maintenance ladder, with no safety gear...
Ngh... Stop shaking, Amy. You can do this. You have to be able to do this!
The small Anaty shifted her tools to where she could reach them and stepped onto the first rung of the maintenance ladder.
Angie! I've got Jacinta! How's Amy doing?
I can't see clearly from the base. All I know is she was in front of the tower's main circuit board a moment ago. By rights, replacing the comms core should be all it takes.
Going by our experience fixing towers before, it should be done soon. With the tower's navigation, the road to the Far South will be safer too.
Wonderful, the four of us can finally set out together!
Before that, though, shouldn't we think about how to get out of a ring of Meridian Red Earth employees and security forces...
All I can do is slow their steps with gravity for a while. I hope Amy can hurry. I've never sustained my Arts this long before, and I'm worried...
We believe in you, Angie! Didn't you tell us all those stories about practicing your Arts at Rhodes Island?
Have you forgotten the time we escaped from Great Springs? My Arts can go out of control—
Sniff... sniff...
Hold on, I think I hear someone crying...
It's Amy!
Amelia always cried just a little longer than other people.

At four she scraped her knee open and cried by the river for an hour. Her father was off working in another country then, and her mother—the only family beside her—was working the mine and couldn't come help her up.
When she'd cried herself out, she patted the dust off and limped home.
When she learned she'd been accepted to Rim Billiton Industrial University, she cried in her room for two hours.

Her mother wanted to make her the carrot mille-feuille that was popular at the time, but she didn't want her mother spending money, so the two of them shared a bowl of carrots stewed in syrup in the kitchen.
When her mother died, she cried for an entire day.

She had resolved to show her mother what she looked like when she'd made something of herself. She wanted to set her endlessly worried mother at ease—that besides her father, she too could be someone her mother could lean on.
But she missed her chance.
She began mailing every result and certificate of her efforts home, afraid of losing another chance to make her family proud.
She fell into the habit of overtime, scoldings, and more overtime, studying the one thing she was good at—the one thing that could make her briefly forget her regret.
If she just kept at it, she should have done brilliantly... So why was she now standing on the verge of losing her job, her friends, her confidence, her dream?
Limbs weak, she climbed, wanting to take back every wrong choice and every wrong thing she'd done—and knowing all the while that she was shaking and crying.
She felt she would never reach the top, that she would always disappoint people, and then—
Amelia!
A familiar voice was shouting from somewhere far, far below her.
J-Jacinta?
Don't look back, idiot, you'll fall! Don't stop moving. If you've got something to say, just say it—I'll be listening from here!
O-okay...
Jacinta... I'm so sorry! When you told me I was actually amazing, at first I—
At first I didn't believe it!
I could tell!
There are so many seniors at the company who say "that's amazing"! But it's just how they say hello! They don't care about anything you make!
Don't shred your throat yelling that! Of all things! What a mood-killer! We've got other things to say!
When you—and Tani, and Angelina! When you encouraged me over and over! I really did start to feel I could do a lot of things!
So I let slip all those thoughts and dreams I'd never told anyone... but... sniff... I still can't do any of it...
Louder! I can't hear you!
I can't tell you with any certainty that I really want to go to the Far South with you! I can't hand in my resignation and walk out of the company! I'm even afraid to climb a comms tower, sniff—
Don't you cry, Amelia!
And now you won't even let me cry!
...What I mean is! Open your eyes and look—you've already climbed! To the top!
Amelia stood at the tower's spire. The sun seemed within arm's reach, and all of Big Ironton lay in her eyes.
The comms technology she developed stretched north from here, linking town after town, mobile mining platform after mobile mining platform.

Giving everyone who had left home the chance to say a few words to the people they cared about. Making sure feelings that are hard to voice but still want saying no longer had "distance" to hide behind.
Amelia suddenly realized that from up here, Meridian Red Earth's logo looked very, very small, while her own shadow on the ground was very, very large.
I'm resigning...
What was that?

I—said—
I!
AM!
RE!
SIGNING!
I'm resigning, and I'm going to the Far South!
Amy! Is the comms tower fixed or not?!
The sensor's working. I f-fixed it—!
Then why aren't you moving?!
I-I really don't have any strength left. It's so high up here...
The security forces have caught up! Think of a way out, quick—the company definitely won't let her walk away now!
Ugh, we finally got the comms tower fixed, and we still can't get to the Far South...
I... sniff... what am I supposed to do now...
Stop crying! What if your legs give out and you can't stay on your feet?!
Then how about...
The hand gripping Angelina's staff burned. She recalled how every practice session with her Arts had felt—not one of them was like this.
In the training room she had spent countless days and nights on how she released her Arts, drawing up training plan after training plan for herself. And still her Arts were always unstable.
After she recovered from that severe onset when she first came to Rhodes Island, Dr. Warfarin had sought her out for a very serious talk.
Dr. Warfarin said that gravity-related Originium Arts were extraordinarily hard to control to begin with, and that if she couldn't control them well, she should use them as little as possible.
Even if one can rely entirely on an Arts Unit, the Infected should always remember this:
When someone uninfected makes a mistake, what's spent is other people's trust. When an Infected person makes a mistake, what burns is her own life.
Angelina had taken Warfarin's words to heart, in fact.
But those words had also planted a small seed in her—that one day she would be the sort of person who burns her life for one person, one thing, one ideal.
An ideal is still somewhat far from her now.
But that one thing worth everything she had, those people, and herself—they were right here before her.
She had already missed one chance to burn. She refused to miss another.
...Make the range of the Arts as wide as I can, the anti-gravity as strong as I can...
(Quietly) It'll be fine. It's going to be fine.
Amelia! Jump!
What?!
Now that we all know every one of us wants to go to the Far South, we shouldn't stop here!
Jump, Amelia, don't be afraid! I'll catch you—I'll catch every one of you!
I'm not afraid, Angie... I believe in you!!
Good!
Tani, Jacinta, are you two ready too?
Yes!
On my count!
Three—
Two—
One—
Jump—!
The carrots stacked neatly in wooden crates, the employees still hurrying to report upstairs, the four girls whose hearts were finally in step—all of them drifted lightly into the air.
Ashton and the security staff felt their heavy feet come free and float up far too easily, like dried carrots dropped into water.
Tani lost all sense of direction the moment gravity left her and spun in the air; Jacinta laughed with delight, gazing around this zone of undone order with pure curiosity.
Angelina, meanwhile, knew this weightlessness well.
It was exactly this feeling that had carried her from Siracusa to Rhodes Island, and from Rhodes Island to thousands upon thousands of cities and regions.
Watching Tani and Jacinta floating beside her, watching Amelia flailing in the air, she had never been so certain that she could be the most reliable guide and friend they had.
In this small floating world, Angelina forgot, for the first time, what she had lost while growing up.
Perhaps she had missed some time with her parents. Perhaps she had missed the moment to tell someone important how she felt.
Perhaps she had been powerless before Rhodes Island's disaster, and before the Infected of Redsand...
But the weight of the staff in her hand reminded her now: she had caught her friends, and this weight was what she wanted to remember, and to protect.
The four of them would go to the Far South together.
Huff... huff... So far.
Well, when we got here the base of the tower was ringed with Meridian Red Earth's vehicles, so this was the only place we could park.
We're finally at the car. Let's go!
The sky... the sky is still spinning...
Comms really are back... Whose terminal is that ringing?
Mine.

Is it Meridian Red Earth giving you trouble again?! Hand me the terminal—I'll give that Mr. Ashton a piece of my—
Huh? You actually handed it over?
I've already replied.
Let me see, let me see!
"The resignation letter is in the bottom drawer on the right. The lock has already been opened for you."
"Goodbye forever, you garbage who wasted my time."
Whoa... Is this the first time Amy's ever cursed anyone out?
That's more like it! Practice more from now on—that was still too soft!
All right, that's enough! I'm growing too, you know... Give me back my terminal. I'm deleting the work chat app.
Done!
Good. Then let's hit the road—
Jacinta.
Mother?
Did Father send you to talk me into coming back...
No. I came to see you off.
You're both letting me go to the Far South?
You weren't planning to ask our permission anyway, were you?
We'll still worry about you, Jacinta. Your condition leaves you far less room for error in life than most people have.
But I saw your smile.
...Huh?
The smile on your face while you were driving—your father and I haven't seen that expression on you since you were infected.
Just as your friend Miss Tani said...
Huh? Me?
We don't agree with your decision, but we've finally understood: you share the things you want to do with us because you love us.
I've come to terms with it. As for your father... he said things that day he didn't mean. Let me apologize on his behalf. You have never been a stain on the Campbell family, Jacinta.
I think he regrets it. It's only that the man has spent too long maneuvering in business to even apologize properly to his own daughter.
Mother...
No, it's nothing. If he still hasn't come around by the time I'm back from the Far South, you'll be on my side, won't you?
Of course.
Get going, girls. Don't worry about the little commotion you caused at Meridian Red Earth—we'll find a way to handle it.
Nothing should hold my child back from setting out. Not even your father and me.
Thank you...
(Quietly) That's really nice...
Tani suddenly had the urge to dig her terminal out of the depths of her backpack.
But that would be such a hassle, she thought.
What mattered most right now was setting out at once for the Far South. Once they got there...
Come on, let's set off!
The checkpoint to the Far South is open, and the sandstorm is moving toward the stretch we're traveling...
Our heading is fine. Once we're inside the sandstorm I can't navigate for everyone, so it'll all depend on the tower Amy fixed.
I can see the outline of the sandstorm already.
Speaking of which, Tani—did your grandmother ever tell you how she crossed the sandstorm to reach the Far South?
Of course she did.
Grandma said she picked a day with low Originium concentration and not much wind and sand to cross that area.
Luckily, the concentration didn't change much while she was crossing the danger zone—but the fast-moving sandstorms still put her through a lot.
In the end it was her pocket watch that strengthened her Arts and kept the sandstorm from swallowing her, so she got to see the Far South!
What does the Far South look like?
She said the Far South looks nothing like Big Ironton... nothing like anywhere else in Rim Billiton!
The ground there is like a mirror—vast, vast stretches of crystal!
Crystal?
Grandma only said it was beautiful—a clear sky, water pooled on the crystal ground, little flowers in the cracks. But I looked up a lot of material afterward...
They say those crystals are actually minerals that form alongside Originium. The Originium in the Far South was all activated long ago and became part of the dust in the danger zone.
And the minerals left behind are extremely hard—so hard that not even the energy of Originium activation could break their original structure...
—Waah! Did we just hit a rock? My backpack nearly went flying!
That startled me. Check your seat belts again!
In that case, before we hit the rough stretch... here!
Carrot pizza?
They say it's Big Ironton's new specialty, but... why?
"Carrot pizza—the perfect gift for friends and family. Even enemies make up after a slice."
The owner promised me himself.
Once we've finished this pizza together, nobody's allowed to bring up Amy getting bullied by that company ever again. Not even as a joke!
You're all... sniff... I'm sorry... thank you...
I know. After we eat it—no, even if we didn't eat it, we'd still be the best of friends.
Angie, why aren't you eating!
Does it have to be carrot pizza...
You don't like it? The owner said his technique is completely authentic. You're bound to taste a bit of home!
I... I'm driving, it's not convenient!
I'll need to contact the Big Ironton control tower soon to steer us clear of danger, so there's no time to eat—
I could feed it to you?
Waaah—

lines.st: Having written this far, it feels like I should bring the letter to a close. It seems I've done nothing but ramble on... I'm truly sorry.
I hope this letter reaches your hands safely—and yet part of me hopes it simply vanishes somewhere between one Messenger and the next, seen by no one at all.
But I've decided to send it anyway, to you. I hope it reaches you. At the very least, that would mean you're well.
I wish you all the best.
With love, Angelina

lines.x: Calling Big Ironton control tower, calling Big Ironton control tower! This is Angelina! Please confirm our position relative to Big Ironton!
This is the control tower. You are continuing to move southeast and are currently at the edge of the sandstorm zone. Your position relative to Big Ironton is—krrsh...
The signal is getting more and more unstable...
Control tower, confirm once more—how far are we from Big Ironton now?
Angel—krrsh... twenty kilometers from Big Ironton! The sandstorm ahead of you is... krrsh... about seven kilometers! These are estimates only; the sandstorm's extent may change at any time...
Control tower—
...Krrsh... krrsh...
...Through! Get through quickly! Originium concentration is rising—krrsh—an active Originium tide from east-southeast—krrsh—
An active Originium tide?!
Control tower, requesting confirmation of the tide's arrival time!
Requesting confirmation of the tide's arrival time!
The connection to the tower is down?!
This is bad... No system, however stable, can withstand interference from an active Originium tide!
...Amelia, check the car's Originium concentration monitor!
...By Rim Billiton standards, it's about a quarter below the safety threshold!
Which means it's already past Rhodes Island's safety standard! Everyone—
—Angie, don't you dare start canvassing opinions! Nobody wants to turn back!
Did I say anything about turning back?
I said get your protective gear ready. I'm speeding up!
Tani, ears up—don't miss a single suspicious sound!
Leave it to me!
