Amelia, it's a bit of a shame, but please release two more "Little Bugs" and report anything unusual around us as it happens!
R-right!
Jacinta, if you're not carsick, please watch what's behind us for me!
Who gets carsick when their life's on the line?!
Then I'm accelerating—
Hold on, I hear something outside the window...
It's Tuft... no, it's a pouched musbeast?!
Why is it following us? Did we really see one before—no, could it have been this same one the whole time?
Why show itself at a moment like this?!
Is it g-g-going to steal the words I want to say even now?!
Angie, the pouched musbeast looks like it's struggling to fly... and it seems to be heading south too! What do we do?
Whatever else, we have to get it inside before the active Originium concentration climbs too high!
The other three nodded one after another.
Angelina steadied the wheel with one hand and rolled down the window with the other, meeting the eyes of the tiny creature battling the storm.
Squeak...?
Come on in, little one!
Squeak squeak!
Almost the instant the little creature was inside, Angelina shut the window tight and gripped the wheel with both hands. The Arts Unit at her side glowed faintly.
Thanks for hanging in there, Tuft...
Huh? Its name is Tuft?
But look at that tuft of fur on its head—it really stands out... Angie, what do you think?
Isn't the fuzz on a pouched musbeast's head what grew after that brave Rim Billitonian hit it?
Oh, you mean that story?
If that's true, then every pouched musbeast should have fur up there, so calling this one Tuft would be about the same as naming a burdenbeast "Big Eyes."
...I don't care! Its name is Tuft, all right!
If you insist on it, I suppose there's no harm...
...Because this time we really are speeding up!
Waaaaaaaah!
Squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak?!
Cough, cough! Angie, I can't see anything out there anymore...
All the "Little Bugs" I released have gone out of contact... Should I send up another batch?
Tani, what about you? Do you hear anything different?
I can't hear! The wind and sand are too loud, I can't hear anything el—
Tani?
I'm listening... It is a different sound, it's...
The car's skidding?!
It's water!
Water?!
Yes, it's water—the wheels are slipping! The surface just turned smooth!
The wind and sand stopped! It's—it's—!
While Tani was searching for the words, the car finally broke through the last barrier. A view none of them had ever imagined unfolded before them.
For a while, none of the four in the car could speak.
Only when the pouched musbeast let out an excited squeak did Angelina come back to herself, slowly bringing the car to a stop and opening the door.
Looking at what lay before her, she fell briefly speechless.
After standing there for a long moment, she chose to spread her arms and welcome the clean wind.
So this is... the Far South...?
A sky washed clear after the rainy season, water pooled like a mirror on the ground, little flowers poking up between the crystals...
Exactly the way Grandma described it! So I really made it. This is...
Tani tapped the ground lightly with her foot, not out of impatience, but because she didn't know how else to let out what was swelling in her chest.
Light splashes bloomed under her feet and wet the toes of her shoes. The damp chill made her shiver.
Then, all at once, she stomped hard.

Grandma—
We made it to the Far South—
The Cautus was facing into the wind, and yet she clearly felt her voice carry very, very far—
We made it—
We finally made it—
After being so tightly strung a moment ago, the shout left the Vulpo feeling slightly short of breath.
She knew she was dizzy and couldn't keep her feet steady, but just then she preferred to believe the earth was inviting her to a light little dance.
So she spun several times in a row, let the dizziness take her balance, and sat down hard in the water.
Whew...
She looked over at Jacinta and Amelia. They too were struck by the sight and couldn't speak for a long while.
I... I never imagined this place would be like this...
It's unlike anywhere I've ever been, like a mirror reflecting the sky...
Amy, I—
Amelia's face was flushed red with excitement.
Hearing Jacinta's voice, Amelia turned her head toward her and met her eyes.
All right, all right. Amelia, didn't you have equipment you wanted to test in the Far South?
I can test my own equipment anytime, so that's not a problem. But according to the "Little Bugs," there's no signal source in the Far South right now...
Are you saying Rhodes Island's equipment is broken too?
Yes...
By rights, equipment like that should connect automatically once the long-range comms system is fixed. Even if it can't, it should retry at intervals. There shouldn't be no signal at all.
Since it still hasn't connected, the device itself may have been damaged during the disconnect...
Oh, right! There's clearly no comms tower here, so how was Rhodes Island's equipment connecting to the long-range comms system at all?
Rhodes Island's device must have a dedicated high-power transmitter that sends data one-way to the comms tower in Big Ironton—

But at Meridian I wasn't responsible for maintaining custom equipment—it might not even be custom-made. It could be something Rhodes Island developed themselves... I have no confidence I could fix it!
—It's all right! I can just take the hard drive with the stored data back to Great Springs for decryption.
Wait, I was so busy being happy that I forgot... the Far South is the end of the journey!
...And?
And a place as flat as a mirror like this... wouldn't one look tell you whether the pocket watch is here?
The four of them looked all around, but the nearly featureless ground held nothing at all.
Fennel... roasted parsnip? What's a parsnip?
It's a vegetable they grow a lot of in Green Meadow Prefecture. It looks quite like a carrot, but it tastes completely different.
Do they sell it in Great Springs? If they do, I'll buy some and have Mom make it tomorrow.
Haha, no need, my little Thumpy. A bit of carrot soup is plenty for your grandma.

lines.st: When I was sixteen, Originium crystals had just begun to appear on my arm. As it happened, that was also when Grandma began eating less and less.
Even though Grandma was by any measure among the longest-lived in Great Springs, those two things still cast a shadow over our home back then.
Grandma clearly noticed.

Father took out his anger on the town's hot-spring business for the Infected, and she gave him a dressing-down. Mother, desperate in her worry, nearly fell for a swindle, and it was Grandma who steadied her.
And for me—growing older with more and more on my mind, past sixteen and still stuck in Great Springs—she once again spent the most time of all.
Just as she had in my earliest memories, she'd take hours to slowly tell me about the things she'd seen and the funny stories from her travels.
But my longing to leave home always had me steering the conversation, knowingly or not, toward certain particular subjects.

lines.x: Grandma, so is it possible you actually lost the pocket watch in Green Meadow?
When your grandma went to Green Meadow, she didn't have half as many wrinkles as when she went to the Far South.
Hmm... But the Far South is so far away.
If I want to be as amazing as you, is there really no way around making the trip to the Far South...
No, wait, Grandma—didn't you say the watch might not have been lost in the Far South at all, and could have been dropped somewhere along Route Zero?
That's right.

lines.st: Thinking back now, her smile at that moment looked a little complicated. Perhaps she'd wanted to tell me something.
Perhaps the watch was simply broken and thrown away. Perhaps it was traded for life-saving supplies when Grandma had no other options. Perhaps it was given to someone who had helped her. Perhaps...

lines.x: ...Perhaps even if I got the watch, I could never become a master of Originium Arts like Grandma?
Was she only trying to keep me from being disappointed, always telling me the watch was lying somewhere between Great Springs and the Far South, waiting for me to find it?
Angie, Jacinta, Amy, look—over here is...
It's the sea! It's the ocean!
The sea...?
The end of the Far South... is the sea?
She spread out the map of Rim Billiton on the ground and only then realized this wasn't the end of the Far South—but that they truly had reached the enormous fjord in southeastern Rim Billiton.
The crystal was no longer flat but rugged and broken. Dizzyingly fine patterns showed in the drops between, until the crystal ended where the sea began, becoming a sheer cliff.
Farther out, sunlight spilled across a cold-toned sea, declaring that the land ended here and gilding everything in sight with an unreal halo.
It was a moment of calm wind and still water. Gentle waves stroked the cliff face, and the sound of them was like a soft call everyone has heard once in a dream.
...Grandma never said the Far South had a place like this.
Don't be discouraged. Maybe she just forgot to tell you—
No, that's not what I meant.
Tani shaded her eyes with her hand and gazed at the sun, veiled by sea mist.
It's just that now, just here and now, I suddenly feel...
...that even if I never find the watch, this place is still beautiful, and I've still walked a very, very good journey.
Mm.
It's freezing!
It really is! I wish I had thick fur like Tuft... Is Tuft all right?
I think she used up all her strength in the sandstorm and then got startled in the car. She's been asleep on my shoulder this whole time.
I was afraid I'd soaked her when I fell into the water, but it looks like she's fine...
What is it?
Look over by the cliff edge... isn't there something small glinting?
...There really is!
At the edge of the cliff, something was glittering in the sunlight.
Could it be... could Grandma really have left her pocket watch... here?
As if in a dream, Tani walked unsteadily toward that clear glimmer at the cliff's edge.
Angelina wanted to call her back, but it was the wish Tani had carried the whole way, so Angelina only followed carefully behind her.
What a beautiful glimmer...
That crystalline light stayed exactly where it was, as if waiting for Tani to come and wake it.
No, it's not a pocket watch—it's... a pouched musbeast's eyes?
There are more—there are so many pouched musbeasts here!
So fluffy... so cute...
Behind the rock face, beneath the reefs, beside the crystal... pouched musbeasts appeared in places the four of them hadn't noticed before.
Some of their pouches held wild fruit, some held flowers and grasses, and some held small glittering objects, as if they truly meant to deliver them somewhere.
Are they here to welcome us?
Come to think of it, the one they're welcoming is probably Tuft.
If it was Tuft who loosened the luggage I'd strapped down before I reached Great Springs, then she's traveled a very long way to get home.
Tuft, we're home—hm?
(A frightened hiss)
For some reason, Tuft didn't look relaxed at all. She shrank back instead, trying to hide behind Angelina.
At the same moment, the fluffy creatures came flying toward the four of them—
My car keys!
My spray can!
Th-th-this—Amelia, weren't you about to say something to me? How about saying it right now?
How am I supposed to remember at a time like thiiiis—
Don't tell me the legend is true and they really are going to steal all our words?!
"There's no way!"
Even as they denied it inwardly, the thought left them uneasy.
Having walked to the end of the land, the four of them raised whatever in their hands could pass for a weapon, ready to take back the stories they hadn't finished telling.
They've knocked down all the "Little Bugs"... What do we do?
Don't look at me, I can't fly!
...There's no end to this!
Angie, can't you do something big with your Arts like in Big Ironton—no, reverse them and bring every pouched musbeast down to the ground?
I could—
Another pouched musbeast swooped toward Tuft on Angelina's shoulder, and Angelina barely dodged while keeping her Arts going.
—but they're not really a threat, and I'm afraid they'd get hurt falling to the ground...
But they're about to make off with everything we own!
Squeak...
And Tuft looks more and more frightened!
That said, protecting Tuft from a swarm of pouched musbeasts was more than manageable.
The lead pouched musbeast clearly realized as much. It circled several times in the air, gathering its companions with their stuffed-full pouches, and then...
Squeak-squeak-squeak, gaa-gaa-gaa-gaa!
It's calling for reinforcements again!
One of them squeaked like that and a whole swarm came. If a whole swarm squeaks like that, how many will come?!
Could it be... calling the biggest, strongest one of all...
I can hear it... Something very big really is coming!
Much bigger than the largest one. It's even walking forward on two legs, and the cloth draped over it is as tall as a person—
It's heeeere—
Hm? Here? Who? Me?
Yes, y—
Er... Huh?
You... aren't a pouched musbeast?
Angelina, what do you think?
Even with her name spoken, Angelina couldn't get a word out for a long moment.
The person in front of her was, of course, not a pouched musbeast.
It was the one who had reached out a hand when she was in trouble, the one she'd always wanted to meet and always missed, the one she had poured her doubts and worries out to.
But... why here?
Coincidence? Some sort of intuition? Or...
In any case, she was standing right in front of her.
Martina...
It's good to see you again, Angelina.
Squeak-squeak-squeak—skritch-skritch-skritch—squeak-squeak!
Hm?
Squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak! Gaa-gaa!
Mm. Hm?
(Quietly) Is this the Miss Martina who helped you that you told us about?
(Quietly) That's right.
(Quietly) She looks like she's having a lovely chat with that pouched musbeast... Are you sure she isn't some shapeshifting pouched musbeast grandma?
(Quietly) How could she possibly be—
Angelina, she's demanding to know why you kidnapped her child.
What?!
...Pff.
She says the four of you kidnapped her child, and that as the mother she can't beat you, so she had to call the father and bring out the whole family.
So... that's how we look to them? Then, Miss Martina, what sort of... um... relative of Tuft would you be?
Pff!
I only wish I could fly as fast and as steadily as a pouched musbeast. If I could, maybe I'd be a better Messenger than Angelina.
Unfortunately I'm just an idler here to observe wildlife. I happened to get on good terms with them, so the desperate pouched musbeast father dragged me over as reinforcements.
All right, let this little pouched musbeast see her mother and father.
Seeing the chaos settle, Tuft let out two careful squeaks.
And the pouched musbeast the four of them had first seen in the Far South cried out in a voice they hadn't heard before—half anxious, half puzzled.
After a few rounds of back-and-forth, Tuft finally stopped cringing the way she had before.
She looked at the four humans on her side, exchanged a glance with her mother, spread her wings, circled the group once...
and pressed her carrying pouch briefly to each of their faces.
Oh my, how lovely.
That means she really likes all of you. Likes you enough to want to put you in her pouch and carry you off.
Mm... Yes.
Tuft landed on Angelina's hand, touched her fingertip with her nose, gave one affectionate squeak, then beat her wings and flew back to her mother.
So she kept chasing after Angie because she was trying to take her child back...
Then why did Tuft look so frightened?
That question was soon answered.
Having confirmed her child was unhurt, the mother pouched musbeast plainly began scolding her, and Tuft shrank smaller and smaller before her, looking about to bury her head under her own body.
Tsk, tsk. Nothing happened to the child. There's no need to lecture her like that.
Besides, now that the misunderstanding is cleared up, shouldn't you be giving back what you took just now?
Ah, I forgot. I can roughly make out what they mean, but they can't understand a word I say.
Hey—
All right, all right. I can see the four of you have a great many questions, so why don't we go to my tent and talk properly?
Just hearing everything you saw and did along the way has taken us to the small hours...
Well, we did get some sleep in the middle, haha...
Mm. It'll be light soon.
How nice. When I was your age, I always dreamed of setting out on a journey like that.
Weren't you a Messenger back then, Miss Martina?
Not yet.
By ordinary standards I'm a very fortunate person. I went to school normally, grew up normally, even went to university and frittered away a few more years than most.
At your age I spent every day weighing what I ought to do after graduating—but only weighing it. I never truly put any effort toward it.
In the end I became a Messenger only because my family had that tradition, and I stumbled onto the path half-aware.
If the choice before me back then had been a clerk's job that never left the office, or a family business to inherit, I'd probably have turned out completely different from who I am now.
Whatever the case, you were the one who helped me then, and it was because I looked up to you that I—
Which is why you're already doing better than I did at that age.
Really?
Honestly, coming to the Far South wasn't me setting out on a journey of my own accord either... If anything, it was my mistake and a string of coincidences...
Look, this is the decryptor I was supposed to send to Great Springs on Rhodes Island's behalf. I sent it to the wrong place, which is why—
So it was sent to the wrong place?
...Huh?
What a coincidence. I received one exactly like it.
What?!
So the first time, I actually sent the decryptor to you?! Together with that letter?
That's right. The outside said to deliver it to Great Springs, but since it arrived with your letter, I opened it just in case.
I couldn't make heads or tails of the principles or the technology, but I could read the instructions inside. It's a decryptor, and the information to be decrypted comes from the Far South.
Once I knew that, I meant to deliver the package to Great Springs on your behalf.
But when I found the office and was about to walk in, I suddenly remembered the things you'd written in your letter.
The Great Disconnect happened right around then, too, so I thought—why not see what choice this mistake leads you to make?
I believed you'd come of your own accord to make up for your mistake. Rather than wait for you in Great Springs, I thought I might as well head straight to the Far South.
If you made it, I'd be here waiting. And if someone other than you crossed the storm—if Rhodes Island's people came—I'd be able to look after things for them too.
Then again, pouched musbeasts are a creature I've long wanted to observe. Perhaps the bigger reason I rushed down here was animal-watching, haha.
As she spoke, Martina took from inside her coat the envelope Angelina had chosen so carefully and set it beside the misdelivered decryptor.
My heart was in such disarray then. I meant to write and tell you how troubled I was, and I hoped you might give me an answer. Who could have guessed...
Amy, haven't you still not calibrated your portable comms station?
Th-that's right! With all the pouched musbeast commotion I completely forgot!
But didn't Angie send Miss Martina a letter? What exactly was in that—
Never mind that for now, let's go, let's go.
To get back to the point, Angelina—where would you go to find a person who never makes mistakes?
I was a Messenger for a long time myself, and I misdelivered letters along the way. Such things are unavoidable. Why be so hard on yourself over it?
About the question I asked you in the letter...
"To Rhodes Island, to this land, to Angelina the Messenger... where exactly do I belong?"
Having traveled this far, I think you've already found the answer.
...Really?
A person's place is determined by the things they choose to do.
...The things I choose to do.
There are so many things I want to do. But... the more I try, the more I realize there's a great deal I simply can't manage.
Such as saving the Infected who wouldn't leave that town?
Or standing beside everyone and fighting alongside them the day Rhodes Island was attacked, instead of waiting somewhere safe, sick with worry.
So you went and did things. A great many things.
...Huh?
If you'd done nothing, perhaps you and I would still have met somewhere. But what about the people you met on your journey?
Tani would have stayed an unhappy switchboard operator, Jacinta would have been hauled back to the sanatorium by her bodyguards, Amelia would have given in to her company's pressure in Big Ironton...
You changed their lives, more or less, and they changed yours, more or less. That is what you chose to do.
As for the attack on Rhodes Island, I don't know the details. But the you of back then—would you have been confident of catching Amelia steadily as she fell from the highest point in Big Ironton?
...No, I wouldn't.
Then why do you think that if Rhodes Island faces another crisis, you won't have the chance to stand at their side?
You are already a very, very remarkable Messenger, Angelina.
And Rhodes Island surely already regards you as an indispensable member. Everyone you've helped has kept a place for you in their heart.
Setting you on a Messenger's path that rainy night may well be the most right thing I've done in my whole life.
Thank you, thank you...
I always wanted to thank you in person, but we kept missing each other so many times that I sometimes wondered whether it was fate arranging things...
No—thank you, Angelina.
I always felt you had no need to thank me, and that I should be thanking you. Thank you for showing me that one small kindness can come back so richly repaid.
Mm—by the way, about the other question you mentioned in your letter...
I-I only asked one question, didn't I?
Let me find it... here it is, in the latter half: "There's so much I want to say, and I don't know how to begin... That question has been troubling me all this time."
Ah, um, I really only wrote that part offhand...
Then shall we... skip that one?
No, I would like to hear your view... I want to know what you think.
All I know is that feelings kept hidden too long inside change. They may change for the better or for the worse—they may transform into a butterfly, or they may rot.
I don't know what that feeling has become inside you. What I'd say is, while it still brings you joy, let it out.
If saying it face to face feels awkward, then how about doing it as you did before—by writing a letter?
Writing a letter...
Oh my, what brings you here?
Looking thoroughly apologetic, Tuft's mother pulled from her pouch one item, two, three...
More than a dozen of the things she and the others had taken from the four girls a short while earlier.
All of them were perfectly intact—and even sorted into four little piles by owner.
Oh, thank goodness. If you lot really hadn't returned what you took, I wouldn't have known how to explain it to Angelina and her friends.
Still—just how deep is that pouch of yours, and how much can it hold? Why is it that you alone brought back everything all those pouched musbeasts carried off?
Excuse me, might I ask...
Martina looked at the pouched musbeast's pouch.
...Would you let me see just how deep your pouch goes?
The pouched musbeast clearly understood Martina's meaning and flashed her claws in evident displeasure.
But she soon realized this human had no intention of actually doing it, so she turned, squeaked softly at Angelina a few times, and left the tent.
How do they tell which thing belongs to whom?
By scent.
That's also why the one you call Tuft likes being with you... Your scent, in fact, is very like her mother's.
Mine? Like her mother's?
Her mother once had brief dealings with people... and as a Messenger, at that.
Could she be the pouched musbeast from the legend?
Legends always have reality as their foundation, and they always spur people to make their contents real.
In any case, when I first arrived in the Far South, Tuft's mother showed an uncanny understanding of a Messenger's equipment, and made off with a fair amount of my food quite smoothly.
Haha...
As for the similar scent—every creature that takes on a Messenger's duties carries the same one...
The scent of countless different regions mixed together... the scent of Terra, the scent of this land.
It's a shame I can't manage a pouched musbeast's particular call. If I could, I might really have given Tani a scare when she suspected I was a pouched musbeast grandma.
Pff.
I never knew you were someone who enjoys observing wildlife—and who... likes to joke around.
That's because our time together has been far too short, Angelina.
What is it?
There are a few of my things mixed in with your pile. They really can't tell one Messenger's scent from another's.
...So there are.
All right, all right. Dividing the spoils can wait until it's fully light. Even with that nap in the middle of the night, I'm quite sleepy now.
Why don't you go see your friends?
Right!
Angelina suddenly spotted an unfamiliar object among the odds and ends that carried Tani's scent.
An object she was certain she had never seen, and yet had heard Tani speak of many times.
Angie, are you two done talking?
We are. Martina's going to sleep a bit longer, so I came out first.
The comms equipment is calibrated. There's nothing wrong with Amelia's technology—we can already reach every node along the whole line.
The bandwidth still isn't what we hoped, though. Even text messages will probably come through one at a time...
But before that...
Let's watch the sunrise first.
True—it's already time for it...
It's beautiful...
The early morning was cold, but the girls, oblivious to it, watched the rising sun in the distance.
It was the sun that shines on everything without mercy. The sun looks coldly over all things on the earth, feeding the good and the wicked alike, lighting delivery rooms and muddy battlefields both.
And it was also, in this moment and this moment alone, a sun that belonged only to the four of them.
Dawns that began with disinfectant and ward rounds, harsh morning light laced with sulfur, a square patch of red cloud above a walled estate, a city's noisy, murky rush hour...
For now, they forgot all of it.
Like newborns, they simply watched that orange glow. They watched the light spill like a rising tide, watched golden new life wash ceaselessly over the sea mist.
They watched it stall at a certain moment, as if hesitating, wavering—and then, in the next instant, pulse free of the cold clouds.
They watched it finally climb halfway up the sky and, weary yet generous, pour out its warm orange without reserve, until it covered their cheeks, red with the sea wind.
The sun had risen.
Somewhere farther than the end of the land, the sun had risen.
The sun... has risen.
Amy, take a picture. Take a picture of our sun.
Got it.
And with that, this journey of ours...
This journey really is over. I'm all right.
Even without Grandma's pocket watch, I've reached the Far South and seen the most beautiful sunrise.
It's time to message home, let them know I'm safe, and tell them I did it. I didn't learn a single Art on the way, but I did it anyway.
If they want to keep me in Great Springs now, "no talent for Arts" won't cut it as an excuse, heheh.
Um, I don't know whether the signal tower in Great Springs has been fixed... but you can still send it! Once it's fixed they'll get it!
Here, Tani. The terminal.
Let me think about how to word it...
And... this too. The pouched musbeasts returned it along with the rest of our things.
Huh?
Huh?!
Is this... the pocket watch?!
Trembling, Tani took the watch from Angelina's hand.
The dazzling morning sun gilded the case in gold, so bright she could barely keep her eyes open, and yet she still read on it a name she knew better than any other...
Inara.
She hurriedly wiped her eyes twice.
The naive fantasies about what the watch would let her do had long since been set aside. Now she wept purely from joy at having found the keepsake her grandmother had lost.
Grandma... Honestly, dropping something this important in the Far South, and letting a pouched musbeast pick it up...
Just like me... all clumsy...
I said I didn't need it anymore, and it shows up at a time like this...
Tani barely held back her tears and wiped at the patches of rust on the watch's case.
Even with the watch in her hands, she had no idea how to use it—but she no longer cared. She only wanted to open it and see the marks time had left inside...
Yet what appeared before the dial was a photograph in the lid.
A photograph of Tani.
"Grandma accidentally lost her pocket watch."
"Hmm... where did I drop it? Maybe Big Ironton, maybe Solar Valley, maybe the Far South..."
"Clever little Thumpy. If Grandma was still using the watch along the way, then she didn't lose it on the road... No, no, there's the return trip too."
"So then—where on earth did she lose it...?"
Tani was suddenly certain: it was right here, in the hour when the sun was just rising, that Grandma had deliberately left the watch behind.
She believed she understood how Grandma had felt. She had seen scenery beautiful enough to stop the breath, made friends she'd never forget, broken through obstacles nobody before her had passed...
But when the sun rose, Grandma was alone.
All those experiences leapt in her chest with nowhere to go, no one to tell. Before her there were only the pouched musbeasts, flown over out of curiosity—
—And so she decided: let it stop here.
She would give the pocket watch, the symbol of countless journeys, to the pouched musbeasts who kept her company in that moment, thanking them for keeping her from being too alone.
Then she would stop beneath this surging sunlight and make this magnificent sunrise the end of her career as a pathfinder. And then she would go back to Tani...
Back to the people she loved, and the people who loved her.
Grandma wasn't just clumsy, she was a dishonest rascal too. She was too embarrassed, so in the end she lied to my face...
She left the watch in the Far South on purpose, she wanted her family with her, and still she insisted she'd lost it...
I can't cry. I can't cry here!
Tani fought her tears back with everything she had, tucked the watch carefully against her chest, and set the terminal in front of her again.
I have to tell my family. Tell them I found Grandma's pocket watch, tell them Grandma really did reach the Far South...
I have so much to tell them. About Grandma, about me, about what I'll do next...
I—
M-messages... So many messages?!
From Uncle Tucker: The Ironfeet won, 180 for 5 to 165 for 8. A cricket match without little Thumpy keeping the beat just isn't the same.
From Dad: Ignore your Uncle Tucker, call that one a test message. How is it? Are you enjoying the trip? Do you need anything? ...We probably can't catch up to you, but I'm asking anyway!
From Dad: We're in Artichoke Village right now! I asked around and heard the long-range comms here were fixed, so we came to message you! I hear you had a hand in that. Amazing!
From Mom: Is the journey going well? Your father wouldn't let go of the terminal—I finally wrestled it away. Does the food out there agree with you?
From Mom: If your stomach acts up, try burning carrot leaves to ash and stirring it into water. It's good for the digestion.
From Mom: Buy your shoes a size larger, remember. Your grandmother taught me that. With larger shoes you can add insoles, but there's nothing to be done about small ones.
From Mom: I've gone on about all sorts of things, but about what happened on your birthday... we all owe you an apology. You're an adult, and you should do what you want to do.

From Dad: Enough of that. Remember to take some pictures for us! Since you're going to the Far South, I hear the scenery there is beautiful. Take a few for your dad—I want to hang them on the wall at home!
From Mom: Don't listen to your father. Take lots of pictures of yourself, and make them pretty!
The tears she'd held back for so long finally broke through.
Messages kept appearing on the terminal one after another, but Tani was already crying too hard to catch her breath.
In the early morning light, the girls held each other and wept.

eps.name: Be Well, Me at the End of the Road

lines.st: Dear Doctor,
I honestly... hadn't planned on writing you a letter.
I'm a Messenger of Rhodes Island. No matter how long I drift out here, I always come back in the end. So why write to you at all?
And yet, the moment I started the trip home—setting out from Rim Billiton's Far South back toward Ultimate Big Ironton—I started writing this letter.
I'll cover the outbound trip in every detail in the mission report, so don't worry about not following along...
...Though now that I think about it, won't the return trip be in the mission report too?
Even so, I'm writing this letter. Because this journey—outbound and return both—was far too enjoyable. So enjoyable it left me with a regret...
...the regret that you weren't with us.

lines.x: How long have Mr. and Mrs. Campbell been in the dressing room?
What's the rush? It's only another meeting with trade representatives from the centrum nations.
That meeting can't even start without the Campbells. If they want to drag it out, let them. It might be a negotiating tactic.
But I hear those trade representatives have already started forming a private alliance among themselves. The situation may not be as rosy as we think...

lines.n: Male Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: ...Let me go pick out a tie, would you...

lines.n: Male Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: This animal-print one is really...
See? He's still picking out a tie. There's no rush at all.
Animal print? Mr. Campbell has never worn an animal-print tie. Could it be some kind of signal... Has something changed?

lines.n: Female Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: ...She wanted to see you wear that tie back then, and you brushed her off with that exact line...
"She"?
"Back then"?
Both the optimistic driver and the pessimistic bodyguard fell silent. Neither moved from his spot, but both pricked up their ears, straining to catch every sound from the dressing room.

lines.n: Male Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: ...But at least leave me some dignity in front of others...

lines.n: Female Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: ...If you don't explain this properly, don't blame me for leaving you no dignity at all!

lines.n: Male Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: I'll apologize, I really will apologize, but this animal tie still—

lines.n: Male Voice in the Dressing Room
lines.x: All right, all right...
Sir, madam! If you're ready, we'll head to the Big Ironton Convention Center—
The Big Ironton Convention Center?
Isn't—isn't that right?
Madam, forgive my bluntness, but even if one of the trade representatives this time is, ah, someone with whom Mr. Campbell has history, it wouldn't do to let private matters interfere with business—
What? We're going to see Jacinta and her friends. What on earth are you two talking about?
Miss Jacinta? Then that tie...
Before he first sent Jacinta to the sanatorium, she wanted to see him wear that tie—and he brushed her off with "it isn't dignified enough."
I'm sure you've heard what Jacinta got up to in Big Ironton recently. Liam Campbell is going to welcome his daughter home—and apologize while he's at it.
So that's what this is about...
Now, gentlemen, it's your turn to explain to me what all that about "someone with history" and "letting private matters interfere with business" was supposed to mean.
Daddy, Daddy, isn't there something new on that shelf?
Sharp eyes as always. That's the photo from this year's cricket tournament. Shall I take it down for you to see?
Yes!
In the photo there are... four big sisters dressed up nicely?
Daddy, why aren't they wearing work clothes?
Because they aren't Solar Valley miners to begin with. They came to help fix the comms tower and joined the cricket tournament while they were at it.
Did they fix the comms tower?
They did. Not only that, they rescued someone from down the mine shaft.
Those big sisters are amazing! So what place did they get in the tournament? Did they win?
Heh heh... Fixing towers and rescuing people aside, beating your dad on the cricket pitch? They've got a long way to go!
This is this year's championship trophy—your dad won it! How about it, isn't it fine? Want it?
Daddy's mean! Daddy didn't let the big sisters win!
No, it's a competition—
I want this photo!
Hold on, little tyrant, don't damage it. Let me go ask who has the film and when we can get another print made...
Tani and the others just came by. They want everyone to get together—everyone who was in the cricket tournament has gone, and you're the only one missing.
What luck! Come on, come on, Dad will take you to get a photo with those big sisters!
Speaking of which, the others were asking whether the liaison is coming.
Him? He probably can't make it. After the comms tower was fixed he went out to do business and actually got into a middling sort of car accident, so he's back at headquarters convalescing.
Is Mr. Barton in? I'm almost fully recovered—could I end my convalescence—
Oh, Mr. Liaison!
Ah, you're better. Come on, join us!
J-join you where?!
Everyone who was in the cricket tournament has gone, so Mr. Liaison should go too!
The cricket tournament?!
Owwwwwww...
I've been drinking for days now, and every time I have your carrot wine I think the same thing: the carrots here really are good.
Aren't they just? High sugar, they keep well, lovely flavor... Using them for dried carrots is a waste!
That's because the village doesn't have that many people who can drink!
I've been meaning to ask, actually—is Great Springs short on carrot wine? If we could trade what each of us lacks—
Carrot wine this good? Where in Rim Billiton wouldn't be short of it?
Excellent! Wonderful! Drink up!
Drink up!
Drink—
Stop!
Madison, we're halfway through a business deal. It'll be done in a moment, just a little longer—
Business? The three girls who came with Tani have already closed the deal.
Even at that they're a step ahead of me?!
